section_ownership.note: Card D02-GEN-REST. Every top-level key of this file is labelled here, so no section is silently hand-maintained. `derived` sections are recomputed by the generator on every run and a hand edit to them is overwritten; `hand_maintained` sections are carried verbatim from the previous matrix, which is why a regeneration no longer reverts a later reconciliation; `integrator_supplied` numbers are measurements the generator cannot take.

header.purpose: A traceable requirement -> implemented profile -> source/model entry point -> executed test stage -> proof/evidence -> remaining-boundary matrix for revision 0.3 as implemented at this checkpoint.
header.counts_are_run_metadata: Every count in this file is run metadata about executed gates, manifests and archived measurements. A count is NOT proof of specification coverage: passing test totals, CT mapping counts, contract module counts and audit unit totals say what was executed, not what was proved. Projection coverage is not safety coverage and unknowns stay in the denominator.
header.verdict_vocabulary: Safe only after all obligations discharge; Unsafe only for a validated reachable violation; everything else Unknown. A provisional Unsafe is never presented as an upstream defect. Raw Cycle 19 units remain unpromoted.
header.independence_rule: The four evidence classes are marked INDEPENDENTLY per requirement. Support in one class is never inferred from another: a proved Lean theorem is not source evidence, an executed native run is not a model proof, and a model regression is not an observation.

evidence_classes.source: evidence taken on real source - QCore source programs through the frontend/driver, or C translation units through the gateway importers
evidence_classes.model: evidence taken in the dependency-free Rust kernel or the trusted verification adapter, over supplied traces, programs or certificates
evidence_classes.observation: evidence from an executed run - native/C11 execution, a CLI probe, a configured audit or a process provider
evidence_classes.mechanized: Lean 4 definitions and theorems registered in an Audit*.lean file and checked by scripts/check_lean_audits.py

support_status_vocabulary.executed: a named gate in the standing per-change gate runs this evidence class at HEAD
support_status_vocabulary.recorded_not_gated: the evidence exists as an archived probe log or transcript; nothing in the standing gate re-runs it
support_status_vocabulary.declared_premise: this class is an explicitly named assumption carried on the certificate/report, not established here
support_status_vocabulary.absent: no evidence of this class exists for this requirement
support_status_vocabulary.not_applicable: this class cannot apply to the requirement as stated

requirements.remaining_boundary: Observation scope/module/bounds substitution rejects; native provenance is declared trusted evidence and whole-program/source-model refinement remains open. Identity is provenance, not attestation: the compiler executable, its environment and the filesystem are trusted. Individual headers are not enumerated - the dependency closure is bound by effect through preprocessed_source_sha256 under -E -P, so a header edit that leaves the token stream unchanged does not change the identity. The declared driver is recorded, never checked for equivalence. The pinned Cycle19 compatibility adapter keeps CSourceInput::HistoricalStdin and its silent choice among 28 units with two or four compile configurations (G01 SS5); its four archived artifacts were not re-measured. Syntax and typed-AST phases still read preprocessed text from standard input, which is why __builtin_FILE/__builtin_FILE_NAME reject rather than being answered. P01-F2 is open: qcorec plugins verify/enable accept schema-valid, digest-intact edits to non-digest manifest declarations. P02 is not an OS sandbox: no namespace, cgroup, seccomp or capability-drop mechanism; no filesystem or network confinement (P03); RLIMIT_NPROC is per-UID and must not be presented as a per-execution child quota; non-Linux refuses rather than partially enforcing; the enforced profile is never selected by default.

ScopedReadSharesV1: one owned Buffer lent to two children with complementary halves of the 1024-unit read authority, both reading it while the parent also reads it, and Buffer writes on either side of the lending window because a write demands reconstructed exclusive authority. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, all-paths task-IR check, reference execution, C11 emission, and three fixed Linux schedules whose emitted C runs under ASan/UBSan/LSan with a heap witness recording every Buffer by address - one object allocated and released exactly once across two live borrowers, a refused second creation returning only its own share, and a refused join returning none and reclaiming nothing. The complementary refusals are mapped as CT04 and CT05. This is not evidence about arbitrary schedules, other targets or the C memory model; ThreadSanitizer does not intercept C11 thrd_create, so data-race freedom rests on the checker's no-write-while-shared rule. The lending budget is over authority handed out, not a separation-logic fraction; disjoint slicing, write shares, more than two readers, byte accounting and nested workers stay refused.

ScopedReadSharesV1: the parent writes its Buffer while both children still hold their halves. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying LoanOutstanding { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, borrowers: [2, 3] }, which names the outstanding total and every borrower rather than the bare fact of a loan. An accepted Linux control moves the same write after both joins, so the refusal is keyed to the outstanding shares and not to writing at all. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

ScopedReadSharesV1: two children each request the whole read authority for one allocation. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying ShareExceedsAuthority { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, requested: 1024 }; the excess request is refused as a whole and the outstanding total is unchanged. An accepted Linux control lends 511 and 513 of the same allocation, so the budget boundary is a boundary rather than a blanket refusal of two borrowers. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

StandardStringV1: an immutable UTF-8 {ptr, len} view of an owned std.buffer's own bytes, copied into a second name by a whole-extent slice ({ptr = p + 0, len = 2 - 0}), inside one flat sequential entry. ScopedWriteLeasesV1 with card WRITE-LEND-TASKS' range write lease and card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE's worker-body byte write, remapped by card CT07-TWO-THREAD-REMAP (wave 37) from the sequential write lend card CT07-WRITE-REMAP (wave 30) mapped, which had itself remapped the read-loan program the wave-28 lane mapped: two WRITE authorities over disjoint ranges of one allocation's int32_t payload - lend buffer 0..2 and lend buffer 2..4 - held by TWO THREADS, each worker writing a byte through its own lease in its own body, the owner reading both bytes back only after both joins, which is when the leases return. Each worker writes its own RELATIVE byte 0 and the events name owner bytes 0 and 2, so the rebasing law is visible in the observation rather than asserted about it. Disjointness is decided at check time by ownership::axes_overlap, called by LeaseRange::overlaps in the scoped-task ledger, and the exclusivity is the ledger's rather than a route rule's: a second overlapping lease refuses at the spawn site before anything is emitted. WHAT MOVED, and it is the scenario's own word: wave 30's two write authorities were bindings of ONE SEQUENTIAL ENTRY - 'NOT two threads', as that card's own semantic profile said, naming WRITE-LEND-TASKS as the residual; that residual's successor landed in wave 31 and was made exercisable in wave 36, so 'independently' now means two threads writing distinct bytes of one object under ASan/UBSan/LSan with the native observation compared line for line against the reference execution of the checked task IR, and the single allocation checked by address. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: no count - CT07 was mapped before this card and is mapped after it, so this is evidence quality and not coverage (constraint 23). Boundaries, stated rather than left silent: the payload is one int32_t, so the two halves are two bytes each (BUFFER_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 4; residual WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXTENT); there is NO ThreadSanitizer evidence, because TSan cannot run any program this route emits, lease or not (residual TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-SEGV, measured on three programs in wave 36), so 'two threads write distinct memory locations without a race' is carried by C11 3.14 plus the sanitizer and allocation-identity evidence and NOT by a race detector; and proof stays unassessed, since wave 31's and wave 36's Lean theorems are about the model's authorities and writes and are not bound to this artifact by a named test (residual CT07-TWO-THREAD-PROOF-LEG). Bounds are split across the two layers that own them: past_range_byte.qcore refuses a real payload byte at the LEASE it goes through, and past_extent_read.qcore refuses a real owner access at the PAYLOAD's extent. Disjointness is overlapping_leases.qcore's OverlappingLeases refusal naming both ranges. Wave 30's sequential program is retained as the sequential_write_halves accept control and wave 28's read-loan program as the read_loan accept control, with wave 30's three sequential reject twins retained as rejection controls, so this remap is a strict superset of the evidence wave 30 published rather than a swap. TSAN CITATION (card TSAN-ROWS-2, wave 39; a citation, not a stage flip - no stage of this row moves): compiler/tests/task_route_tsan.rs reads THIS fixture through the real pipeline (compile_files, entry null) and runs its own emitted C under ThreadSanitizer through the pthread binding of tests/support/thread_sanitizer.rs, changing no emitted byte - unbound it dies at the 0x18 fault every task program dies at (every_subject_dies_unbound_at_the_one_fault); bound it runs clean under the unforced schedule (every_subject_runs_clean_under_thread_sanitizer_when_bound) and under two FORCED schedules (every_subject_runs_clean_under_each_forced_schedule): both workers created and released before either body runs and both threads live until both bodies have run, and last-created first with each body to completion - zero races, stdout byte-identical to the reference execution, the realised schedule read back from the harness's own trace. The overlap mutation on this fixture is reported under all three schedules (overlapping_writers_are_reported_under_every_schedule), 20 of 20 runs each (docs/reports/tsan-rows-2/artifacts/catch-rates.json). So the sentence above that reads 'there is NO ThreadSanitizer evidence' describes wave 37's state and is superseded by this citation; 'two threads write distinct memory locations without a race' is now ALSO carried by a race detector, over the schedules named, with TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-PTHREAD-BINDING's and TSAN-FORCED-BODY-OVERLAP-NOT-FORCED's boundaries. ADMITTED, with the composed premises stated: the pack is DUTY-FREE (the composed body admits no acquisition - REGION-JOINS-DUTIES refuses one at Q302 - so the one thing the opening can discard is the parent-local remainder), and ALL JOINS PRECEDE THE REGION (every TrySpawn/Join span of the checked task IR precedes the region statement, refused at Q600 in both directions when false, so no child exists and no child holds any grant at the opening). The published abandoned_credit is re-derived by the driver from an independent fold of the written statements before publication, and the harness compares the whole published split - granted/restored/spent under the four unchanged FlatEpochBoundV1 premises, plus the abandoned figure - wholesale. The region erases from emission and the epoch charges no axis for the parent-local strict credit (REGION-JOINS-EPOCH-AXIS); no native or sanitizer evidence is claimed, and the region's credit quantities are written statements, not measurements of any execution.

ComposedEpochTasksV1 (source.epoch.tasks.v1, card CT24-CLEANUP-TASK-COMPOSITION): a flat-epoch plan over a checked scoped-task region whose parent owns `owner`, lends its worker a counted read share at the spawn, and then directly in the exact Result::Ok arm executes a handled region that adopts the same owner. The discharge erases to a real `drop owner;` at the region's own source position, before the later join; the unedited task ledger refuses that release at Q600 LoanOutstanding. Accepted controls do not confer stage credit: the same cleanup after join admits and publishes released=[owner], abandoned=3, and cleanup of an independent owner before join does the same, proving the case is neither a blanket placement refusal nor an unsupported-region fallback. Refused controls pin missing join [Q600], arbitrary nested if/loop and spawn-error-arm placement [Q302], double cleanup-pack use [Q304], and unsupported region-body syntax [Q302]. Direct task-scope regions retain the prior after-every-creation-and-join gate; only this exact success-arm statement receives the conditional placement. ComposedEpochTasksV1 (source.epoch.tasks.v1, cards T08-COMPOSE, REGION-JOINS-DUTIES and REGION-JOINS-LOAN): a flat-epoch plan over a real checked scoped-task region whose parent owns `owner`, lends the worker a counted read share of it at the spawn (`read owner share FULL`, declared in the plan as the place-free `read;` clause), joins, and only then writes an error region that ADOPTS the owner (`move owner;`), credits 5, spends 2 and takes its decided error edge; the catch's `quant open R as pack` binds the sealed pack as a linear capability and `discharge pack;` destroys the adopted owner and abandons exactly the parent-local remainder 3 -- the unedited qcore_core::error_region model's own Destroy and AbandonCredit on the discharge. That is CT25's scenario, `cleanup destroys owner after joins and loan expiry`, expected Accept, and the case is ADMITTED with every word a checked fact, each carried by a named rule: CLEANUP DESTROYS OWNER by the model's Destroy on the discharge of the opened pack, made a real emitted, custody-checked and reference-executed destruction by the erasure (the discharge's `drop owner;` is written into the region's blanks after every join, where the unedited task route checks it; the published `released = [owner]` is read out of the model's own cleanup trace and cross-checked against the reader's independent duty fold before publication); AFTER JOINS by the wave-28 span rule (every TrySpawn/Join span of the checked task IR precedes the region statement, refused at Q600 in both directions when false) re-asserted on the published ledger; AND LOAN EXPIRY by three facts of unedited models -- the owner IS lent (the derived capture list is [[read]], from the checked IR's ScalarOperand::Loan, reconciled against the declared `read;` clause), the share RETURNS AT THE JOIN (the task ledger's own reclamation), and the destruction is ORDERED AFTER the expiry because the joins precede the region -- while the pre-expiry destruction is a measured refusal (the ledger's own LoanOutstanding, live_share_drop.qcore) and so is the pre-loan one (the erased drop before the spawn leaves no owned buffer to lend, before_join.qcore). The runner compares the whole published evidence wholesale -- the credit-recovery split under the four unchanged FlatEpochBoundV1 premises, the abandoned figure, the released duty list and both capture lists -- and re-asserts the adopting-pack premise (exactly one published body Acquire per released owner) and the span premise on the published objects. BOUNDARIES: both write authorities and the loan live in one entry's task scope -- the lender on this route is always the creator (REGION-JOINS-LOAN's discharge of T08-COMPOSE-LOAN) and creator-scope bytes are outside the epoch allocation (REGION-JOINS-EPOCH-AXIS, re-measured by that card: certificates byte-identical with and without the loan and the adoption). The region erases from emission (measured byte-for-byte against a hand-written twin by compiler/tests/region_joins_loan.rs, not re-measured here); the region's credit quantities are written statements, not measurements of any execution; and no native, sanitizer or proof evidence is claimed -- the capability card's native counting-allocator run carries no sanitizer, so none is readable from it (constraint 23), and the emission/native stages read unassessed (CT-COMPOSED-NATIVE).

named_followups.title: RLIMIT_NPROC conformance test is load-dependent
named_followups.why: a_declared_process_limit_stops_the_fixture_from_forking installs RLIMIT_NPROC=1, which counts every process of the real UID, so under load the host observes Io(Broken pipe) instead of Terminated. Two independent runs reproduced it; it passes in isolation and passed both merged full-gate runs. The assertion is deliberately not weakened. Wave-7 note: P03-F added a deterministic companion under the cgroup pids quota; the original assertion is byte-for-byte unchanged. Wave-17 note: GEN-CTREASONS measured a second load-sensitive row, `vp04_vp07_vp08_process_lifecycle_and_payload_budgets` (compiler/tests/cycle20_verifier_plugins.rs) — fails at load average 50, passes at load average 37 on the same binary — and EXTERN-MODES measured the confined-process fixture failing with Io(Broken pipe) under load and passing in isolation. Neither assertion is weakened; three rows are now recorded load-flakes to verify in isolation. Wave-26 note: two of the five recorded rows tripped across two cards' full-gate runs — the confined-fixture write test (EXAMPLES-SUITE-WIRE's first run) and the RLIMIT_NPROC row itself (its second, and CT-WIRE-LANE's) — each failing with character-for-character the same `Io(Broken pipe)` assertion, each verified in isolation at 12 passed / 0 failed on the same binary and the same tree, and each row passing on the run where its neighbour failed. No assertion was weakened and no test was re-run in isolation to obtain a pass. The same runs exposed a GATE defect rather than a test defect: `cargo test --workspace` is fail-fast, so one of these rows silently hid every target after it in crate order — a whole crate, `crates/qcorec/tests/examples_cli.rs` included — making the number that run printed a lower bound rather than a measurement. The integrator ADOPTED the fix at the wave-26 close: AGENTS.md's standing per-change gate now documents `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (follow-on GATE-NO-FAIL-FAST), a deliberate STRENGTHENING, so a recorded flake can no longer shrink the suite it is reported against. AMENDED (EXECUTION-QUOTA-LOAD-INDEPENDENCE, 2026-10-12): the Io(Broken pipe) shape of the confined-fixture write row and of memory_growth_beyond_the_declared_limit_is_bounded is a fixture that never read its request racing the host's first write; every verifier-host fixture now reads its whole request first (tests/support/process_fixture.rs) and is written by a separate process, which also closes the ETXTBSY shape. Measured before and after under a host-stall load in docs/reports/execution-quota-load-independence/README.md; constraint 16 records the figures. The vp04_vp07_vp08 and standalone_host wall-clock rows are untouched by the card. AMENDED (PROCESS-FIXTURES-FS-WRITE-OUTSIDE-HOST-CRATE, 2026-10-14): the out-of-process fixture writer is now tests/support/process_fixture.rs at the repository root, and every executable a test or example writes or copies and then runs goes through it (census: 16 files, the six of the ledger entry and ten more). real_packages_preserve_unknown_and_reject_mutations's own executable rewrites (providers/conformance/tests/packages.rs) are among them, which closes the inherited-descriptor shape of ETXTBSY for that row; the row stays listed because its recorded ExecutableFileBusy was not reproduced by the card.

named_followups.title: source.extern-call.v1 follow-ons
named_followups.why: resource_out(nullable) and resource_stored landed in wave 10 (EXTERN-F1), with resource_owned admitted only in the stored owner position per §C04.2; the nonnull out form is refused by design. Measured: resource_stored is admitted and checked but unreachable from a single source module — the v1 adapter error arm may abandon nothing, so a second live acquisition refuses at Q025 (EXTERN-F1-STORE-REACH, filed against the error-arm-release follow-on, the gate deliberately not weakened). Still open: removed/reallocated/released modes, sentinel/errno adapters (O03 interaction), extents, variadics, concurrent/error-region contexts, cost summaries, linkage verification, the inline Q020/Q021 consumer. EXTERN-ERR-REL landed in wave 12: the else arm renders the cleanup edge (same identities, once, reverse order), STORE-REACH closed at four levels, AdapterDepartingArgument named; 'carried into the error path' measured unimplementable on this route (EXTERN-ERR-REL-PAYLOAD). EXTERN-MODES landed in wave 17: `resource_released(p, nonnull)` and `resource_return_reallocated(p, nullable)` over an `Owned` subject become callable, each at a measured boundary — the release is the delta the error arm was already describing (§C04.2 separates discharging an obligation from transferring it), and the reallocation is the one departing argument an acquiring call may carry because §C04.3 states its failure arm, so the subject stays live on the error arm and must be dispositioned there under the unweakened abandonment rule. `BridgeRefusal::ReleasedParameter` and `::ReallocatedReturn` are retired by name, as are two Lean theorems, each keeping its load-bearing half. Three modes stay refused on measured grounds, not deferred: `resource_released(p, nullable)` (NullableReleasedParameter), `resource_return_reallocated(p, nonnull)` (NonnullReallocatedReturn) and `resource_removed` (RemovedParameter — a removal names a child the profile stopped tracking when it was stored, and EXTERN-F1 premised that residual rather than modelling an index, so admitting it would mint a caller identity out of a premise). No diagnostic code and no reserved word were added; `move NAME` spells all four departing modes and the declaration decides which ran. Three new fixed ASan/UBSan/LSan fixtures link a real C `free` and a real `realloc`. New: EXTERN-MODES-REMOVED-INDEX (needs a modeled owner-to-child index, a change to what `resource_stored` publishes), EXTERN-MODES-NULLABLE-RELEASE (needs a checked no-null-actual statement at a custody position) and EXTERN-MODES-SENTINEL (the sentinel/errno adapter needs §C04.4 vocabulary for the success test and must take its errno classification from `qcore_core::os_endpoint`, the O03-REACTOR precedent). Extents, variadics, function pointers, callbacks, structs, concurrent and error-region contexts, cost summaries, linkage verification and the inline Q020/Q021 consumer are carried unchanged. W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING addressed the sentinel half where it applies to the resource loader: the scalar failure sentinel `-1` of a descriptor is representable (`sentinel`/`valid` validity on the `descriptor` kind, C04.6), with guard narrowing in the C gateway; the checked extern-call route (`qcore-contract::extern_bridge`) has one custody kind and refuses every kinded declaration by name, and errno classification is untouched, so EXTERN-MODES-SENTINEL stays open for the extern-call model. AMENDED by CG22-INDIRECT-CALLS-AND-CALLBACKS (gateway rule 11p, main b6a3dc42): the C gateway's function-pointer part is generalised there (a call through a function pointer is resolved only to a candidate set the unit's Clang AST closes and rewritten to the calls C may make; an open set keeps its refusal), and an inline function-pointer parameter declarator is now read as `fnptr`. The extern-call route (qcore-contract::extern_bridge) is unchanged: function pointers and callbacks there stay carried.

QUIRIN-SOCKET-V1 provides std.socket and source.socket.v1 behind it - the module registry's NINTH entry - a checked TCP AND UDP surface over loopback (let S = tcp / udp, bind, listen, connect, accept, send, recv, sendto, recvfrom, close) whose defining decision is that EVERY PEER OF EVERY SOCKET in an admitted program is another socket of the same program, in one thread. That is not a testing convenience grafted onto a general surface: it is what makes the route's two determinism obligations DECIDABLE. The model carries each connected stream's committed bytes and each bound socket's datagram queue, so a receive the program's own history does not satisfy is REFUSED at Q085 rather than deadlocked on at run time - and so are an accept with nothing queued, a second unaccepted connection on a depth-one queue, a send beyond the in-flight bound, a STREAM close with unread bytes (it resets the connection, which the peer observes at a moment this program does not decide) and a listener close with a queued connection, while a DATAGRAM close with queued datagrams is ADMITTED on stated grounds because the queue is discarded locally and nothing observable changes. What a receive yields is published in SocketCertificate::receipts and COMPARED BY THE EMITTED PROGRAM, which exits 88 on disagreement, so the named premise SOCKET-V1-STREAM-BYTE-ORDER produces a FAILED RUN if it is false and never a wrong verdict. Blocking is argued in three parts of which only the third is a premise: a receive cannot block (a theorem about the model), a connect and an accept cannot block (structural - connect targets a listening socket of this same program whose queue the model knows is empty), and a send cannot block is SOCKET-V1-LOOPBACK-BUFFERED-SEND, made quantitative (MAX_PAYLOAD 1024, MAX_INFLIGHT 4096, both inside the smallest default socket buffer of all three targets) and converted into a BOUNDED FAILURE - every wait polls with a finite 5000 ms timeout and a distinct status - because a program that blocked forever would produce no evidence at all. Custody is the UNEDITED qcore_core::ownership checker's, reached exactly as source.buffer.v1 reaches it; the close discipline is read out of os_endpoint::close_poststate rather than invented, and it answered the poisoned Attempted with no permitted recovery where the card expected Indeterminate, which is why a failed close exits 89 rather than retrying. Every bind is to port 0 and no port is spellable in source, reaches a certificate field or reaches an observation record, so parallel runs cannot collide; a UDP receipt carries `from` and the emitted program compares the reported source address field for field, so a stray datagram fails the run rather than being read as this one. named_followups.title: |> landed; || and && lowered onto branching in wave 19; singles reserved for bitwise
named_followups.why: Wave 18 landed the pipe operator |> as a pure token-stream desugaring (first-argument insertion, left-associative; byte-identical emitted C vs the hand-written twin; linearity through pipelines inherited from the existing checkers; a pre-existing divergent re-tokenization path in source_extern found and repaired). The measured surface bounds the rest: QCore has NO if statement (Q500; zero ifs across 294 source files) and no boolean expression tier, so the logical operators landed as claimed tokens with actionable refusals under the scope guards — single | is logical or and && is logical and BY DECISION, both refusing at Q038 until a lowering exists; || redirects to |, a lone & in logical position redirects to &&, bare & stays reserved for a future binary/bitwise operation, [| and |] are byte-unchanged, and bitwise OR having no symbol left is flagged open, not answered. The Pipe pass owns Q036-Q038 after an integration-time band relocation (UncheckedLinkage shipped Q032-Q035 first; the T07/T09 precedent). Residuals in dependency order: a source if/branching construct is the prerequisite for OR-LOWERING and AND-LOWERING; PIPE-CHAIN (multi-stage pipelines need expression-valued statements), PIPE-LET, PIPE-STMT-STAGES. Wave 19 landed the whole residual chain. IF-STATEMENT landed the branching prerequisite source.branch.v1 (if/else/else if, a decidable condition tier, custody-join agreement; band Q044-Q046; sequential route only with every other route's refusal pinned; ZERO new reserved words) and corrected wave 18's premise: five of six semantic models already branched internally — only cleanup_lowering lacked a branch constructor, so both arms flow through the existing checkers unedited and the conditional leak refuses through the pre-existing join net check. Then OR-AND-LOWERING SUPERSEDED the operator table by user direction: logical or is `||` (one token) and logical and `&&`, both short-circuit, admitted in the condition tier and lowered onto the branch construct with byte-identical emitted C against hand-lowered nested branches (associative on the nose for homogeneous chains, proved); single `|` and `&` refuse at Q038 with the bitwise reservation stated and `^` lexes as a reserved xor token — the open bitwise-OR-symbol note is RESOLVED (`|` is bitwise or, reserved). `&&` binds tighter than `||`, both left-associative, parentheses group; `|>` in a condition is refused, not ranked. No new code: Q045's tier widened and Q038's condition restated through §L21; Q043 went to ComposedStdIo. Five pins moved deliberately, no program's verdict changed; [| |] |> byte-unchanged. New: BITWISE-OPERATORS (needs an integer expression tier; inherits the longest-match constraint), IF-CONNECTIVE-NEGATION; from IF-STATEMENT: IF-RUNTIME-CONDITION, IF-ARM-ACQUIRE and -ATTRIBUTION (an acquiring arm refused by the pre-existing ownership join at Q103, measured and kept), IF-ARM-RETURN, IF-ARM-CALL, IF-ROUTE-WIDENING, IF-CONDITION-BINDINGS, SEQ-STATEMENT-TOKENS (the sequential driver still re-lexes source bytes; inert for conditions, recorded not repaired). After the card there is ONE: c_program::ENTRY_SIGNATURE is the only int main( spelling in the crate and c_program::assemble the only code that writes it, backends contribute keyed Fragments in declared sections (Banner < Config < Compat < Includes < Declarations < Prelude < FileScope) plus one Entry, and THE SINGLE-ENTRY GUARANTEE IS A TYPE RATHER THAN A CHECK because assemble takes exactly one Entry by reference. named_followups.title: The first source-level aggregate type landed; fourteen residuals, each naming its missing capability
named_followups.why: AGGREGATES-V1 is wave 27's language head. source.record.v1 lands `type NAME { FIELD: i32, ... }`, `let p = NAME { FIELD: OPERAND, ... };` and `let a = p.FIELD;` on source.buffer.v1, with every OTHER route's refusal measured and pinned rather than widened, and route selection changing in exactly one condition - a record type DECLARATION - which no program written before the card can satisfy, because `type NAME {` did not parse at all. THE CARD'S DESIGN DECISION IS FIELD CUSTODY AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: a v1 record is a plain copyable value whose fields are all i32, so it contributes NO qcore_core::ownership operation, opens no obligation and derives no effect - because the cycle-3 ownership IR addresses an owner by a plain NAME and has no notion of a path, so `p.buf` is not a question check_ownership can be asked. The consequences are the EXISTING route's rules rather than new ones: `drop p;` refuses at Q052 with 'is not a buffer this entry acquired', and a leak beside a record still refuses at Q054 with the inherited checker's own message. ZERO reserved words, and the constraint-14 census is why: the obvious spelling `record` was REJECTED ON EVIDENCE, because docs/reports/remaining-v07/probes/d02_boundary_record.qr is the single line `record R { }` and TWO ARCHIVED REPORTS PIN IT TO Q000, so claiming the word would have falsified a frozen archive (constraint 21) - the syntax was renamed rather than the pinned surface edited, character for character the buffer -> bytes and work -> effort shape. `struct` is census-clean and was still not taken, on the ground that the language already has a declaration head for a named type. ZERO new diagnostic codes: Q051, Q052 and Q053's conditions are widened and stated in SS L21 under the Q-NAMESPACE-DECISION ice box, which the wave's language head therefore respected rather than being excused from. NO LINE OF NAME RESOLUTION CHANGED EITHER, and that too was a measurement: a field name sits before a `:` at a construction and after a `.` at a read, and frontend::lexical_references has drained both positions since long before the card, so a construction of an undeclared type refuses at Q013 as an ordinary unknown reference. The `.` adjacency is PINNED rather than assumed - `p.x` is Word Dot Word and cannot collapse into a float, so SOCKET-INET-ADDRESSES' Float Dot Float reading of 127.0.0.1 is untouched, and a NUMERIC field path is one float token and refuses by name. The census also ran in the other direction and found the six whole-token-stream route-selector words, whose collision is fail-closed in both halves (Q015 declared, Q000 constructed) - NATIVE-LIBRARY-SOURCE-BINDING's span exclusion was measured and DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED, because it would retire the Q015 half and leave a type that declares and cannot be constructed. Records emit real C structs with one distinctly named member per field behind load-bearing prefixes, and the payoff is CT09's own scenario EXECUTED - three declared fields, three different values, three reads, byte-compared against a sanitized ASan/UBSan/LSan run, so a lowering that gave two fields one member would print one value twice. One emission change lands outside the aggregate and is byte-neutral by an argument about which programs the emitter can reach (a buffer-free program now carries no buffer prelude, forced by -Wall -Wextra -Werror on an unused static); byte identity is MEASURED rather than asserted, the base commit's compiler rebuilt in a scratch tree and all 80 emitting programs compared byte-identical. 56 tests, 28 audited Lean entries in one new audit file, no new axiom. Corpus-neutral by construction. Standing constraint 15k records the decision. New, each naming its missing capability: AGGREGATE-OWNED-FIELD (a field that owns a resource - needs a field-path owner vocabulary, a partial-move rule, a drop-through-aggregate rule and a leak rule at normal exit that sees into the aggregate, none of which exists), AGGREGATE-VIEW-FIELD (a string field - smaller, but needs source.string.v1's exact borrow window, constraint 15h, to reach through an aggregate), AGGREGATE-FIELD-WRITE (`p.x = 5;` - cheap on this model but adds a rule to every composition), AGGREGATE-FIELD-TYPES (a field of a type other than i32), AGGREGATE-NESTED (a record field whose type is another record - needs a recursive rule and a termination argument for the declaration graph), AGGREGATE-ACROSS-CALL (a record-valued parameter or result), AGGREGATE-ROUTE-WIDENING (admitting the construct on the string, event, socket, HTTP, extern, task, mutex or epoch routes - each a separate checked model), AGGREGATE-STRING-COMPOSE (the composed string/buffer route, which refuses a record at Q068 today), AGGREGATE-BOUND-FROM-FIELD (a `for` bound read out of a field - known to the checker, not to the lowering, exactly LOOP-BOUND-FROM-BYTE's shape), AGGREGATE-REFUSAL-CASCADE (a refused construction leaves its binding unbound, so a later field read earns a second diagnostic; needs a poisoned-binding notion this route does not have, and the cascade is left alone rather than suppressed), AGGREGATE-LIBRARY-MODULE (a `module library;` file declaring a record, refused at Q058 today - a record type that outlives its file is a module-system question this revision's one-entry routes do not pose), AGGREGATE-SELECTOR-WORDS (the six route-selector words above), AGGREGATE-CT09-LAYOUT (CT09's LAYOUT proof; this card supplies the ACCESS proof and an executed layout OBSERVATION, and the honest reading is not to conflate them) and EXAMPLES-AGGREGATES (a published examples/records/ family - see EXAMPLES-SUITE-O). One measurement-hygiene finding is published rather than hidden, because it cost a full workspace run: a gitignored baseline tree extracted under measure/ is nonetheless VISIBLE TO A TEST THAT WALKS THE FILESYSTEM, and a whole-tree census test saw four .qcore files where it pins two. A baseline tree must be removed before the gate runs, or kept outside the worktree; gitignoring it is not enough.

named_followups.title: The quantitative error region has a source path; thirteen residuals, and the operation variant was measured unreachable by design
named_followups.why: QUANT-REGION-SOURCE closes CT21/CT22's recorded gap - 'no source path emits RegionOp::QuantOpen' - and CORRECTS ITS OWN FRAMING IN THE PROCESS. source.region.v1 lands `error region NAME { ... } catch (ERROR) quant open NAME as BINDING { discharge BINDING; }` on the SEQUENTIAL route: it is not a route of its own and selects nothing, which is what gives it the existing certificate, reference execution, C emission and native comparison unchanged, and every other route keeps the refusal it already had (measured, not assumed). The sealed CleanupPack is bound as a LINEAR capability consumed EXACTLY ONCE - that linearity is the whole content of the word 'quant' here - and the region's body admits five kernel operations (Acquire, Drop, AddStrictCredit, SpendStrictCredit and the decided Raise), so this is NOT the open-plus-close-with-an-empty-interior fallback the card allowed for. ZERO reserved words (every word is already reserved and the shape already parsed, so the census is EXACT rather than statistical: before the card the statement collected R as a referenced name and refused at Q013, which means no program in this repository could contain it at all), ZERO new codes (Q302's condition widened to the reader's own shape refusals, with Q303-Q309 and Q300 reached from a second route at the codes that pass already allocates), NO new SourceOp, NO new CFG terminator and NO C backend rule. THE RECORDED GAP WAS MEASURED FALSE IN ONE HALF: RegionOp::QuantOpen, the operation VARIANT, is unreachable from a valid program BY DESIGN - its own doc comment says so - because the admitting constructor is the error_region::QuantOpen STRUCT on a catch clause, and the variant is retained so an opening outside a catch has an explicit Q302. The v1 PATH bound is deliberate and refused BY NAME rather than left silent, because analyze_error_regions calls handle_catch only for an error exit that reaches a matching clause, so a clause on a path the region does not take is a clause NOTHING DECIDES and admitting one would be silent rather than fail-closed. CT21 and CT22's ARCHIVED REASONS are retired - the opening and the credit both exist now, CT21 refusing at Q305 with two controls and CT22's credit half accepting with AbandonCredit(3) in the discharge's cleanup trace - while CT22 keeps a NARROWER gap in its scenario, 'after joins', which a lane must publish in its own stage-evidence record rather than carrying the archived one (constraint 23). The manifest is untouched and CT coverage does not move. 29 end-to-end tests, 8 unit tests, one new Lean module and audit whose load-bearing theorem produces the kernel's own discharge result and proves the emitted release sequence IS that result's cleanupTrace. Corpus-neutral. Standing constraint 15l records the erasure and the two do-not-repair rules. New: REGION-NORMAL-EXIT, REGION-MULTIPLE-CATCH, REGION-MULTIPLE, REGION-PROPAGATE, REGION-FAILING-ACQUIRE, REGION-IN-ARM, REGION-HANDLER-BODY, REGION-CATCH-PAYLOAD-BINDING and REGION-NESTED (each a refused shape with the capability it needs named - a multi-path region analysis, per-region diagnostic attribution, a second emission shape for a sealed pack leaving the entry, the handler's own statement vocabulary, four models that join a branch, the payload vocabulary), REGION-EFFECT-ROW (the sequential route has no effects syntax, so a region-carrying entry's Throws row is DERIVED from the module's declared error set - a boundary, not a claim), REGION-OUTER-LIVE-RESOURCES (a resource acquired outside the region contributes no RegionOp, so the model's ledger is a region-local view rather than the entry's), REGION-QUANTOPEN-OP-VARIANT (above) and REGION-CREDIT-WITH-JOINS (CT22's 'after joins' half - the same missing composition CT23-T07-SEAM names from the other side: credits on one route, error paths and joins on another).

named_followups.title: A gateway diagnostic names the C a person wrote; presentation-only re-pin, eight residuals
named_followups.why: GATEWAY-C-LOCATION is wave 27's arbiter and the user's reserved slot. Every line number the existing-C gateway carries is a line of the unit's `clang -E -P` PREPROCESSED text, and diagnostics presented it directly - 'live obligation acquired at preprocessed line 19357' names a 20,471-line expansion no editor opens and no reader can check. By the user's ruling the presented coordinate is now the ORIGINAL, pre-preprocessing file:line (L19357 is flb_input_chunk.c:2267) and the preprocessed number stays INTERNAL - pin identity, leaf identity, certificate comparability. The map pairs the analysed -E -P text with a second, presentation-only MARKED -E run through the same marker reader legacy_enumeration has used since E01-TAIL, and the pairing is CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: same length and same trimmed text line for line, or the whole map is refused. The anti-forgery property is stronger than 'hard to forge' - NO PRESENTED FILE SPELLING IS EVER READ FROM A FLAGLESS MARKER - and rests on three rules: a frame's spelling is adopted only from an ENTERING marker, so a #line, which Clang re-emits flagless, can never write one; include depth 0 is not named by a marker at all but resolved by the caller against the audit's own configured file; and a disagreeing flagless marker WITHDRAWS the coordinate for every line it governs rather than relabelling it, the diagnostic falling back to 'preprocessed line N', which names itself as internal. Proved in general as presented_files_are_entered_files (QCore.SourceCoordinate, one new audit file), with both measured #line directions of E01-TAIL pinned against real preprocessings. Standing constraint 12 is untouched: the scope reader is not read, not written and cannot be influenced, and the map is built only AFTER a unit's result is settled. Four fail-closed grounds all carry ReasonCategory::EnvironmentUnavailable on the producer-supplied path, so SS L21.1 rule 1 applies and none can contribute to a provisional Unsafe; a refused unit keeps every internal position and is never given an approximate coordinate. THE RE-PIN IS PRESENTATION-ONLY AND MEASURED TO BE: a fresh Clang pin, both runs reading the same 1,415-entry database, the BEFORE run reproducing the preceding baseline's diagnostics.json and chunk-contracts.json BYTE FOR BYTE, and the AFTER run compared leaf by leaf by the card's own oracle at ZERO STOP findings - 185 units, 4,834 functions, 54,383 diagnostics each with the same (function, preprocessed line, category), every unit key but functions and origin_coordinates byte-identical, every function row's status unchanged, leak 266, unknown_alias 4,344 and unsupported 49,773 all unmoved, and four of the five artifacts byte-identical between the two runs. What moved: 54,371 rows gained an origin, 266 descriptions had their SITE substituted (exactly the leak leaves - the only category here whose text names one, each rewrite verified to leave the text on both sides byte-identical), 178 unit rows gained an origin_coordinates account and two envelope keys changed. ZERO withdrawn lines and ZERO refused derivations across the corpus, so the anti-forgery rules are load-bearing for the PROPERTY rather than for the numbers. Spot checks read each coordinate back out of the pinned checkout by hand, reproducing the wave-22/23 records' :2483 and :2623 oracles and a deterministic cross-library sample. The corpus baseline moves to docs/reports/gateway-c-location/artifacts/; the preceding archives stay frozen. New: GATEWAY-LOCATION-LINE-ONLY-DIRECTIVE (a #line with no file spelling renumbers the file it is written in and is indistinguishable from one of Clang's own resynchronisations, which it must be, or every file with an #if 0 block would lose its coordinate; it moves no file identity, no include depth and no audited scope, and is the directive's C11 SS 6.10.4 meaning), GATEWAY-LOCATION-CONTRACT-TEXT (contract-text locations are out of scope BY THE USER'S RULING for this card), GATEWAY-LOCATION-INTERNAL-CHANNELS (the certificate, source-effects.json, chunk-contracts.json, the census APIs and the probe examples keep the preprocessed position - the user's ruling, not an omission), GATEWAY-LOCATION-INPUT-IDENTITY-REFUSAL (two unit-level refusal texts still name a preprocessed or input line; they fire BEFORE any analysis, where no map exists and no unit row is published, and one is additionally pinned by a qcore-schemas test), GATEWAY-LOCATION-SYNTHETIC-EXIT (12 leak rows sit at the synthetic preprocessed line 0 and carry origin null; giving a synthetic exit a coordinate would mean CHOOSING one, which this card will not do - their text still names the acquisition's original coordinate), GATEWAY-LOCATION-UNSAFE-REPREPROCESS (the Unsafe arm carries no preprocessed text and re-runs validate_unrestricted_c11 to obtain the authoritative bytes rather than accept a text derived another way; adding the field would touch 37 match sites), GATEWAY-LOCATION-SECOND-PREPROCESS (one extra marked -E run per unit with diagnostics; the enumeration already holds that output and could hand it over, but changing its shape touches the pinned denominator route - E01-TAIL-COST-DOUBLE-PP from the presentation side) and GATEWAY-LOCATION-HEADER-REACH (the header arm is exercised only by a fixture, because the pinned route's MainSourceDefinitions scope puts all 54,371 presented coordinates at depth 0).

named_followups.title: A hand edit to a carried matrix section can leave the derived count beside it stale
named_followups.why: Measured by card CT-WIRE-LANE-4 (wave 32) while taking constraint 25's clobber question seriously rather than assuming it. The committed matrix's dimensions.named_followups read 39 against 40 rows actually present in the carried named_followups section: commit 1c7d8e45 added the TRACE-ALPHABET-LEASE-REFUSAL-UNEXERCISED row by hand and did not move the derived count beside it, so the file was INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT between regenerations and nothing checked the pair. Tracing that produced a second consequence of the same edit: the file was also reserialized to the pre-HYGIENE-16 indent=2 format, having matched the generator's own indent=1 output at d31a8dc3, b5838915 and the wave-31 close -- so commit 1c7d8e45 wrote this file OUTSIDE ITS GENERATOR, and the next regenerating lane inherits an unreviewably large whole-file diff, as CT-WIRE-LANE-4 did. This lane's regeneration repairs both. The general shape stands as the residual: `dimensions` is DERIVED (`counted from the emitted rows`) while `named_followups`, `requirements` and the other hand-maintained sections are CARRIED, so any hand edit to a carried section can silently desynchronise a derived count and drift the file's format, with nothing checking either in between. Discharge: a check that compares each derived dimension against the carried section it counts -- the same shape as HYGIENE-14's repair of the bucket tally -- plus a format assertion, or a stated decision that hand edits are expected here and the counts advisory between regenerations. PARTIALLY DISCHARGED by card STABILITY-REEVAL-1 (wave 34), and narrowed rather than closed. scripts/tests/test_build_matrix_sections.py gains class CommittedMatrixIsSelfConsistent with two tests against the COMMITTED matrix - which is the gap, since the two pre-existing tests compare generator output against generator output, both self-consistent by construction, so neither could ever see drift in the committed file. That is why this residual fired twice and was caught both times by a person. test_each_derived_dimension_matches_the_section_it_counts covers the two dimensions whose name IS a section name (requirements, named_followups); test_the_committed_matrix_keeps_the_generators_byte_format covers the second half, a hand edit in another serialisation - the exact condition of commit 1c7d8e45, which buried a single real line in a 12,673-line reserialisation diff. Both were shown non-vacuous by mutation: setting dimensions.named_followups to 45 (the exact historical drift) turns the first red, and re-serialising at indent=2 turns the second red; the matrix was restored and verified byte-identical by sha256 afterwards. STILL OPEN: the derived cell and product counts (requirement_evidence_cells, ct_cells, ct_rows, unverified_spec_items), which this card deliberately left alone because each needs its own derivation rule and a wrong one would pin a wrong number.

named_followups.title: `return CALL(args)` with a non-neutral contract or summary is withdrawn, with its measurement published
named_followups.why: Card C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION (wave 33) offered two sub-shapes and landed one. Sub-shape B - apply a callee's declared contract or validated W4 summary at a return position - is WITHDRAWN, and the grounds are measured over the real population rather than sampled. Of the 335 `return CALL(...)` leaves among the 511 functions the baseline blocks on the return position alone, only 12 (3.6%) name a callee with a declared contract; 94 name a callee the corpus already reports as uncontracted elsewhere and 227 name one declared nowhere, so for 323 of 335 clearing the return refusal would merely EXCHANGE it for a `call to uncontracted function` leaf and decide nothing. A cross-cut by whether W4 could derive a summary at all puts 236 of 335 (70.5%) in the unit's own .c and 99 outside it. Note also that a call whose contract is all-Borrowed with result None is ALREADY admitted today through admitted_neutral_call, so B's real content is narrower than it sounds. The soundness cost is decisive: applying a callee's Consumed/Released parameter mode at a return position would DISCHARGE a live obligation of the caller at that exit - invariant 1's forbidden direction - on a route whose observe_exit has no arm for a call result at all, constructing ReturnedValue only from EscapeIfOwned/Escape. Discharge: a card that lands a return-position effectful instruction together with its ReturnedValue construction, the matching summary validation and the certificate recheck, and that states up front how many functions it DECIDES rather than how many refusals it converts. Its decisive population today is 12.

named_followups.title: Most pure field-chain returns are refused by member typing, and the cost is unmeasured per premise
named_followups.why: Card C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION (wave 33) admitted a pointer-valued bounded typed access chain in a `return` and moved 33 of the 511 return-only-blocked functions (6.5%). The natural candidate population is the 75 pure field-chain returns the card's whole-population census measured, of which only 31 are admitted. The remainder fail on F4 premises the card must not weaken: the member is not typed EXACTLY `struct TAG *` (a `char *`, a `cfl_sds_t`, a typedef the reader will not resolve, a `void *`), the record is incomplete, a union or has more than one definition in the unit, or the base is bound because it is named in some call's argument list elsewhere in the body. Discharge: measure, PER REFUSED PREMISE, how many functions a widened member typing would decide - PREDICTED BEFORE IT IS ATTEMPTED, as AOM-POISON-CONDITION-FRAME's discharge condition requires - and only then decide whether any premise can be widened without losing the base-premise argument the wave-33 admission rests on. That argument is that an admitted chain names no place the projection binds; a premise that weakens the base is not a typing change but a soundness change, and must land RETURN-POSITION-ESCAPE-UNREACHABLE's test in the same card.

named_followups.title: A fresh worktree starts without third_party/libevent and nothing forces the init before a gate
named_followups.why: AGENTS.md's standing gate opens with `git submodule update --init --recursive`, described as once per checkout, and invariant 5 pins the submodule revision with a test that fails if it is absent or moved. A delegated card's worktree is a fresh checkout, so the step is due every time and is enforced only by each agent remembering it. Wave 33 lost work to this twice: C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION reported the libevent pin gate firing at the END of an audit run and costing it a full BEFORE run, and the integrator's own first gate on the VERIFIER-HOST-CLOSED-INPUT-DEADLINE candidate reported 10 failures - the revision pin plus every libevent census and header test - all of which vanished after the init, with 4,544 passed / 0 failed. Two independent hits in one wave is a process defect rather than bad luck, and the cost is asymmetric: the failure surfaces late and reads like a regression. Discharge: make the gate self-check the submodule before it runs anything expensive, or have worktree creation do the init, so a defective checkout cannot be mistaken for a defective change.

named_followups.title: an_off_cycle_node_does_not_return's hypothesis asserts whole-graph acyclicity, so it is vacuous exactly where its card operates
named_followups.why: proof/QCore/JoinedProvenanceCycles.lean:153 states an_off_cycle_node_does_not_return with the single hypothesis (increasing : forall p n, n in g.succ p -> rank p < rank n), which ranges over EVERY edge and so asserts the whole graph is acyclic; under it no node returns to itself, trivially, for every node. It therefore says nothing about an off-cycle node IN A GRAPH THAT HAS CYCLES, which is the only case card JOINED-PROVENANCE-CYCLES exists for. The shipped code tests exactly that excluded case: crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_joined_provenance.rs:218 acyclic_sites is a PER-NODE test (on_cycle(node) is 'node is reachable from itself') run inside fixed_point, whose doc comment says it is 'computed as the greatest fixed point over a cyclic graph'. SECOND LAYER, also measured: Steps (line 136) is pure graph reachability, while the property the docstring and report claim ('runs at most once PER CALL') is about execution; the file HAS an execution relation, Reach (line 48, carrying a World), and the off-cycle theorem does not use it. The ledger is clean - grep -c an_off_cycle_node_does_not_return AGENTS.md is 0 - so the overreach lives in the Lean docstring (lines 148-152) and in docs/reports/joined-provenance-cycles/README.md:154-156. DISCHARGE: prove the per-node property over Reach for a graph that may contain cycles elsewhere - the statement the code needs - or record that the theorem covers wholly acyclic graphs and that acyclic_sites' restriction is OBSERVED, not proved, published beside the report rather than edited into it (constraint 21).

named_followups.title: fixed_point_is_sound is described by the hypothesis it lacks rather than the premise that carries it, and TransferSound is named nowhere outside Lean
named_followups.why: AGENTS.md says 'soundness on a cycle is fixed_point_is_sound, proved by induction on the arrival with no acyclicity hypothesis'. True, but the theorem carries three hypotheses and the principal one is (transfers : forall p n, TransferSound g site p n) - the abstract transfer is sound on EVERY edge. rg TransferSound over the whole tree returns hits in ONE file only, the Lean module itself: the premise is named in neither the report, the increment record nor AGENTS.md. The card does carry a general caveat (GATEWAY-LEAN-ABSTRACT-NOT-EXTRACTION, report:133-137) naming three premises - extraction, CFG construction, declared release effects - but the abstract interpretation's own correctness obligation is a fourth and is the one that does the work. This is STABILITY-REEVAL method step 2 exactly: the theorem is PROVED, its premise about the shipped transfer is OBSERVED. DISCHARGE: name TransferSound in the report's premise list beside the other three, or discharge it against the shipped transfer.

named_followups.title: acyclic_solution_is_unique holds only among solutions agreeing at the entry, and the ledger states it without that condition
named_followups.why: AGENTS.md: 'the fixed-point equation has exactly one solution on an acyclic graph (acyclic_solution_is_unique), so no acyclic body's verdict can move.' named_followups.title: Constraint 5c says modelling for(;;) exactly is untaken and would need Lean plus a re-pin; the shipped CFG builder has done it since Cycle 19 with neither

named_followups.title: The invariant that keeps a known non-null pointee-less pointer from arising holds at all fourteen write sites and is asserted nowhere
named_followups.why: This card asked whether an AbstractPointer can be inserted with targets empty, unknown false and may_be_null false - a claim of a known, non-null, pointee-less pointer that downstream readers could take as resolved. ANSWER: NO, measured by exhaustive enumeration of every construction, insertion, join and in-place mutation in legacy_c.rs. The invariant is targets.is_empty() implies (unknown || may_be_null). It holds at all six struct literals, the clone insertion, all three join arms, and every write to the two booleans; the single non-literal unknown=false site (:7887) immediately sets may_be_null (:7888), and the load-bearing may_be_null=false site (:7890) is guarded at :7880 by unknown || targets.len() > 1, so an empty-targets binding reaching it had unknown true. But the invariant is asserted NOWHERE - no doc comment on the struct (legacy_c.rs:5257-5263), no debug_assert, no Lean - and it rests on two conjuncts a plausible well-intentioned edit would remove: widening the :7880 guard to 'also narrow the empty case', which reads like a completeness fix and makes :7890 produce the triple directly; and replacing the Infeasible early return at :7893-7898 with a fallthrough. DISCHARGE: state the invariant as a doc comment on AbstractPointer and enforce it at a single insertion helper with a debug_assert, and name it in constraint 10b beside 'Non-nullness does not establish lookup identity'. Cheap, and JOINED-PROVENANCE-CALL-FRAMES will be editing next door.

named_followups.title: AbstractPointer derives Default and its Default is exactly the triple the invariant forbids
named_followups.why: legacy_c.rs:5257 derives Default on AbstractPointer { targets, unknown, may_be_null }, so AbstractPointer::default() IS targets empty / unknown false / may_be_null false - the triple POINTER-EMPTY-TARGETS-INVARIANT-UNSTATED shows must never reach state.pointers. It does not today: the two AbstractPointer::default() uses at :6649 and :6652 are local temporaries handed to mark_unresolved_effect and discarded, and there is no state.pointers.entry(..).or_default() anywhere. But or_default() is the idiomatic Rust one-liner and is already used six times in this same file on the neighbouring field_links, contained and conditional_replacements maps, so a future entry(name).or_default() on pointers would insert the forbidden triple silently, with no compile error and no test failure. DISCHARGE: remove the Default derive and spell the two temporaries as explicit literals. Do NOT discharge it by making the default unknown: true - that would silently change those two temporaries' behaviour, since mark_unresolved_effect with unknown true marks EVERY resource, an accusing change needing its own re-pin.

named_followups.why: * **`CALL-FRAMES-ALLOWLIST-LOCAL-ONLY`** — **new, and a vacuity finding about this card's own work.** The frame test inside `step` cannot currently fire through `derive`: `outgoing` applies the same `conditional_names` membership test after **every** node, so every name reaching a call is already in the frame. The guard is therefore a *local* enforcement of the premise, driven by a direct `step` test (`a_call_forgets_a_name_the_frame_list_does_not_carry`) and by §5's mutation, but no CFG can present it with an unrecognised name today. named_followups.title: The native comparison compares the logged event sequence, not the C operations beneath it; three mutations escaped before the repair
named_followups.why: Measured by card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) and published rather than smoothed over, because it is the STABILITY-REEVAL shape found inside the card's own new evidence. CT46's sanitized native run compares the emitted program's stdout byte for byte with interpret_mutex_program's observation, and that stdout is produced by the typed diagnostic sink -- so it is evidence about the LOGGED sequence. Three mutations of the emitted C therefore ran byte-identical, exit 0, clean under ASan/UBSan/LSan: (a) deleting the real mtx_lock while keeping its log line; (b) moving the real mtx_unlock away from its log line; (c) calling the child function directly instead of thrd_create. Two repairs landed in the same card rather than a caveat: run_mutex_crossing now asserts on the EMITTED TEXT that every logged mutex event is immediately preceded by its own mtx_lock/mtx_unlock call -- the adjacency one renderer writes, proved as QCore.MutexShareCrossEmission.a_logged_acquisition_is_preceded_by_a_real_one -- and the thread boundary is pinned by emitted_c_contains plus a main_excludes check. With those, (a), (b) and (c) go red. WHAT REMAINS: the adjacency check covers the mutex operations only. A dropped payload WRITE is caught for a different reason -- the following read's sum is computed by C and would move -- but that is an accident of this fixture's shape, not a rule, and no equivalent structural check exists for touch/log pairs. DISCHARGE: extend the adjacency assertion to every (operation, log) pair the emitter writes, and drive each with its own emitter mutation; or state the non-mutex pairs as a measured boundary with the reason each is caught by something else.

named_followups.title: A typed-error exit inside a child refuses, because the model gives a child's exit status no meaning at the join
named_followups.why: Card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) admits a non-nested fork/join mutex trace and refuses one whose child segment carries a MutexInvariantEvent::ErrorExit, classified Outside at the segment's own Spawn. The ground is that CheckedMutexInvariantV1 gives a child's typed-error exit no meaning AT THE JOIN: the emitted child function would have to return a status, and the creator would have to do something with it, and neither is anything the model decides. Rendering one would therefore invent semantics, so the arm fails closed instead. The refusal is driven by a hand-built trace in crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/mutex_c_emit.rs and shown non-vacuous by mutation, and it is proved in QCore.MutexShareCrossEmission (a_child_error_exit_is_refused). Whether it is reachable from SOURCE was not measured: lower_child_task refuses a typed-error exit at a child's top level, so reaching it needs one inside a `with lock` in the child's body. DISCHARGE: give the model a meaning for a child's error exit at the join and render it, or measure the source-level reachability and record the arm as a justified backstop, as MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-ARMS did for its arms C and D.

named_followups.title: CT46's fork/join rendering has had no MSVC run, and none is claimed
named_followups.why: Card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) compiles and runs CT46's own emitted C under ASan/UBSan/LSan on LINUX only. The manifest's four flipped stages are gated linux/macos for the run and linux/macos/windows for the emission, exactly as the route's existing sanitized runner is, and the emitted program's thread operations go through the embedded c11_threads_compat.h whose Windows arm is the winpthreads subset. No cl.exe or clang-cl run of a fork/join mutex program has happened, so no Windows claim is made -- the SLICE-PERMISSIONS-WINDOWS-RUN / WRITE-LEND-TASKS-WINDOWS-RUN precedent, and MSVC ships no ASan/UBSan in this harness in any case. DISCHARGE: run compiler/tests/ct_corpus.rs::ct_manifest_and_fixture_set_agree_and_mapped_cases_execute on a Windows host with the emitted CT46 program compiled by cl.exe, and record the byte comparison; the sanitizer half stays unclaimed there by construction.

named_followups.title: CT46's fork/join rendering has had no macOS run, and none is claimed
named_followups.why: The Apple sibling of MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-WINDOWS-RUN. Card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) gates CT46's native and sanitized stages linux/macos and the harness compiles the same file on both, but only the Linux arm was exercised. The macOS arm additionally differs in two recorded ways: Apple's AddressSanitizer implements no LeakSanitizer, so the harness forces detect_leaks=0 there and the reclamation of the protected allocation would be unwitnessed; and C11 threads reach Apple Clang through the pthread-backed subset. DISCHARGE: run the CT corpus on a macOS host and record which half of the Linux evidence reproduces -- byte comparison yes, leak detection no, on the EVENT-V1-APPLE-RUN precedent.

named_followups.title: The worker-side lease exercise's native test ran the Linux arm only; no Windows or Apple run is claimed
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) landed the worker-side range write and its sanitized native comparison: two threads writing distinct bytes of one int32_t payload under ASan/UBSan/LSan, native stdout byte-identical to the reference execution's own rendering, one allocation released once. That run is LINUX. The macOS arm compiles the same test file (the Apple threads shim include is wired) but was not executed here, and no MSVC run has happened at all. The tests/support/windows_c.rs path is carried UNCHANGED by this card - the emitted difference is two new preamble helpers and two diagnostic kinds, neither platform-specific - so this is an unexercised arm rather than a suspected one, on the WRITE-LEND-TASKS-WINDOWS-RUN and STRING-CONCAT-WINDOWS-RUN precedent. No Windows or Apple claim is made or implied anywhere in the card's report or in standing constraint 15h's appendix. named_followups.title: A program mixing whole-payload and byte access has a host-dependent observation, because the payload's object representation is
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) made the worker's byte write a write to a real byte of the emitted struct qcore_buffer's int32_t payload - ((unsigned char *)&buffer->payload)[index] - deliberately, because that and only that makes two workers' writes DISTINCT MEMORY LOCATIONS under C11 6.2.6.1/4 and 3.14 and therefore not a data race. A value-level read-modify-write of the whole payload was considered and REJECTED for exactly that reason, not for cost. The consequence is that the relation between a byte at index i and the int32 value is the host's object representation. The reference execution models the same representation (i32::to_ne_bytes), so reference and emitted C AGREE ON EVERY HOST and nothing here is unsound; what is host-dependent is a published TRANSCRIPT of a program that mixes whole-payload and byte access. The card's flagship is representation-independent BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck: C11 7.20.1.1 makes int32_t two's complement with no padding bits, so the initial value 0 has an all-zero representation on every conforming host, and a byte written at index i and read back at index i is the same byte whatever the order of the four. The route admits the mixed programs with this boundary stated rather than refusing them, because refusing would need per-buffer byte-write history the checker does not carry. CONDITION: either commit the route to a byte order at the reference/emission boundary, or refuse a whole-payload access on a buffer with byte-write history - whichever a later card measures to be cheaper - and say which programs each choice costs.

named_followups.title: The owner has no byte write: the whole-payload write remains its only write footprint, deliberately
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) gave a LEASE HOLDER a byte write and deliberately did not give one to the owner, and the reason is a dependency rather than a preference. Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS' rule that 'the owner holds no whole-payload authority, read included, while any lease is out' is stricter than both the read-share route and the sequential lend's per-byte exclusion, and standing constraint 15h states WHY in one clause: because the owner's only spellable footprint here is the whole payload. Admitting an owner byte write would introduce a second owner-side footprint that rule was never measured against, and would immediately raise a question the route has no answer to - whether an owner byte write OUTSIDE every live lease is admitted, which is an ADMITTING direction and so needs the per-byte owner exclusion the ledger does not currently compute. The refusal is in the IR and driven by its own test (the_ir_refuses_an_owner_byte_write), not only by the frontend's earlier message. The owner's byte READ is admitted, and takes the same ledger gate its whole-payload read takes, so a lease outstanding refuses it by the existing rule. CONDITION: a card that wants an owner byte write must re-measure wave 31's whole-payload suspension against a second owner-side footprint and land the per-byte owner exclusion, with the disjointness decided by ownership::axes_overlap as everywhere else.

named_followups.title: A read share admits the whole-payload read and no byte view
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) admits a byte read through a write lease (relative to its low) and through an owner (absolute), and refuses one through a borrow<Buffer> read share by name, in the IR, driven by its own test (the_ir_refuses_a_byte_read_through_a_read_share) as well as by the frontend's earlier message. The refusal is fail-closed and cheap to keep: a read share is a COUNTED share of the whole payload, and giving it a byte view would need a cross-model rule relating share counts to byte ranges that no model in the tree states. Nothing is blocked by the refusal today - the whole-payload read a share already admits is strictly more information than any byte of it. CONDITION: a card that wants byte-granular read shares supplies the rule relating counted shares to ranges, on the sequential route's read-loan overlap precedent (constraint 15h: two overlapping BORROWS are deliberately not refused, because both are immutable and conflict on nothing), and shows it non-vacuous in both directions.

named_followups.title: A range write lease's bounds live in [0, 4) because the task route's Buffer payload is one int32_t
named_followups.why: Introduced by card WRITE-LEND-TASKS (wave 31) and NOT discharged by WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36), which makes it more valuable rather than less. BUFFER_PAYLOAD_BYTES is 4 - the real bytes of the emitted struct qcore_buffer's int32_t payload - so every lease of this route is a sub-range of four bytes and a two-worker disjoint split is two bytes each. Wave 36 turned that from a permission into a demonstration: two threads really do write distinct bytes of one object under the sanitizers. But four bytes is a thin demonstration, and the interesting cases for disjoint concurrent writing - a split buffer worked on by several workers, a chunked fill - are all out of reach until a byte-extent buffer (bytes(N)) can cross a spawn. Recorded here because wave 36's report names it and no tracker held it. CONDITION: as wave 31 stated it - a bytes(N) buffer crossing a spawn boundary, with the lease bounds decided against that extent rather than against the int32 payload, and the emitted C carrying the real allocation. Amended by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: a record field of type `bytes` in a task module refuses by this name (`Q500`) — the task route's owned record field is `own<Buffer<T>>`, and a byte-extent buffer still crosses no spawn.

named_followups.title: The sixth constraint-16 row measured failing at mid-range load, after its repair
named_followups.why: `closed_input_does_not_mask_descendant_timeout_or_accept_a_partial_request` (crates/qcore-verifier-host/tests/standalone_host.rs:175) failed once inside a full gate at load average ~40 on 16 cores and passed 12/12 in isolation at load 23.7 to 27.6. named_followups.title: Two over-approximations of constraint 5's one sentence disagree on 16% of the family
named_followups.why: `FunctionTypes::may_bind` (bound_names) and `UntrackedBases::never_bound` (untracked_bases) disagree on 2,933 leaves (16.0%): 2,893 where may_bind says the base is bindable and never_bound says it is not, and 40 the other way. Constraint 5's wording is may_bind's, and may_bind is the stricter refuser here, so a card reading never_bound works in a space roughly FOUR TIMES larger than the constraint describes without saying so. Neither function is defective; they are consumed by different rules. It is a trap for any wave-37 arbiter. DISCHARGE: state in constraint 5 which reading the premise names, or prove the two agree wherever an admission consults them.

named_followups.title: One unparsable member declaration makes every member of that record unclassifiable
named_followups.why: `TypedAccessModel::read_record_body` refuses a whole record body on any '(', ')', '{', '}', ':' or '=', so 173 of 909 record tags (19.0%) in the pinned corpus are refused wholesale - 98 on '{', 66 on '(', 9 on ':' - accounting for 2,713 unresolved-member leaves. The one genuine CODE DEFECT the census found, filed on its own merits. It is NOT a promising arbiter: the measured ceiling is 2 sole-blocked functions, 1 with constraint 5's premise intact. DISCHARGE: a per-member total-or-reject reader - classify the member declarations that parse, mark the ones that do not as explicitly unreadable so they stay refused - landed with its own measured re-pin, or a recorded decision that the 2-function reach does not justify the risk. NOT A DISCHARGE: citing the 2,713 leaves. SECOND MEASURED VALUE, card BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37, sections 6.2 and 11.2; recorded at the wave-37 close): the two-function ceiling is the STANDALONE number. Beside the base-type reader's Rank 1 repair the same repair is worth five more functions, because 41.6% of Rank 1's leaves land on a record body refused whole. A repair worth 2 alone and 5 in company is a different proposition; the disposition itself (declined as a standalone arbiter) is a wave-38 cut decision and is not changed here. AMENDED (FB-LOOP-CHAIN-ACCESS-IDENTITY-BLOCKERS, report docs/reports/fb-loop-chain-blockers/README.md): the function-pointer part is repaired. read_record_body reads a body whose only unparsed member declarations are exactly SPECIFIERS ( * NAME ) ( PARAMETERS ); that member joins no class and every other member reads as without it (QCore.FunctionPointerDeclarators). Measured on the pinned corpus at main b157c9cba: +2 Safe, 104 Unknown rows trade leaves, no Safe -> non-Safe once rule 5g's store keeps its domain of fully read records (without it cio_options_init lost its Safe). Still refused whole: '{' (nested aggregates), ':' (bitfields), '=' and every other parenthesised declarator (arrays of function pointers, attributes). DISCHARGE (narrowed): a per-member reader for those shapes, measured with its own re-pin, or a recorded decision.

named_followups.title: Admitting an access can move counts in the admitting direction for unrelated reasons
named_followups.why: A cross-cutting soundness hazard for every admission candidate, and the one most easily missed. Admitting an access makes its statement no longer refused, so that statement's RefusedWrites no longer poisons any binding. Constraint 10a already records that sparing a binding can UNMASK a stale scalar fact a NoOp mutation left behind (AOM-POISON-NOOP-INCREMENT: `pass++` lowering to NoOp so a Clear-bound scalar stays definitely-null for ever, making a `pass != 0` edge Infeasible and suppressing the refusals inside it). A wave-37 arbiter's re-pin can therefore move counts for reasons unrelated to the access it admits. DISCHARGE: the arbiter measures, for its own admitted set, how many refusals disappear through an edge becoming infeasible rather than through the access being modelled, and publishes the two numbers apart.

named_followups.title: The Declaration arm's census reads a window the gate did not read
named_followups.why: For the 15 `Declaration`-arm leaves the gate's predicate is not `contains_unmodeled_access` but a separate bracket/dot test over the declaration prefix, so the census reads a different window from the gate. 15 leaves of 18,555; recorded rather than repaired. DISCHARGE: give the declaration arm its own census window, or state the arm is out of every arbiter's scope and drop the axis for it.

named_followups.title: One published leaf of 18,555 is explained by no census statement
named_followups.why: 0.01% of the family. The likeliest cause is the `for`-clause path: `classify_simple` is also called for a `for` init and increment clause, where the statement the parser attributes is the `for`'s own line rather than the clause's first token, so the census's (function, line) key can miss. Not chased, because it is one leaf and the direction is understood. named_followups.title: CT10-REASON-ROW and MATRIX-UPDATED-STALE-AT-WAVE-27 are now both a deferred decision and a named_followup
named_followups.why: Card STABILITY-REEVAL #2 registered both names in named_followups, correctly, because STABILITY-REEVAL #1 had raised them and no tracker carried them (STABILITY-REEVAL-1-RESIDUALS-ORPHANED). This is also the shape STABILITY-REEVAL #2 item 5 asks the close rule to cover from the other direction (retiring a tracker entry must re-home every name it was the sole tracker for). DISCHARGE: state which mechanism owns a name that is both, and add the cross-check to the close rule - or, if both are to be kept, make each entry name the other so ending one is visibly half the job. CT-REMAINING-IMPLEMENTATION resolves CT10-REASON-ROW in both its tracker retirement and its reconciliation deferred_decisions record. The next numbered wave close must carry that resolved decision because outstanding_decisions discovers only numbered close directories. The other names and the general dual-tracking mechanism remain open.

named_followups.title: 158 leaves of the dominant base-type cause name an anonymous aggregate, which no tag-resolving reader change can reach
named_followups.why: Introduced by BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37). The card's Rank 1 reader change resolves TypedefTarget::Aggregate("struct TAG") to DeclaredType::Record(TAG). 158 of the cause's 3,220 leaves (4.9%) carry the head `struct` with NO tag - typedef struct { ... } t; - so there is nothing to resolve to; 33 more carry `union`, which must stay Opaque because a union member may overlap a pointer, and 4 carry `enum`. Reaching the anonymous ones needs a SYNTHETIC tag keyed on the typedef name, which is a new record identity that W4 derivation, W4 validation and certificate rechecking would all have to reproduce (constraint 8's both-readers rule). DISCHARGE: a card that lands the synthetic tag with its own measured re-pin, or a recorded measured decision that 158 leaves do not justify a new record identity.
