named_followups.title: An element store from a named pointer (`v[i] = p`) stays refused
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS admits an element store only when its value is an acquiring contract call (every parameter borrowed, an owned result) or the null constant. After `v[i] = p` the name `p` would remain an alias of an element whose custody the collection now holds: a later release through `p` would be a second release the ranges do not see, and a later borrow of `p` after the element's release a use after release the projection could not report, because an unknown binding is admitted at a borrowed position. The card therefore keeps the refusal byte for byte (test `storing_a_named_pointer_keeps_the_refusal_it_had`). The base census counts 57 `NAME[...] = NAME` stores in 42 functions (36 Unknown), 4 of them from a name an acquiring call bound; it reads source tokens and does not separate pointer-to-pointer bases from scalar arrays. DISCHARGE: a rule that retires the stored name's binding into a refusal-bearing state (every later use refuses) or proves it dead, with Lean parity and a measured re-pin. AMENDED by CG11-POINTER-VALUED-STORES: unchanged; `v[i] = p` is decided by the older element route (W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS) before rule 10v is asked (hard invariant 3), and rule 10v would refuse a named pointer value anyway.

named_followups.title: Only the canonical counted `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)` carries an exit equation; the corpus fills by append over traversals and releases with `while (i-- > 0)`
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS recognises a counted loop only as `for (I = 0; I < B; I++)` around at least one lowered element operation, with `I` and `B` declared integers no other lvalue designates, no write of either in the body, no `break`/`goto`/label/`switch`, and an unsigned index no narrower than an unsigned bound. The append `v[n++] = ACQUIRE(...)` needs no loop recognition and is admitted in any loop. The base census found 20 loops around element stores or releases: 9 fill loops (1 canonical; the rest append over pointer or list traversals, which W43-INDEX-TRAVERSAL owns), 11 release loops (9 canonical), 0 partial-cleanup loops, 2 `while` loops (`while (i-- > 0) rd_free(grps[i]);`), and 6 non-canonical `for` loops (a member bound `args->qcnt`, a narrower unsigned index against a `size_t` bound in rd_kafka_conf_dump_free). Reconciled with W43-INDEX-TRAVERSAL on the merged tree (merge eea0b30b): traversal adds no separate fixpoint (the existing work list reaches the loop's fixed point), and the only fact both state is a declared scalar's zero. Traversal keeps it as a target-free binding in the custody pointer map, joined by the custody join, where any joining path lacking it drops it; this card keeps it in a collection-only set whose join ignores a path that is vacuous for the collection (a counted loop's body edge under a bound that is zero when clamped). Reading traversal's fact instead was measured: 5 of the 32 collection tests regress, the brief's fill-with-partial-cleanup among them, because the partial cleanup's first-iteration body edge is vacuous and its stepped index would erase the entry zero at the cleanup header. The body-edge `i < n` fact, the clamped zero, the exit equation `i = max(0, n)` and the vacuous edge have no traversal counterpart (traversal evaluates no bound). Both cards forget an index stepped in a subscript (`v[n++]`, `B[X++]`). DISCHARGE: a decrementing release sweep, `while` headers and member bounds read under their own premises, and the zero fact made vacuity-aware in the shared custody map so the collection-only copy can be deleted, each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin. RE-READ by CG27-LOOPS-RECURSION-BUDGETS (gateway rule 11x): unchanged. CG27's loop summary is the counted-user pass's, not the collection pass's; no decrementing sweep, `while` header or member bound is read, and the collection-only zero fact stays. Its custody counterpart, the work list's settled loop-head state, is now stated as an inductive invariant (QCore.LoopInvariants.Induction.postfixpoint_bounds_every_iterate), which is what a vacuity-aware shared zero fact would have to preserve.

named_followups.title: No contract or summary mode states "an owned array of owned elements": destroy helpers over a caller's array stay Unknown and a returned collection publishes no summary
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS decides collections this body acquired. A helper that releases a caller's array (`destroy_prometheus_label_list`, `destroy_prometheus_sample_list`, `free_metrics`, `free_resource_attributes`, `rd_kafka_conf_dump_free`, and cmetrics' seven `destroy_*_list` NULL-assigning loops) has an unbound formal base, so every element operation keeps its refusal byte for byte; and a body that returns a filled collection is itself Safe but its exit is observed as `Ambiguous`, because a one-identity `Owned` summary would let a caller free the array and leak its elements (test `a_helper_returning_a_filled_collection_publishes_no_summary`). Resource vocabulary version 1 has no clause for element custody. DISCHARGE: a contract/summary clause for a collection result and a collection release (`resource_released_elements(p, n)` or similar) with loader, gateway, W4 validation and Lean parity, measured on the corpus.

named_followups.title: Automatic arrays of owned pointers (`T *a[N]`) and descriptor arrays (`int fds[N]`) are not collection owners
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS keys a collection by the heap identity of a `T **` base. An automatic array has no identity, its lifetime is the frame's, and it decays to a pointer a callee can reach whenever it is named without a subscript; `ut_tq_test`'s `struct ut_tq_head *tqh[3] = {NULL, …}` is the corpus witness (its braced initializer is refused as well). Descriptor, stream and directory elements are refused. On the merged tree with W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING (merge eea0b30b) a collection's owner, every element's acquisition and every discharging release must be of heap kind, a statement reading a tracked descriptor keeps its refusal, and all five element and loop instruction variants are refused by `admits_descriptor_read` (tests `a_stream_element_keeps_the_refusal_it_had`, `a_stream_release_of_a_heap_element_keeps_the_refusal_it_had`; Lean `only_heap_elements_are_collected`). A kind-indexed collection is not cheap: descriptor arrays are `int *fds` or `int fds[N]`, whose elements are integers (the `T **` premise, the null-test refinement and the null-constant store do not apply; validity is a `-1` sentinel), and a kind mismatch on an element would need its own settled-state accusation. At this card's census no descriptor release was contracted; W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING has since declared `close`. DISCHARGE: an automatic-array owner with its lifetime and decay premises, and kind-indexed elements (integer-carried descriptor collections with sentinel validity, stream and directory elements with kind-matched releases), each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: The element leak, element double release and element use-after-release arms reach no function of the pinned corpus
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS proves and unit-tests its accusing arms (tests `freeing_the_array_with_live_elements_is_an_element_leak`, `a_partial_cleanup_that_frees_only_the_array_leaks_the_prefix`, `releasing_an_element_twice_is_a_double_release`, `a_second_release_loop_is_a_double_release`, `testing_a_released_element_is_a_use_after_release`, `an_element_operation_through_a_released_array_is_a_use_after_release`, `overwriting_a_live_element_is_a_leak`; Lean QCore.IndexedCollection). At its arbiter no element operation's array resolved in any corpus function, so the AFTER diagnostics are byte-identical to BEFORE apart from the report's `scope` string, and the unchanged leak pin (271) records that absence rather than the arms' verification. DISCHARGE: the first arbiter in which an element operation's array resolves (most likely after W43-COLLECTION-SIZEOF-DEREFERENCE-ALLOCATION) attributes every element leaf it adds or removes, with a witness for each violation candidate.

named_followups.title: An element node carries its refusal as a fallback, so the certificate firewall does not see an unreached one as a retained `Unknown`
named_followups.why: check_legacy_safety_certificate rejects any function whose CFG retains a `LegacyInstruction::Unknown` node, even one the abstract semantics never reaches. Card W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS lowers an element store, release or null test to its own instruction carrying the classifier's refusal as `fallback`; the fallback applies (byte for byte) whenever the array does not resolve in the reaching state, and a node no state reaches applies nothing. The card treats an element node like any other modelled instruction (an unreached one raises nothing) rather than like a retained refusal, deliberately: counting it as `Unknown` would reject every Safe collection body. The difference from the firewall's stated caution is therefore real on a path the analysis pruned. DISCHARGE: a recorded decision that an unreached modelled element node needs no containment, or a firewall rule that rejects an element node with no settled incoming state, with the corpus re-measured.

named_followups.title: Several descriptor callees and kinds are observed only through the libc probe or not at all
named_followups.why: In the W43-DESCRIPTOR-NATIVE-CHECK measurement the observed Fluent Bit paths never call dup, dup2, fcntl(F_DUPFD), fdopen, fdopendir, dirfd, openat, pipe2, socketpair, eventfd, tmpfile or mremap (executed only by the libc probe), and nothing calls accept (the build uses accept4), dup3, memfd_create, mkstemp, popen/pclose or getifaddrs/freeifaddrs, so the process_stream and ifaddrs kinds are unobserved. Targets not exercised: upstream (client) connections with TLS, c-ares asynchronous DNS sockets, in_tail inotify, in_exec, librdkafka. References inside shared libraries (libssl, libcurl, libsystemd, libyaml, libsasl2, libc internals) are not interposed by --wrap. Discharge: a pinned scenario reaching each named callee from a Fluent Bit path with measured records, or a recorded determination that the pinned build does not reach it; and an LD_PRELOAD complement or a declared boundary for shared-library callers.

named_followups.title: flb_config_exit closes the engine manager channel's read descriptor twice, and closes -1 when the engine never started
named_followups.why: Observed in every run reaching full engine teardown (11 runs): flb_config_exit closes config->ch_event.fd (src/flb_config.c:607) and then config->ch_manager[0] (:617), one descriptor generation (flb_engine.c:1201 stores ch_manager[0] in ch_event), and the second close returns EBADF. When the engine never started, ch_event.fd is -1 and the nonzero guard calls close(-1) (37 runs). Only EBADF was observed; loss of a descriptor reused by another thread between the closes is inferred, not observed. Native observation, source-confirmed; not a static verdict. Discharge: an upstream change that closes the generation once (pinned rerun showing release_at_most_once and operand_identity_valid hold), or an explicit decision to leave it unreported. AMENDED (CELL-RESULT-SET-ALIGNMENT, 2026-11-04, docs/reports/cell-result-set-alignment/README.md): re-observed natively at 046accf6 and master 49592c4fd on every teardown (`close(13) = 0` then `close(13) = -1 EBADF`, the :607 alias of ch_manager[0] then :618). The flb_config.c:607 risk is this double close, not "-1 read as live". The user's patch (all three versions) removes the alias close and resets ch_event.fd; with the third version every teardown closes ch_manager once (v3-closed.strace). Evidence only.

named_followups.title: flb_sched_destroy closes every scheduler timer descriptor twice
named_followups.why: Observed 38 times in 10 runs: flb_sched_destroy (src/flb_scheduler.c:843) calls mk_event_timeout_destroy on each timer, which closes its descriptor, then flb_sched_timer_destroy -> flb_sched_timer_cb_disable closes it again because timer->timer_fd was never reset (mk_event_epoll.c:350); the second close returns EBADF. It runs on output worker threads while other threads are live, so a reuse race is possible but was not observed. Native observation, source-confirmed; not a static verdict. Discharge: an upstream change and a pinned rerun with release_at_most_once holding, or an explicit decision to leave it unreported.

named_followups.title: A storage root that cannot be read makes Fluent Bit double-free its ChunkIO context at shutdown
named_followups.why: Surfaced by W43-DESCRIPTOR-NATIVE-CHECK's injected opendir failure and reproduced without injection (storage.path directory with mode 0300): glibc aborts with 'free(): double free detected' in cio_destroy <- flb_storage_destroy (src/flb_storage.c:1000) <- flb_engine_shutdown. flb_storage_create's cio_load failure branch (src/flb_storage.c:727-732) destroys ctx->cio without clearing it, unlike the storage_backlog branch below it. Heap lifetime, outside the descriptor scope; the aborted run is kept as a rejected run. Discharge: an upstream fix with the pinned injection scenario accepted on rerun, or a recorded decision on routing it upstream.

named_followups.title: mk_socket_server leaks its socket when bind or listen fails
named_followups.why: The Monkey socket driver of W43-DESCRIPTOR-NATIVE-CHECK called the actual mk_socket_server on a listening port: bind fails with EADDRINUSE and the socket from mk_socket_create stays live at exit; the failure path (lib/monkey/mk_server/mk_socket.c:336-340) returns without closing it. No pinned Fluent Bit configuration reaches Monkey's server sockets, so this is a Monkey library error path. Discharge: an upstream Monkey fix with the pinned driver scenario showing no live socket at exit, or a recorded decision.

named_followups.title: A proxy plugin whose registration fails keeps its dl handle for the life of the process
named_followups.why: fluent-bit -e with a DSO lacking the flb- prefix routes to flb_plugin_proxy_create, which dlopens it and ignores flb_plugin_proxy_register's result; the proxy stays on config->proxies, which flb_config_exit never walks, so the handle is live at exit (observed once). Harmless for the CLI; for an embedding that calls flb_destroy and continues, the handle and proxy allocations would outlive the context (inferred). Discharge: a teardown of config->proxies or a refusal on registration failure, observed releasing the handle; or a decision that the process-lifetime handle is intended.

named_followups.title: The native descriptor observer can miss a multithreaded use after release and cannot tell the intended generation on reuse
named_followups.why: descriptor_observer.c records uses before the call and releases under its lock, so a use recorded before a release but executed after it is missed (false negative, never false positive); poll/select descriptor arrays and raw syscalls other than the recorded descriptor numbers are not observed; and, as with CT50-PROOF-ADDRESS-REUSE-UNPROVED, a reused number or address is a new generation whose intended owner the records cannot show. Discharge: a stronger ordering (for example per-descriptor sequencing across the call), interposition of the remaining use channels, or an explicit decision that these stay declared boundaries of the native evidence.

named_followups.title: ctr_random_get leaks descriptor 0 natively; the Fluent Bit binary does not reach that arm because startup takes descriptor 0 first
named_followups.why: W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING reports ctr_random_get provisional Unsafe (`if (fd > 0)` after open("/dev/urandom")) with the witness status 'reachable only if open returns 0; not observed natively'. The pinned build compiles that arm (its configure test leaves CTR_HAVE_GETRANDOM empty). W43-DESCRIPTOR-NATIVE-CHECK Phase B observed it: the actual lib/ctraces/src/ctr_random.c function, called by a driver whose stdin stream was closed first, got 0 from open, skipped read/close and exited with descriptor 0 live (pinned run ctraces.random.stdin_closed; the landed open contract admits 0 as a valid descriptor, 0 contradictions). Through the real binary (in_event_type traces, 10 calls) open returned 54, including with descriptor 0 closed at spawn, because flb_create's data pipe takes descriptor 0 first (W43-DESC-FLB-CONFIG-DATA-PIPE-ZERO-GUARD). Native observation under a stated precondition, not an upstream defect claim. Discharge: an upstream `fd >= 0` guard with the driver scenario showing no live descriptor at exit, or a recorded decision on routing it upstream.

named_followups.title: Started with descriptor 0 closed, Fluent Bit never closes its data pipe because flb_config_exit tests ch_data[0] for nonzero
named_followups.why: Observed by W43-DESCRIPTOR-NATIVE-CHECK Phase B (pinned run engine.event_type_traces_stdin_closed): with descriptor 0 closed at spawn, flb_create's flb_pipe_create(config->ch_data) (src/flb_lib.c:181) returns the pair [0, 3], and flb_config_exit guards its destroy with `if (config->ch_data[0])` (src/flb_config.c:611), so neither end is closed and both are live at exit. Same guard class as ctr_random_get's `fd > 0` and the `ch_event.fd` nonzero guard (W43-DESC-FLB-CONFIG-CHANNEL-DOUBLE-CLOSE). A process launched without standard input is the precondition; the CLI then exits, so the leak outlives nothing there, while an embedding calling flb_destroy and continuing would keep both descriptors (inferred). Native observation, source-confirmed; not a static verdict. Discharge: an upstream `>= 0` guard with the pinned scenario showing no live pipe at exit, or a recorded decision. APPENDED (CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE, 2026-11-03): the census finds the same guard class over Monkey creators' results in flb_config_exit itself (`config->ch_manager[0] > 0`, `config->ch_notif[0] > 0`, `config->ch_notif[1] > 0`, flb_config.c:617/:625/:627 at 046accf6), in flb_engine_started/flb_engine_failed (`ch_notif[1] <= 0`), flb_input_collector_destroy (`coll->fd_timer > 0` against a -1 sentinel) and elsewhere; source readings, listed in CELL-GUARD-DESCRIPTOR-ZERO-READ-AS-ABSENT and CELL-PROTOCOL-PER-END-GUARDS. AMENDED (CELL-RESULT-SET-ALIGNMENT, 2026-11-04, docs/reports/cell-result-set-alignment/README.md): re-observed natively at 046accf6 (stdin closed, -Y, two SIGHUPs, SIGTERM): ch_data is pipe2([0, 3]) and is never closed at either reload or exit; no later channel takes descriptor 0 (it stays held). The same on master 49592c4fd. The user's second patch version (`>= 0`) closed it once; the third (`> 0`) leaves fd 0 unclosed again, which the user accepted (USER DECISION 2026-11-04, verbatim: "Accept the leak"). Under the declared live set [1, MAX] the analyzer reads these `> 0` dead edges as absent (CELL-RESULT-SET-DESCRIPTOR-ZERO-POLICY). Evidence only; nothing filed upstream.

named_followups.title: Pointer-valued return reads: a load or an interior address
named_followups.why: Card W45-RETURN-EXPRESSION-FAMILIES admits a call-free read in `return` position only when the enclosing function's definition declares a scalar value result, so the returned value carries nothing whatever the operand's member typing. After it, 140 refused return leaves over 129 Unknown functions (37 sole-blocked) sit in functions returning a pointer (sized from the pinned source's definition line, docs/reports/w45-return-expression-families/census/residual-sizing.txt): 119 call-free accesses (`node->host`, `rk->rk_name`, `&rk->rk_conf`, `messages->elems[index]`), 14 compound expressions with a call, 6 conditionals, 1 comma. A pointer-valued `B->F` is a load when F is a pointer member but an interior address when F is an array (its decay), and `&B->F` always is one; an interior address is a result derived from B that must keep its derivation (`Derived` with `nullable`/`stepped`), and publishing it as a result that carries nothing would let a caller free B and keep using the result unaccused. Discharge: a card that tells loads from interior addresses by member typing, lowers a load through an untracked base to an exit that escapes nothing (constraint 5b's pointer-leaf answer) and an interior address to a derived binding the derived-result summary route (W43-RESULT-ALIAS-RETURNED) can validate, with Lean parity and a measured arbiter.

named_followups.title: Sub-object stores whose member the record reader does not resolve: 2,141 statements on 605 Unknown functions, 7 functions freed by them alone
named_followups.why: Card W45-SUB-OBJECT-STORES admits a sub-object store only into a scalar or single-pointer member of a complete, unambiguous, non-union struct. `read_record_body` is total-or-reject, so one function-pointer, bitfield, union or unread member refuses every member of the record: `(reply)->rkbuf_err = E` (880 parenthesised librdkafka stores, rd_kafka_buf_s), `otel_span->kind = ENUM` (an enum typedef member reads as aggregate-valued). Measured at the card's AFTER census (docs/reports/w45-sub-object-stores/census/residual-after.txt, reader class destination:member; the freed count is for this class alone with every other gate refusal of the function also in it). DISCHARGE: a per-member record reader (a member classified by its own declaration, with the record's layout premises stated) or typedef-enum members read as scalar, each with Lean parity for the reader and a measured re-pin of this rule. AMENDED by CG11-POINTER-VALUED-STORES (rule 10v): an identity-free pointer store into a member W45's lexical reader refuses (a record with a function-pointer or bit-field member elsewhere) is read by Clang's field id and admitted under rule 10v's premises (cio_options_init moves to Safe). Scalar stores and every other value keep this entry's refusal. Registered size carried, not re-run by its census.

named_followups.title: A clause-level review marker holds every call site of its declaration, not only those where the deferred clause decides the call
named_followups.why: Card W45-CONTRACT-DEFERRED-REVIEW withholds the whole contract for a clause-level marker (contract spec C06.1): a v1 contract is applied as one conjunction and no consumer applies part of one, so dropping only the deferred clause would let the remaining, possibly weaker, clauses decide. The consequence is that deferring a clause that does not decide a given call (a `resource_borrowed` scalar, say) still holds that call Unknown; the gateway test `a_deferred_clause_is_never_silently_dropped` pins this. DISCHARGE: a partial-application semantics that applies the undeferred clauses at a call site only when the deferred position provably carries no tracked identity there, with a Lean proof that the deferred clause cannot then decide the call, and a measured corpus re-pin showing no verdict moves towards Safe or Unsafe because of a deferred clause.

named_followups.title: The pending-review section counts recorded held-call refusals, a lower bound on textual call sites
named_followups.why: The `pending_human_review` section's `held_call_sites` counts the held-call refusals the analysis recorded. The analysis of a path stops at its first refused statement, so a second call to the same pending callee later on that path records no refusal of its own (measured in `qcore-audit`'s `every_marker_is_listed_with_its_digest_and_what_it_holds`: three textual call sites, two recorded). The section's `meaning` says so. DISCHARGE: count the call sites the gateway's hold rewrite (`review_hold::hold_call_sites`) rewrites per unit, publish them beside the recorded refusals, and pin the two counts on a fixture with a repeated call.

named_followups.title: The configured `quirin-audit CONFIG.json` route does not yet publish the pending-review section
named_followups.why: Card W45-CONTRACT-DEFERRED-REVIEW publishes `pending_human_review` and its console tally on `quirin-audit current`, `quirin-audit contracts` and the corpus arbiter, as its brief named; the configured route (`crates/qcore-audit/src/lib.rs`, the `.assumptions.json` sidecar) was left alone because a concurrent card was editing that file. Its unit rows already carry the `awaiting-human-review` reason code, since the gateway's unit reason carries it. DISCHARGE: add `qcore_audit::pending_review::section` to that route's assumptions sidecar and its tally to its console, with a configured-route test.

named_followups.title: A held call is published under the diagnostic category `unsupported`
named_followups.why: The gateway refuses a held call through the existing unmodelled-statement channel, so `diagnostics.json` lists it under `category: unsupported` and counts it in `diagnostic_counts.unsupported`, exactly as it lists a withdrawn declaration (LOADER-ABI, LOADER-ABI-MODES). The unit reason counts held calls apart and the unit `reason_code` is `awaiting-human-review`, but the per-diagnostic category does not say so. No corpus unit carries one today. DISCHARGE: a dedicated `LegacyDiagnosticKind` for a held call with its own report category, which moves the verdict-bearing artifact's schema and so needs a deliberate re-pin of the archived baseline; the withdrawn-declaration refusals could move with it.

named_followups.title: An inheriting declaration cannot be deferred on its own
named_followups.why: Contract inheritance (C15) admits no clause after `contract inherit PARENT;`, so a child inherits exactly its parent's markers: a deferred parent defers every child, but a child of an undeferred parent can be deferred only by writing its contract out by hand with a marker. DISCHARGE: admit exactly one contract-level review marker after `inherit PARENT` (e.g. `contract inherit PARENT requires resource_review_pending("REASON");`), elaborated as a marker on the inherited contract, with the inherited-declaration agreement check comparing everything but that marker, the C15 and G05a grammar updated, and Lean parity for the propagation rule.

named_followups.title: A `for` header's init and increment clauses are refused, not classified, when stripping their grouping tokens is not faithful
named_followups.why: `split_for_clauses` strips `(`, `)`, `[` and `]` from a `for` header's init and increment clauses (`W4-EXPR-POS-FOR-CLAUSES`, recorded in docs/reports/remaining-w4-expr-pos/README.md and never registered here), so `q_free(p)` in either clause read as the names `q_free p` and lowered to `NoOp`. Card W45-PARENTHESISED-CALLEE (gateway constraint 10c, rule 3) refuses such a clause unless its stripped classification was already a refusal, and keeps the stripped classification only where every group wraps one name (`TAILQ_FOREACH_SAFE`'s `(elm) = (tmpelm)`). On the pinned corpus that refuses 5 clauses in 5 functions already Unknown: 4 `RD_MAP_FOREACH_ELEM` headers whose `rd_map_iter_begin`/`rd_map_iter_next` calls were dropped, and 1 `TAILQ_FOREACH` increment `(e) = ((e)->link.tqe_next)` whose stripped spelling was faithful but whose group wraps a member chain (one `unresolved resource identity` report exchanged). DISCHARGE: classify the two clauses from their original spelling through the ordinary statement classifier, as the condition already is, retire rule 3, and re-pin the corpus with every moved leaf attributed.

named_followups.title: A call through a callee expression that is not a name is refused
named_followups.why: Card W45-PARENTHESISED-CALLEE normalises only `(NAME)(...)` (any depth of parentheses) and refuses every other callee expression: a conditional `(c ? f : g)(x)`, an address `(&f)(x)`, a cast `((T) f)(x)`, a comma `(a, f)(x)`, a call's result `g()(x)` and a subscript `a[i](x)`. None of these replaced an admission in the pinned corpus (0 leaves carry the refusal), so the residual is unsized there. DISCHARGE: model the forms C gives a single designator (`(&f)(x)` is `f(x)`; a cast to a function-pointer type of a function designator calls that function) and desugar a conditional callee into its two branches through the W44-BRANCH-CONDITION-CALLS edges, each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: The rule that every wait in the TSan forcing and binding headers polls quietly (a relaxed atomic, inline, no call and no release per iteration) is enforced by two held rows over today's wait sites, not by a shape check
named_followups.why: Card W45-TSAN-ROWS-LOAD-SENSITIVE (wave 45) found that clang instruments atomics and function entry/exit even in a no_sanitize("thread") function, so a wait loop that takes and releases the forcing header's spinlock on every poll gives ThreadSanitizer a new epoch and fresh trace events per iteration; ~20,000 polls (a partner descheduled ~5 ms) recycled the waiting worker's own history and TSan v3 silently dropped the planted race. The exit barrier and the join-edge-removal stand-in now wait quietly, and a_held_partner_still_has_its_overlap_reported_under_forced_together and a_held_worker_still_has_the_removed_join_edge_reported_under_every_schedule (compiler/tests/task_route_tsan.rs) hold one worker 100 ms so a loud wait at either site fails every run (measured 3 of 3 with the old barrier restored, 2 of 2 with the 50 ms stand-in restored). Nothing checks a NEW wait loop: the_forcing_header_stays_invisible_to_thread_sanitizer lists forbidden primitives and the no_sanitize attribute, and a future loop that calls qcore_forced_lock/unlock per poll passes it and fails only under load or under a hold that reaches it. The same silent drop also bounds the clean rows: a zero there is 'no race reported', so a loud wait could have turned a real race into a clean row under load. DISCHARGE: a shape check over SCHEDULE_FORCING and PTHREAD_BINDING that no sched_yield loop body contains a call or a release-ordered atomic, or a held row per wait site registered with the header; or state permanently with the two held rows named as the guard.

named_followups.title: Scheduler timer retained when a retry request fails to allocate (C1): observed-local on a real build
named_followups.why: W45-FB-RETRY-FAULT-INJECTION reproduced, on fluent-bit 864c3d97 built with Clang, the source-level C1 candidate from fb-system-audit-cards/retry: flb_sched_request_create (src/flb_scheduler.c) links a timer into sched->timers before allocating its request; gdb forcing that allocation to fail (the same null-check branch a real flb_malloc failure takes) leaves the timer linked with a zeroed type and NULL data ('C1: timer 0x7ffff0031060 type=0 data=(nil)') alongside the '[engine] retry ... could not be scheduled' warning, while the control run's teardown walk shows no such entry. The timer is freed inside flb_sched_destroy at teardown, not before and not after -- the Codex report's contrary guard ('not a permanent leak, because teardown reclaims the timer') held. Native observation under an injected premise, NOT an upstream defect or production-leak claim; no Quirin verdict moves. DISCHARGE: the investigation question is discharged observed-local; the semantic card FB-RETRY-LIFETIME is not discharged and C4 (FB-STALE-COMPLETION-REACHABILITY) remains untouched.

named_followups.title: Temporary task user left when a simulated synchronous output fails to enqueue (C2): observed-local, simulation
named_followups.why: W45-FB-RETRY-FAULT-INJECTION reproduced, on fluent-bit 864c3d97, the source-level C2 candidate from fb-system-audit-cards/retry, under a simulated FLB_OUTPUT_SYNCHRONOUS flag forced via gdb on the in-tree retry output (no in-tree plugin sets that flag at this revision, so this is recorded as a simulation, not an observation of any shipped configuration). flb_output_task_singleplex_enqueue (src/flb_output.c) adds a temporary task user before flb_output_task_queue_enqueue; gdb forcing that call's node allocation to fail, in both a first-dispatch and a retry variant, left the temporary user un-decremented ('users=1') and the task un-destroyed through the ordinary path in both variants, visible in the engine's own '(1 pending tasks)' shutdown accounting; each task was destroyed only at grace-period expiry. Control runs in both variants show the same task destroyed with users=0 well before SIGTERM. The Codex report's contrary guard ('input teardown ultimately destroys tasks despite the count, so the bounded consequence is retention until teardown, not a leak') held in both variants. Native observation under an injected premise and a simulated flag; NOT an upstream defect or production claim; no Quirin verdict moves. DISCHARGE: the investigation question is discharged observed-local under the stated simulation; FB-RETRY-LIFETIME is not discharged.

named_followups.title: Zero-user task left mapped after a queued retry's flush fails (C3): observed-local, simulation, single-route setup
named_followups.why: W45-FB-RETRY-FAULT-INJECTION reproduced, on fluent-bit 864c3d97, the source-level C3 candidate from fb-system-audit-cards/retry, under the same simulated FLB_OUTPUT_SYNCHRONOUS flag as the C2 entry. flb_output_task_queue_flush_one (src/flb_output.c) drops a queued task's temporary user before calling flb_output_task_flush; because that call is asynchronous by construction even under the simulated flag (it posts an event and returns 0 immediately), a second task's scheduled retry naturally queued behind the one in flight, giving a genuine queued_task->retry != 0 case with no extra input or raised rate needed. gdb forcing flb_output_task_flush to return -1 at entry (a script fix from the run guide's literal 'step into the call, then return -1', which does not work as scripted because the call site spans multiple source lines -- recorded with the discarded first attempt's log) reproduced a task retained at users=0 with no other route or retry, explicitly named by the engine's own accounting at shutdown ('task_id=0 still running on route(s)'), and destroyed only at grace-period expiry through flb_engine_destroy_tasks / flb_input_instance_destroy (input teardown, del=0) rather than the control's ordinary flb_task_users_release path (del=1). The Codex report names other active routes/retries as a contrary guard; this run deliberately used a single-route setup so that guard does not apply, isolating the candidate, while the teardown-reaps-everything guard held (freed at input-instance destruction, no crash, no use-after-free). Native observation under an injected premise and a simulated flag; NOT an upstream defect or production claim; no Quirin verdict moves. DISCHARGE: the investigation question is discharged observed-local under the stated simulation and single-route setup; FB-RETRY-LIFETIME is not discharged.

named_followups.title: OR-6 (queued_task not used after the flush fails) is not stated: a container element recovered with container_of has no identity, and no summary says a callee frees one
named_followups.why: Card W45-FB-RETRY-LIFETIME stated OR-1 and OR-7 as checked provider contracts but not OR-6. `flb_output_task_queue_flush_one` obtains `queued_task` from `mk_list_entry_first(&queue->pending, ...)`, a container_of expression the gateway reads as an unresolved identity, and the free that would make `queued_task->retry` a use after free happens inside `flb_output_task_singleplex_flush_next` (N3, source reading at 046accf6: unchanged bodies, flb_output.c:312-351 and 392-411). Neither the element identity nor a callee summary that frees the first in-progress element is in the vocabulary. Size: 1 obligation, 2 functions. DISCHARGE: an element-identity rule for `mk_list_entry*` over a published container (coordinated with FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY's iteration mechanism) and a per-arm callee summary stating the element released, with Lean parity, then a contract for OR-6 decided by `quirin-audit`. ADVANCED by W45-CONTAINER-ROOT-REACH (2026-09-26): after its foreign unlink `flb_output_task_queue_flush_one`'s `queued_task` is a tracked identity (it is re-published into `in_progress`, and its read at flb_output.c:339 is refused as a read through a published object), and `flb_output_task_singleplex_flush_next`'s unlink and free of `ended_task` are modelled; but a body with a foreign unlink publishes no summary (W45-FOREIGN-UNLINK-SUMMARY), so no caller learns that flush_next frees the element. OR-6 stays not stated. AMENDED by CG17-LAYOUT-DERIVED-EXTENTS (gateway rule 11u, base b6a3dc42): container_of now has a base/subobject provenance rule, but it names the enclosing object only for a pointer established as `&x->m` of the same body; OR-6's `queued_task = mk_list_entry_first(&queue->pending, ...)` (and flush_next's `ended_task`) is a list lookup over `(H)->next`, refused by that rule as `not-a-member-address` by design: its identity is rule 10f's container premise (P-CRR-MEMBER), unchanged. Re-measured on the system route at b6a3dc42 (unchanged by the card): flb_output_task_queue_flush_one Unknown (counted-user operation on `queued_task->task`, flb_output_task_flush's refuted contract, unresolved `queued_task`, an indirect access, the uncontracted flush_next), flb_output_task_singleplex_flush_next Unknown (the uncontracted flush_one: the pair is mutually recursive). Size unchanged: 1 obligation, 2 functions. The blocker stays W45-FOREIGN-UNLINK-SUMMARY (a summary stating the released element).

named_followups.title: OR-7's -1 clause on flb_output_task_flush is undecided: flb_output_flush_create's body reaches an uncontracted callee
named_followups.why: The counted-user derivation of the header-inline `flb_output_flush_create` stops at `flb_output_flush_id_get` -> `flb_output_thread_instance_get`, which has no contract and no body in the output unit, so every non-threaded path of `flb_output_task_flush` has an undecided count and `resource_user_exit(task, -1, restored)` is undecided (the 0 clause is refuted on the threaded arm regardless). Size: 1 clause. DISCHARGE: a declaration of the user effect (neutral) of the callees the derivation reaches, or the unit that defines them in the selection, then a re-measured clause.

named_followups.title: OR-1's success clause is undecided on the `return flb_output_task_queue_flush_one(...)` exit: the callee's counter operations are on a container element
named_followups.why: `flb_output_task_singleplex_enqueue`'s clause `resource_user_exit(task, 0, added)` holds on the `return 0` exit and is undecided on the exit returning `flb_output_task_queue_flush_one(...)`, whose drop and flush act on `queued_task->task`, not a formal. OR-1 itself (the -1 clause) is decided refuted. Size: 1 clause. DISCHARGE: W45-FB-OR6-ELEMENT-IDENTITY's element identity plus an exit clause for flush_one checked against its body.

named_followups.title: flb_task_users_release and flb_task_users_dec(task, FLB_TRUE) stay uncontracted: a release check may destroy a borrowed formal
named_followups.why: The counted-user vocabulary has `resource_user_dropped_checked` and `resource_user_release_check`, but declaring them for Fluent Bit would let a caller keep using a task the check may have destroyed: no custody mode states 'may release the borrowed object'. The FLB_TRUE call sites therefore stay outside `flb_task_users_dec`'s literal premise (4 leaves in the system slice at 046accf6 read `call to flb_task_users_dec outside its declared literal-argument premise`) and `flb_task_users_release` is undeclared. DISCHARGE: a may-destroy custody mode for a borrowed position with gateway and Lean parity, then the two declarations checked against their header bodies.

named_followups.title: Two counted-user declarations are applied in the output unit as cross-unit premises no analysed body checks there
named_followups.why: `flb_output_thread_pool_flush` (`resource_user_neutral`, body in src/flb_output_thread.c, outside the system selection) is never checked in the slice; `flb_task_retry_destroy` (`resource_released(retry, nonnull)`, `resource_user_neutral`) is checked in src/flb_task.c, where its neutral clause is undecided because `flb_sched_request_invalidate` is uncontracted. OR-7's refutation rests on the first, OR-1's on the second (through the derived neutrality of `flb_output_task_queue_enqueue`). Both bodies were read at 046accf6 and change no user count. DISCHARGE: add flb_output_thread.c to a selection and declare or derive the neutrality of flb_sched_request_invalidate and flb_task_clear_route_retry_context, so both clauses hold where their bodies are analysed. RE-SCOPED by W45-REFUTED-CONTRACT-WITHDRAWAL (2026-09-26, contract spec C06.4, gateway constraint 10g): both declarations are now named in every run's `refuted_contracts` terms as unchecked, not refuted — `flb_task_retry_destroy`'s neutral clause is undecided where its body is analysed and `flb_output_thread_pool_flush` has no analysed body — so they stay applied as declared premises. Their only consumers in the slice are the two refutations (OR-1, OR-7), which are provisional Unsafe candidates on the OR functions' own rows; no Safe rests on either, and every caller of the two OR functions is now held Unknown (`contract-refuted-by-body`). Discharge condition unchanged; the general residual (unchecked declarations of analysed bodies applied as trusted premises) is W45-UNCHECKED-DECLARATIONS-TRUSTED.

named_followups.title: A publication discharges only into a container reached from an unrebound formal or a local initialised from one; the MK-LIST corpus leaves need more
named_followups.why: Gateway constraint 10d refuses a publication into any other container. The 4 corpus leak leaves registered under MK-LIST-ADD-BORROWED-PUBLICATION (mk_rconf_read, mk_vhost_create, mk_vhost_set_property, mk_vhost_set_single) were not withdrawn: in each the linking statement is refused upstream (indirect memory access) or the container lies inside an object the body acquired, which needs an owner/child relation mk_list lacks. DISCHARGE: a nested-container relation (a published child of a body-acquired owner that the owner's own publication carries) with Lean parity, and an arbiter attributing each withdrawn leaf. RE-SCOPED by W45-CONTAINER-ROOT-REACH (2026-09-26): its census of every mk_list_add site (corpus and slice) found no publication refused for its container, so widening container roots reaches none of the 4 functions. mk_rconf_read, mk_vhost_create, mk_vhost_set_property and mk_vhost_set_single publish into formal-chain containers (or, for mk_vhost_create's alias, a body-acquired owner) and are blocked by the entry: an uncontracted mk_string_dup store into the object refuses and poisons its binding before the link. Static containers are now admitted (P-CRR-STATIC, 0 census sites). What stays open here: the owner relation (a publication into a body-acquired owner that is itself published or returned: 8 corpus sites in 5 functions, 3 slice sites in 1 function, none a first blocker) and the entry blockers above. DISCHARGE unchanged for the owner relation; the 4 leaves need the string-duplication contracts first. AMENDED by MONKEY-VHOST-PROPERTY-CUSTODY (gateway rule 12d; main bfbf0d673): the entry blocker named above is gone (`mk_string_dup` is declared, providers/qcore-provider-libevent/contracts/monkey/string.qv), and the owner of a field-linked child is no longer withdrawn when each child is exactly live and unencumbered: rule 12d carries the children into the container and an unlink hands them back. Re-measured with this follow-up's census.py on the AFTER corpus: mk_vhost_set_property's publication (mk_lib.c:499) now carries no leaf (the function stays Unknown on its DocumentRoot branch, MONKEY-DOCUMENTROOT-OVERWRITE-CANDIDATE), mk_rconf_read's (mk_rconf.c:463) none either, and cio_chunk_open's and flb_input_chunk_create's `owns linked objects` refusals are lifted (both stay Unknown on other blockers); mk_vhost_create (mk_lib.c:481) and mk_vhost_set_single (mk_vhost.c:611) now stop at the owner relation itself. The owner relation is unchanged in size: 8 corpus sites in 5 functions (owner-returned 5, owner-published 3: mk_string_split_line, mk_vhost_read, mk_vhost_set_single, mk_vhost_create, mk_server_listen_init) plus 1 owner-local (mk_vhost_fdt_worker_init), each still Unknown; 85 mk_list_add/del sites in all. named_followups.title: Pins are evaluated by quirin-audit's routes and the corpus arbiter only
named_followups.why: `qcore_audit::contract_revision::apply_pins` runs in `quirin-audit current`, `quirin-audit contracts`, the configured `quirin-audit CONFIG.json` route and `quirin-audit pinned`. A caller of the gateway API, the checked extern-call route (`source.extern-call.v1`) and the other compiler examples apply the environment they are given, in which no pin was evaluated, so a pinned contract there is applied as loaded. Contract spec C06.2 states the boundary. DISCHARGE: an inventory of every verdict-publishing route, each either evaluating pins against its audited source or refusing a pinned contract it cannot evaluate, with a test per route.

named_followups.title: Contract locks live in the provider crates' source trees and are not packaged
named_followups.why: Audits load resource contracts through the load path, where each crate's `contracts.lock` sits beside its `Cargo.toml`; `providers/contracts.py check` verifies each lock against the current contract texts (`quirin-audit pin --verify-contracts`). The five executable provider packages carry their contracts unchanged and no lock, because no audit loads resource contracts from an installed package today. DISCHARGE: when an audit route loads resource contracts from an installed package, package the crate's lock with a SHA-256 pin in its inventory, verify it in `providers/package.py verify`, and evaluate pins from it.

named_followups.title: The pinned-source identity is lexical and whole-tree
named_followups.why: `crates/qcore-audit/src/c_identity.rs` reads every `.c` and `.h` blob of the audited HEAD and records every top-level declaration and definition of a pinned name, without preprocessing. Any textual change to any such site, including a renamed local, a moved prototype or a new declaration in an unrelated file, puts the contract out of force (the fail-closed direction), and a conditional group that closes an outer brace makes every body in its file run to the end of the file. A site the scanner does not recognise as top-level (a definition produced by a macro, say) is not part of the identity. DISCHARGE: an identity bound to the preprocessed definitions the audit's own units see, with a measured comparison on the Fluent Bit corpus of false mismatches and of missed sites against this scanner.

named_followups.title: A call held for a pin mismatch is counted as a recorded refusal and listed under the diagnostic category `unsupported`
named_followups.why: As for a pending review (W45-REVIEW-HELD-CALL-SITE-COUNT, W45-REVIEW-HELD-DIAGNOSTIC-CATEGORY), the `contract_revision` section's held counts are recorded held-call refusals, a lower bound on textual call sites, and `diagnostics.json` lists a held call under `category: unsupported`; the unit `reason_code` is `contract-pin-mismatch`. DISCHARGE: discharged together with those two residuals, the pin hold counted and categorised by the same mechanism.

named_followups.title: `quirin-audit compare` does not report a pinned contract moving between reviewed identities
named_followups.why: Since the integration review of W45-CONTRACT-REVISION-MODE a pinned lock entry holds several reviewed identities, and each run's `contract_revision` section records the one a contract in force matched (`matched_reviewed_at`). `quirin-audit compare` compares contracts by mode, status and text digest only, so a contract in force at both runs through different identities (`ctr_destroy` in the pilot, through the 66910c10 identity at 864c3d97 and the 046accf6 identity at 046accf6) is not listed as changed. DISCHARGE: `compare` lists each contract in force whose matched identity differs between the runs, with both identities' revisions, and a test pins it on a two-revision fixture.

named_followups.title: Backlog OB-2/OB-3 need a wrapper-to-chunk reference relation, return-conditioned clauses and per-element identity; v1 states none
named_followups.why: W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY expressed the storage-backlog obligations as checked specifications (providers/quirin-provider-fluent-bit/contracts/fluent_bit/storage_backlog.qcore, contract spec C06.3). OB-2 (no chunk closed while a wrapper refers to it; the -3 arm of sb_append_chunk_to_segregated_backlogs, observed natively as the partial fan-out ASan use-after-free) and OB-3 (at most one wrapper per chunk per queue) relate a wrapper, a queue and a chunk; the v1 vocabulary states only argument and result custody. Measured reach of a relation clause alone in this slice is 0: the chunk is an element of stream->chunks (sb_segregate_chunks) or of a wrapper (cb_queue_chunks), both untracked by the projection, and the failing insertion is inside a loop whose callee has no return-conditioned summary. DISCHARGE: a C09 relation clause (wrapper refers to chunk; close requires no outstanding reference), a return-conditioned clause, and per-element abstract identities for admitted list iterations, with loader, gateway and Lean parity, then the slice as arbiter deciding OB-2 on the -3 arm; any refutation stays a provisional Unsafe, never an upstream defect claim. AMENDED (CG24-ALIAS-EXTENT-FRAME-VOCABULARY, wave 48 round 11, gateway rule 11e): the card's derived relations are bounds relations of a result to its argument bases (bounds_return_derived, multi-base), not the custody relation this entry needs (wrapper refers to chunk; close requires no outstanding reference), and it adds no return-conditioned clause or per-element identity. Re-measured on base 6cab1ad9: the storage-backlog declarations' leaves sit in 7 non-Safe system-route functions (17 leaves: the five sb.c bodies whose declared specification is not established, flb_engine_start and flb_input_chunk_release_space_compound), none of them as the only obstacle; 1 corpus leaf, not sole; 0 on the tail-pause slice. The reach of a relation clause alone stays 0. The DISCHARGE stands.

named_followups.title: flb_input_chunk_map's chunk has three dispositions (stored, closed on the routes_mask arm, left open); no v1 mode is faithful, so OB-4/OB-5 stay Unknown
named_followups.why: W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY left flb_input_chunk_map undeclared: on success the chunk is stored into the returned input chunk, on the routes_mask allocation failure it is closed (BC-1), and on the other NULL arms it is left open. OB-5 (chunk closed exactly once on a NULL map return; cb_queue_chunks closes it again) and OB-4 are therefore not decidable; BC-1 remains a source-reading candidate. Unchanged between 864c3d97 and 046accf6. DISCHARGE: a per-arm (or per-return) disposition clause in C09 with loader/gateway/Lean parity, or a source argument; then the backlog slice deciding OB-5. AMENDED (CG23-RELATIONAL-POSTCONDITIONS, gateway rule 11r): re-read on the prepared source (src/flb_input_chunk.c), flb_input_chunk_map returns NULL on four arms and closes the chunk on one of them (the routes_mask allocation failure, :1512-1516). No return-code class separates the arms, since every failure arm returns the same NULL, and a disposition over a pointer result is not in the vocabulary (C04.13 admits signed integer results only). The function's own corpus row is Unknown (50 unsupported, 41 unknown_alias leaves). The entry stays open: it needs a per-arm source argument or a caller-side relation, not a return-code disposition. System route at main b6a3dc42: flb_input_chunk_map 1 call leaf in 1 function; cb_queue_chunks Unknown (20 unsupported, 12 unknown_alias).

named_followups.title: Backlog OB-6/OB-7/OB-10: callees release objects reachable from their arguments (wrappers of a queue); v1 Borrowed states nothing about them
named_followups.why: sb_remove_chunk_from_segregated_backlogs, sb_destroy_backlog(s) and sb_release_output_queue_space free wrappers (and queues) reached through a borrowed context; their checked specifications (all Borrowed) are not established by the bodies, whose element releases refuse as unresolved identities. OB-6 (no wrapper used after a callee frees it), OB-7 (eviction retires every wrapper before the close) and OB-10 (teardown) need a clause for objects released through what an argument reaches (P-B08-SHALLOW is the current premise). DISCHARGE: such a clause with parity, or a container-ownership relation for list elements, then the slice as arbiter. FB-TEARDOWN-DESTROY-DECLARATIONS (2026-10-16) leaves six teardown functions of the same class undeclared: flb_task_retry_clean (a retry of task->retries), flb_sched_request_invalidate (a request of the scheduler's lists), flb_output_exit and flb_input_exit_all (every instance of config's lists), flb_engine_destroy_tasks (every task of a list) and flb_tail_file_remove_all (every file of ctx's lists): declaring them resource_borrowed would hide the release of an object a caller may still track (system 16 and slice 4 uncontracted leaves at 8b360766c).

named_followups.title: Backlog OB-9 needs ChunkIO return-code summaries (cio_chunk_up_force CIO_OK/CIO_ERROR/CIO_CORRUPTED/CIO_RETRY) and the uncontracted cio_chunk_lock/cio_error_get/cio_chunk_get_real_size
named_followups.why: sb_segregate_chunks' end states per chunk (OB-9) depend on ChunkIO return codes; cio_chunk_lock, cio_error_get and cio_chunk_get_real_size are uncontracted in the slice. Facts belong in qcore-provider-chunkio. DISCHARGE: ChunkIO declarations read against their bodies (in qcore-provider-chunkio) and a return-code-conditioned vocabulary, then the slice deciding OB-9.

named_followups.title: Backlog OB-1 (a wrapper is linked into exactly one queue): the link is now modeled (rule 10d), the leg fails on the byte counter's indirect access and no clause states 'exactly one queue'
named_followups.why: Before the merge of W45-FB-RETRY-LIFETIME, sb_append_chunk_to_segregated_backlog was provisional Unsafe on the unmodeled mk_list_add publication (MK-LIST-ADD-BORROWED-PUBLICATION). On the merged tree rule 10d models the link and withdraws that leak; the function's checked specification (all Borrowed) is still not established, on one indirect access: the saturation test reads backlog->ins->fs_backlog_chunks_size (OB-8, FB-BACKLOG-ACCOUNTING). OB-1's uniqueness half ('exactly one queue') is stated by no clause. DISCHARGE: the counter's read admitted (typed chain through a borrowed formal) and a membership-uniqueness clause, then the slice as arbiter for OB-1.

named_followups.title: Intrusive-list iteration (gateway 5l) rests on stated premises; 43 element and 34 header leaves stay refused
named_followups.why: Gateway constraint 5l admits mk_list/cfl_list headers and container_of element reads under four premises stated, not proved: P-ILI-BODY (checked lexically), P-ILI-UNTRACKED (an element is not an identity the body tracks; the lexical guard declines a function where one call receives both &X->... of a possibly tracked X and the iterated head; linking through a wrapper call is P-B08-SHALLOW), P-ILI-CALLEE-FRAME (a callee handed the container does not unlink the protected node; OB-7 depends on it) and P-ILI-BRACED. Rule 4 added no refusal in the corpus or the slice (17 plain bodies with an unlink or release call; the two read release another object or unlink a second link; 15 not read individually). After the card, 43 element-read braced leaves and 34 list-header for-loop leaves remain in the corpus (from 326 and 269), declined by the guard, an untyped head chain or an unbraced body. DISCHARGE: per premise, a model of the callee frame or a measured guard refinement with its re-pin; per residual leaf class, an admission with its own measurement.

named_followups.title: mk_http_error: descriptor from open() on the custom-error-page arm is never closed (provisional Unsafe candidate)
named_followups.why: W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY's declaration reader exposes, in lib/monkey/mk_server/mk_http.c (pinned corpus), a leak of the descriptor fd opened at :1301 and neither closed nor stored before the return at :1315 on the custom-error-page arm; the source's own comment reads 'This fd seems to be leaked'. It is the card's one added leak after its refused-call hand-on repair; unit mk_server/mk_http.c moves Unknown -> provisional Unsafe. Not an upstream defect claim. DISCHARGE: a native observation with a control on a bound build, or a refuting source argument.

named_followups.title: No trusted-core certificate checker exists for a user-contract checker plugin's Safe claim
named_followups.why: The firewall counts a plugin's `Safe` only with a certificate the registry issues from a trusted-core `WitnessChecker` replay. `quirin-audit` registers none for the `quirin.user-contract-check.v1` task, so every plugin `Safe` it sees is `Pending` (`plugin-claim-uncertified`, QP008 or QP016); the certified row is exercised only through the library route with a test double of a checker. DISCHARGE: a versioned trusted-core checker for a precisely scoped user-contract claim, with independently replayable evidence, positive, negative and mutation tests, and the command line registering it.

named_followups.title: No trusted-core counterexample checker exists, so no plugin Unsafe is validated
named_followups.why: `qcore_verifier_host::plugin_firewall::CounterexampleChecker` is the hook a plugin's `Unsafe` needs; no production implementation exists and `quirin-audit` passes none, so every plugin `Unsafe` is `Pending`. The validated row is exercised only at the host with a test double. DISCHARGE: a trusted-core counterexample checker for a named capability, validating a witness against the core's obligation inventory, with mutation tests, and a report stating how a validated plugin `Unsafe` is presented (provisional, never an upstream defect).

named_followups.title: Checker plugins and user load paths reach `quirin-audit current` and `contracts` only
named_followups.why: `user_plugins::run` is hooked into `CurrentAudit::with_contracts` and `NoBuildAudit::with_plugin_checkers`. The configured `quirin-audit CONFIG.json` route and the corpus arbiter (`quirin-audit pinned`) select contracts by manifest and never read a user load path, so a checker binding cannot reach them; a caller of the gateway API applies the environment it is given. DISCHARGE: an inventory of the verdict-publishing routes, each running the bindings of the load path it resolves or refusing one it cannot, with a test per route.

named_followups.title: The callee chain reads applied contracts from the control-flow graph's contract calls
named_followups.why: `user_plugins::fold_unit` joins a bound contract's verdict into every function whose CFG holds a `LegacyInstruction::ContractCall` (or an admitted nested call) of it. Six call shapes (assignment, initialisation, return, condition, discarded cast, expression operand) were probed to lower to `ContractCall`; a contracted call applied through any other instruction would not carry its link, and a refused call applies no contract and already leaves its function `Unknown`. DISCHARGE: the gateway records the contracts each function applied as part of its summary (or a census proving every applied contract is a `ContractCall`), with a test per lowering route.

named_followups.title: A checker plugin's task borrows `parameter_mode_respected` for a whole-contract claim
named_followups.why: The core-derived task for a binding has one obligation per bound function with property `parameter_mode_respected`, the closest existing `ObligationProperty`; what a user's checker actually checks is not in the closed vocabulary, so the claim's scope is the contract as a whole rather than a named property. DISCHARGE: a dedicated obligation property (a schema change) naming the checked claim, carried into the task digest, with the firewall and the report unchanged otherwise.

named_followups.title: Checker packages run under the host's default execution profile
named_followups.why: A binding names a package, and `ProcessProvider::from_package` runs it under the default profile (`unenforced-legacy`: process-group containment, deadline and output bound, no declared rlimits or confinement); the sidecar records the profile and limits. A user load path cannot yet request `linux-rlimit-v1` or `linux-confined-v1`. DISCHARGE: a binding field selecting the profile (and a confinement policy), refusing one the host cannot enforce, with the refusal tested.

named_followups.title: `quirin-audit contracts` and `quirin-audit CONFIG.json` take no `--checkpoint-dir`
named_followups.why: Only the `current` route is checkpointed; the no-build contracts route (`no_build.rs`) and the configured route (`run_config_with_jobs` in `lib.rs`) fold their units whole, so their peak memory is still the whole corpus's. Both files were being edited by W45-CONTRACT-REVISION-MODE when the card ran, so the hooks were deferred. DISCHARGE: the same group-by-group sealing, resume and composition on both routes, each with a byte-identity test against its whole run.

named_followups.title: Checkpoints record the certificate binding outcome, not certificate bodies or callee summaries
named_followups.why: The `certificates` section is derived from the published rows (a Safe resting on a certificate bound to the compile-task identity, a refused binding, or none). The certificate itself (`LegacySafetyCertificate`) and the gateway's interprocedural callee summaries are not serde types, and the current route publishes neither, so no checkpoint carries them and the per-function summary step is the published function row. Nothing composed depends on them. DISCHARGE: serializable certificate and summary types, a checkpoint section for each (schema version 2), and decomposition covering them.

named_followups.title: Checkpoints bound the retained results, not the working set: inside a group, memory scales with `--jobs`
named_followups.why: A checkpointed run holds one group's results, but that group's units run `--jobs` at a time, each holding its own analysis and Clang output. On the 185-unit corpus, after the pin evaluation's source read was made to stream (it had held the checkout's 85 MiB of C twice and set a 182 MiB setup peak), the checkpointed peak RSS is 111, 331 and 872 MiB at 1, 4 and 16 jobs against the whole run's 172, 392 and 928; at every job count the peak is librdkafka's group (report, Memory). W45-MEMO-MEMORY removed the member-release memo, whose full-text key W45-GATEWAY-MEMO-KEY had made every worker thread hold: on the arbiter the peak is 153, 349 and 848 MiB at 1, 4 and 16 jobs against main's 154, 426 and 1,091, and the checkpointed run at 16 jobs is 879 against 1,108 MiB (docs/reports/w45-memo-memory/README.md §3). The scaling with `--jobs` remains. The only control inside a group is `--jobs`. DISCHARGE: a memory-aware admission of units in flight (a resident-set budget or a per-unit weight bound) measured on the corpus, or a recorded decision that `--jobs` is the control.

named_followups.title: The resume fingerprint repeats the preparation of `CurrentAudit::evaluate_entry` in a second function
named_followups.why: `checkpoint_run::fingerprint_task` recomputes a unit's compile configuration and preparation facts without analysing it, by repeating the preparation steps of `current.rs`'s `evaluate_entry_into` (left untouched because W45-CONTRACT-REVISION-MODE was editing it). A divergence can only disable reuse, never reuse a wrong result, because the analyzer binary digest is in the identity and the fingerprints are compared whole; the fixture and corpus runs show reuse working end to end. A group recomputed under `--resume` also prepares its units twice. DISCHARGE: one shared preparation function used by both paths, the prepared unit passed on to the analysis, and a test comparing the two fingerprints on prepared, refused and absent units.

named_followups.title: A checkpointed run has one group in flight, so a group's longest unit idles the other jobs
named_followups.why: The checkpointed `current` run analyses one group at a time to bound memory; every group ends when its longest unit ends, while the whole run overlaps groups. On the 185-unit corpus it cost nothing at 16 jobs (115.8 s against 130.8 s whole, a noisy host) or 1 job, but doubled the wall time at 4 jobs (288.1 s against 141.7 s), where librdkafka's group alone took 230 s. DISCHARGE: an explicit bound of groups in flight (for example `--max-groups-in-flight M`, M groups analysed concurrently, each sealed and dropped in plan order), measured for wall time and peak memory at 1, 4 and 16 jobs.

named_followups.title: Rule 10d refuses mk_list_del of a formal's own object whose container is unnamed
named_followups.why: Card W45-CONTAINER-ROOT-REACH admits the foreign unlink only for an element reached through a container this body names and may modify (U1). A destructor that unlinks and releases the object its caller passed (`cio_chunk_close`, `flb_input_chunk_destroy`, `flb_task_retry_destroy`, `flb_sched_request_destroy`, ...) names no container, and the caller may hold that object published, as an untracked element or as its own custody; a `Released` summary would accuse a caller that published it (release after escape) although the callee unlinked it first. Size: corpus 12 sites in 11 functions (9 rule-10d leaves, 3 behind a refused call), slice 10 sites in 9 functions (8 rule-10d leaves). DISCHARGE: a summary vocabulary stating 'unlinks, then releases, its argument' that a caller applies to a published object as an unlink followed by a release, with Lean parity and the arbiter.

named_followups.title: A body with an admitted foreign unlink publishes no summary and establishes no specification
named_followups.why: Gateway constraint 10d rule 6 withholds every summary of a body that takes custody of an element of a container its caller supplied: a caller holding the container would otherwise read `Borrowed` (or `Released`) for it and keep restoring its own published objects that the callee released (QCore.ContainerRootReach.the_borrowed_summary_would_hide_a_double_release). Its measured cost: `flb_task_queue_destroy` (slice) keeps one leaf, the unresolved identity of the `queue` it frees, which W4 would otherwise discharge as `Released(queue)`; `flb_output_task_singleplex_flush_next` has no summary for OR-6. DISCHARGE: a summary clause stating that the call may release what a formal's containers hold, applied at callers by dropping every published site reachable through that argument (the published set loses them; a later unlink refuses), with Lean parity.

named_followups.title: Foreign unlinks rule 6 still refuses, and the member uses of a foreign element
named_followups.why: Measured after W45-CONTAINER-ROOT-REACH: (1) an element of a container a callee returned, Monkey's thread-local lists (`mk_server_listen_free`, `mk_vhost_fdt_worker_exit`: 2 corpus leaves); (2) an element name also written another way (`mk_vhost_destroy`'s `halias = NULL`: 1 corpus leaf); (3) an element name bound over a local list as well as a formal's (`schedule_request_promote`: 3 slice leaves, one on the local list itself); (4) an embedded array element (`header_lookup`'s `&p->headers[i]`: 1 corpus leaf); (5) a static head, which rule 5l does not read (0 census sites); (6) after an admitted foreign unlink the element is a tracked identity whose pointer members this body never linked, so a member release or null test of it (`mk_mem_free(file->path)`, `if (ep->file)`, `queued_task->retry`) refuses and poisons the element before its own release: in 8 corpus functions (10 elements) and 2 slice functions the element's release or read keeps an unresolved identity (a third slice function, `sb_destroy_backlogs`, hands its element to the uncontracted `sb_destroy_backlog` first). DISCHARGE: per part, a root premise for a callee's container (a declared static-duration return), an element-binding reader over initialised names, a container-of reader for embedded elements, rule 5l's static heads, and a member-custody premise for an element's unlinked members (the P-B08-SHALLOW analogue), each with Lean parity and the arbiter.

named_followups.title: Declared container clauses are never checked against a body, so they can be unchecked but never refuted
named_followups.why: C06.4 withdraws a declaration its own body refutes, and the two refutation arms are a refuted counted-user clause and a contradicted custody duty. `resource_published`/`resource_unpublished` (C04.8) are applied at calls only: no pass checks a declared container clause against the body it names, and W4's conflict check compares the custody projection only. Size: 2 declarations (`mk_list_add`, `mk_list_del` in `providers/qcore-provider-libevent/contracts/monkey/intrusive_list.qcore`), whose `static inline` bodies every including unit defines. DISCHARGE: a per-path check of a defined body against its declared publication and unlink (the object linked into the named container on every exit, or unlinked), feeding a third refutation arm, with Lean parity and a measured corpus and slice.

named_followups.title: A declaration its analysed body neither establishes nor refutes is still applied as a trusted premise
named_followups.why: C06.4 withdraws only refuted declarations; an unchecked one (an undecided clause, a body that does not validate) keeps constraint 4's and 8's trusted reading, deliberately: making `resource_body_checked` the default would withdraw every cross-unit application and, on the pinned corpus, at least 22 of the 24 declarations with an analysed main-source body, on no evidence (`docs/reports/w45-refuted-contract-withdrawal/artifacts/body-checked-default-census.json`). In the Fluent Bit slice the unchecked premises include `flb_task_retry_destroy` (neutral clause undecided in `src/flb_task.c`) and `flb_output_thread_pool_flush` (no analysed body). Size: 22 corpus declarations (lower bound). DISCHARGE: per declaration, either its body establishes it (validated W4 summary equal to it, every clause held) or it moves behind `resource_body_checked`; or a report status that names every Safe resting on an unchecked declaration of an audited body. AMENDED (W45-SR5-SOUNDNESS): inside the defining unit a declared resource_user_neutral() is no longer applied unverified: call_effect verifies it against the body (DECLARED-NEUTRAL-UNVERIFIED-AT-CALL, discharged); the slice at 046accf6 is leaf-identical. Open as before: every cross-unit application, and every other unchecked declaration.

named_followups.title: A unit whose only open leaves are refuted-contract holds is classed unsupported-syntax at unit level
named_followups.why: The held call's statement classifies as `stale-evidence` (`ReasonCategory::classify`, rule added by W45-REFUTED-CONTRACT-WITHDRAWAL), but the unit reason is the projection summary, which counts the hold among `unsupported`, as it already counts constraint 8's mode withdrawal; review and pin holds have their own summary components. Size: 0 units in the pinned corpus and the Fluent Bit slice (every unit with a hold has other refusals). DISCHARGE: a summary component for refuted and mode-withdrawn holds, classed ahead of the source categories, with the reason-code corpus and the L21.1 table updated.

named_followups.title: Production and validation readers that tests exercise on the real tree read the working tree, not the tracked files
named_followups.why: W45-TEST-HYGIENE (validation constraint 29) moved every test-side repository walk to tracked files; the readers the tests call still read the directory. An untracked or ignored module in a contract root makes `qcore_contract::load_path_manifest::qcore_files` refuse the load path (QI014), failing 21 tests in five compiler test binaries after the card as before it (`docs/reports/w45-test-hygiene/README.md`, set B). Size: 9 readers: `load_path_manifest` `qcore_files`; `compiler/src/first_party.rs` profile discovery; `scripts/contract_corpus.py`'s default walk as `build_matrix.py` uses it; `build_matrix.py`'s `proof/Audit*.lean` and provider-template globs; `scripts/reconciliation_sweep.py`'s report, rule and increment scans; `scripts/build_docs_index.py`; `scripts/check_lean_audits.py`'s `Audit*.lean` glob; `providers/contracts.py`; `providers/package.py`'s template glob and contract copy. The two loaders read an installed tree by design and refuse fail-closed; the repository generators can publish an untracked file's contribution. DISCHARGE: per reader, either it reads tracked files when run on a repository checkout (the generators and package build), or a recorded decision that it reads its directory by design with its fail-closed behaviour stated (the loaders).

named_followups.title: Checked counted-loop measure for the engine slice (the FB-ENGINE-PROGRESS implementation card)
named_followups.why: The census (docs/reports/w45-fb-engine-progress/census/census.json) finds 29 of 121 slice loops whose bound is a local counted-loop shape (3 against a constant, 11 against an unwritten local/parameter/field, 10 against a uint16_t count, 1 right-shift, 4 do-while(0)), 87 whose bound is a list length that needs a list-finiteness contract premise, and 4 with no measure. W45-FB-ENGINE-PROGRESS cut no implementation: a measure is a new analyzer rule with a Lean theorem, and the card was measurement-first. DISCHARGE: Property: for a `for` loop whose counter is a local integer set to c0 in the init clause, tested `counter < B` where B is a literal or macro constant, a local or formal not assigned or address-taken in the loop, or a uint16_t value, advanced by exactly one `counter++` per iteration and not otherwise written or address-taken in the body, the checker records the bound B - c0 as a checked measure (Rust rule plus a registered Lean theorem that the measure is non-negative and strictly decreases). It records a bound fact beside the resource verdict and moves no verdict; no progress verdict. Slice: src/flb_engine.c handle_output_events (:909, accepted, <= FLB_ENGINE_OUTPUT_EVENT_BATCH_SIZE = 1), src/flb_input_chunk.c flb_input_chunk_get_direct_routes (:2286, accepted, <= 65535), src/flb_task.c flb_task_create (:652, accepted, <= 65535). Refusing controls, each Unknown: plugins/in_storage_backlog/sb.c cb_queue_chunks (:611, no counter), src/flb_scheduler.c ipow (:237, without an exp >= 0 precondition), random_uniform (:106). Corpus byte-identical unless attributed.

named_followups.title: One transient fstat failure leaves the backlog collector without yielding: observed-local at 046accf6
named_followups.why: E2: on an unmodified Debug build at 046accf6, gdb made ONE collector-originated cio_file_update_size (lib/chunkio/src/cio_file.c:853) take its failure arm (fs_size = 0, CIO_ERROR). _cio_file_up returns CIO_ERROR there without closing the descriptor it just opened (cio_file.c:853-856), so every later cio_chunk_up_force of that chunk failed at 'file descriptor already exists' (cio_file.c:827-830; 11,999 such log lines), and cb_queue_chunks (sb.c:611-722) entered once and did not return across 12,000 observations (6.8 s, 0 flush-timer dispatches). Control C2 (one transient open failure, which leaves no descriptor) queued all 13 chunks and yielded 10 of 10 passes. Injected-premise native observation, NOT an upstream defect or production-hang claim; no Quirin verdict moves. DISCHARGE: The investigation question is discharged observed-local. A production-relevant claim needs an unforced trigger (a real fstat failure on an open chunk descriptor, or the mmap-failure arm, see W45-FB-CIO-MAP-FAILED-STATE) on a pinned build; the semantic bound is W45-FB-ENGINE-PROGRESS-MEASURE's refusing control and stays Unknown.

named_followups.title: A retry whose chunk cannot be brought up is rescheduled without spending an attempt: observed-local
named_followups.why: E3: gdb set the result of flb_input_chunk_set_up to -1 in flb_engine_dispatch_retry (src/flb_engine_dispatch.c:114-115) on every retry dispatch (the value cio_chunk_up returns at storage.max_chunks_up, cio_file.c:837-841). With retry_limit 3 the retry was dispatched 12 times in 26 s with attempts = 1 throughout, 11 reschedules and no drop; the callback returned each time. Control C3 (no fault) spent attempts 1, 2, 3 and dropped the chunk ('cannot be retried') 5 s after the first retry. Cross-invocation revisit under an injected persistent premise, NOT an upstream defect claim; the source comment (flb_engine_dispatch.c:116-123) states the reschedule is intended. DISCHARGE: Observation discharged observed-local. A progress claim needs a stated release premise (up slots eventually free) or a checked policy; no verdict moves.

named_followups.title: Ring-buffer collector drain has no per-call batch limit (census EP-L047, unresolved)
named_followups.why: flb_input_chunk_ring_buffer_collector's inner `while (1)` (src/flb_input_chunk.c:3746-3780) runs on the engine thread and exits only when the ring buffer is empty or the input pauses; threaded inputs write the ring buffer concurrently. Under PR (no concurrent producer) it is bounded by the ring buffer's capacity; without it no bound holds. Not exercised natively. DISCHARGE: A native run with a threaded input producing at or above the drain rate, recording the drain's iterations per call and engine flush dispatches, with a quiescent-producer control; or a reading that establishes a producer-side bound.

named_followups.title: random_uniform's rejection loop needs 1 <= range <= RAND_MAX (census EP-L096, unresolved)
