named_followups.title: No trusted-core checker accepts a quirin-audit subcommand plugin's certificate or witness
named_followups.why: Card W45-AUDIT-SUBCOMMAND-PLUGINS classifies every subcommand verdict claim with the checker-plugin firewall (`qcore_audit::subcommand_plugins::classify_claim`). A claim's `certificates` are references only: no verification task binds them and no `WitnessChecker` or `CounterexampleChecker` reads them, so every `Safe` claim is `Pending` (QP008 without references, QP016 with them) and every `Unsafe` claim `Pending` (QP010); the certified and validated rows are unreachable on this route (0 claims from the shipped plugins today: the libevent plugin claims nothing). Related to, and not discharged by, W45-PLUGIN-CERTIFICATE-CHECKER, whose task is the user-contract checker's. DISCHARGE: a versioned trusted-core checker for a precisely scoped subcommand claim (a task derived from the claim tuple, evidence bound to the plugin's SHA-256 and the request digest), wired so a certified claim is `Safe` only through a registry-issued `CoreCertificate`, with a test that an unbound or refuted certificate stays `Unknown` and the Lean model's `accepted` case reached.

named_followups.title: An external quirin-audit subcommand is contained by process group and working directory, not sandboxed
named_followups.why: The host runs `quirin-audit-NAME` in its own process group with its output as working directory, kills the group on a quota breach and at the end of the run, and accepts only artifacts inside the output with their declared SHA-256. Nothing stops the plugin writing elsewhere (the libevent plugin refuses protected outputs itself, but that is the plugin's check, not the host's), and a descendant that calls `setsid` leaves the group and escapes the kill; the host then reports `plugin-escaped-descendant` only if the descendant still holds standard output. The verifier host's `linux-confined-v1` profile (Landlock filesystem rules, a cgroup process quota) is not applied here. DISCHARGE: run subcommand plugins under the verifier host's confining profile (writes limited to the output, reads declared), with tests that a write outside the output and an escaping descendant are refused or killed; or record the measured boundary in contract spec C11.2 as the decided scope.

named_followups.title: External quirin-audit subcommands refuse to run on a non-Unix host
named_followups.why: The quota kill is a process-group kill (`kill(-pgid)`, with `waitid(WNOWAIT)` on Linux so the group ID stays reserved while the rest of the group is killed), so on a host without `std::os::unix` the route reports `plugin-spawn` (`Unknown`) and runs nothing; the integration tests are `#![cfg(unix)]`. The libevent plugin is Unix-only in practice anyway (CMake with make). DISCHARGE: a Windows job object with kill-on-close and the same quotas, with the integration tests run on Windows CI; or a decision that subcommand plugins are Unix-only, recorded in contract spec C11.2.

named_followups.title: Host verdicts a subcommand run joins are read from `--audit-report` as given

named_followups.title: The typed-position join withdraws Safe functions through AST closure classes that rules 5l and 5i read as unbound
named_followups.why: Rule 10o serves, at every P2 statement and P3 position of a function the lexical reader reads, the join of the extended lexical closure and the rule-10l AST closure. After rule 10o the lexical closure reads every nested, for-clause, later-declarator, parenthesised and brace-initialiser assignment (the re-emitted disputed set, docs/reports/w47-lexical-closure-nested-assignment/artifacts/after/disputed-corpus.json, has no root of those classes left that the AST binds and the lexical closure does not), so what the join still adds are AST classes the lexical closure reads under established rules: a statement-expression value (rule 5l's container_of element: 127 admitted-row roots in 32 corpus function records, 498 in the system slice), a sub-object store whose root is the admitted store's own (rule 5i; including file-scope objects), and a static array initialiser counted by the AST's may_bind. Measured withdrawals (Safe -> Unknown, none an unsound Safe): corpus mk_fifo_queue_get (q), mk_plugin_cap (plugin), rd_kafka_Uuid_str (bytes), unit_test_telemetry_decoded_int64 (unit_test_data); system flb_engine_get_chunk_backpressure_percent (ins), sb_find_segregated_backlog_by_output_plugin_instance (backlog); plus summary cascades from the static inline flb_task_get_route_data/_status/set_route_status/set_route_data bodies. DISCHARGE: the AST closure reads rule 5l's admitted container_of element and rule 5i's admitted scalar or never-bound sub-object store as the lexical rules do (or the join is narrowed to the binding classes the lexical closure models, with a stated argument), with matching audited Lean, negative controls (a statement expression holding a custody call, a sub-object store of a tracked value) and a measured re-pin restoring the six without flipping any other row. AMENDED (round-2b integration, 2026-09-28): merging W47-ACCESS-PATH-POSITION-RESIDUALS (rule 10n) onto rule 10o adds an address class: an address taken of a root (`&global_queue.items` at a Borrowed head, the pinned control in container_root_reach.rs) counts as a possible binding, so 10n's typed address fallback refuses it; in the corpus the card's twelfth gain, rd_kafka_toppar_needs_query, stays Unknown, and 33 Unknown functions keep refusals the card alone removed (37 indirect-access, 7 for-condition, 2 branch-condition leaves; docs/reports/w47-access-path-position-residuals/integration/). Restoring them needs the address-of-a-non-pointer-member case shown not to bind the root. NOTE by CG10-BOUND-UNTRACKED-ROOTS (gateway rule 11d): four of the six withdrawn functions are Safe again through the separate per-path premise, not through the AST closure (unchanged): corpus mk_fifo_queue_get (q) and mk_plugin_cap (plugin), system flb_engine_get_chunk_backpressure_percent (ins) and sb_find_segregated_backlog_by_output_plugin_instance (backlog); the flb_task_get_route_data/_status/set_route_status/set_route_data bodies' `*out` stores are admitted too, so their summary cascades return (flb_input_chunk_drop_task_route Safe on the corpus and the system route). rd_kafka_Uuid_str and unit_test_telemetry_decoded_int64 stay Unknown. The DISCHARGE (the AST closure reading rules 5l and 5i's classes) stands.

named_followups.title: Derive who resumes an input coroutine after it yields
named_followups.why: W47-LOOP-OWNER-COROUTINE-HOP derives an input coroutine's initial resumers (each loop dispatcher that constructs it with flb_input_coro_collect and resumes the returned handle; include/fluent-bit/flb_input.h::input_pre_cb_collect now runs on flb_lib_worker non-threaded and input_thread threaded, with no unresolved path), but not who resumes a body after a non-terminal yield: the continuation runs on whichever thread handles the event the body registered before yielding (flb_coro_resume(connection->coroutine) at src/flb_engine.c:1609, src/flb_input_thread.c:470, src/flb_output_thread.c:336, src/flb_downstream_worker.c:223; flb_time_sleep's timer at include/fluent-bit/flb_time_utils.h:33), a handle taken from flb_coro_get(). The census therefore leaves every coroutine body that may reach a yield unresolved. named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-C-STRUCT-IMPORT: a member whose C type has no §G02t equivalent — a nested struct, an array, a pointer, an enum, a `char`, a `long long` on LP64 — may stay unlisted as opaque bytes but refuses at `Q063` when listed. named_followups.title: The header read at check time and the one built against are bound by static assertions, not by the digest
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-C-STRUCT-IMPORT: the certificate names the header's SHA-256 and its resolved absolute path and directory (so it is host-specific), and the emitted C re-asserts the size, each listed offset and each listed type; a header edited after checking in a way that keeps every listed member's type and offset and the size still builds, though its digest differs. named_followups.title: A record holding an owned `bytes` field does not cross a `.qr` call
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS: records of scalars cross calls by value on `source.scalar-calls.v1`, which has no buffer vocabulary, and the buffer route that owns records with `bytes` fields models its entry only; a record type holding `bytes` anywhere refuses on the scalar-calls route by name (`Q020`), and a module with a buffer and a second function stays on the buffer route's entry-only refusal (`Q051`). `source.resource-calls.v1` has `own<bytes>`/`borrow<bytes>`/`lend<bytes>` but its own byte representation (`qcore_bytes { data, len }`) and no record events. Amended by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES moves a record that owns across a spawn and a `join` on the scoped-task route as its leaves (the ledger's per-leaf custody, a record result carried as one completion outcome and unpacked into leaf slots); the representation would carry over to a `.qr` call, but `source.resource-calls.v1`'s own byte representation and statement set still hold no record. Size unchanged (L).

named_followups.title: A whole record with an owned field cannot be moved to another binding
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS's survey: `let g = f;` is the copy bind (constraint 15k), and for a record that owns it refuses at `Q054` (`CopyOfOwned`); there is no move spelling, and `let j = o.inner;` of a sub-record that owns refuses by name (`W48-QR-NESTED-OWNED-SUBRECORD-MOVE`). DISCHARGE: a move spelling (for example `let g = move f;`) as an IR move of an aggregate re-keying its leaves, with the use-after-move of the source and a Lean statement. Amended by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES moves a record that owns whole across a spawn (`move r`) and a return (`return move r;`) on the scoped-task route; `let q = r;` of one that owns still has no spelling there and refuses by this name (`Q600`).

named_followups.title: A whole sub-record that owns a buffer is read field by field only
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS: `let j = o.inner;` copies a sub-record of scalars, and refuses by name (`Q051`) when `inner` holds an owned field anywhere below, since that would move an aggregate out of another and the IR has `MoveOut` for one leaf only. Size S–M. DISCHARGE: an IR `MoveOutRecord` re-keying every leaf under the path to the new binding and leaving holes, with the whole-record drop tolerating them, and Lean parity. Amended by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES refuses the same shape on the scoped-task route by the same name: a whole read `let j = r.inner;` and a whole `move r.inner` capture of a sub-record that owns (`Q600`); a sub-record of scalars is read and captured by `copy`.

named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS: `o.inner = k;` refuses by name (`Q051`); a write names a scalar field or refills an owned one. Size S for a record of scalars (a copy); M for one that owns (a refill of every leaf, each a hole). named_followups.title: `source.scalar-calls.v1` has records but no field write
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS: a field write derives `mut` on `source.buffer.v1` and `source.ffi.v1`, and this route's rows admit `io` and `throws<ArithmeticError>` only, so `p.x = e;` refuses by name (`Q020`); a function builds the record it means with a construction instead. named_followups.title: A function that may raise `ArithmeticError` cannot return a record
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS: a throwing function returns its value through a scalar out-parameter in the emitted C, so a record result there refuses by name (`Q020`), and no `match` can bind a record `Result::Ok`. named_followups.title: The extern route admits a module whose record type declaration it never reads
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-USABLE-RECORDS's survey (`extern_move.qr`): a module declaring `type F { tag: i32, buf: bytes }` beside an admitted extern entry that never names `F` is admitted by `source.extern.v1`, which reads no record declaration (every record statement there refuses at `Q025`/`Q026`). named_followups.title: A record changed on one continuing `match` arm is unusable after the match
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: the scoped-task lowering represents a record as leaf slots and a field write as a fresh slot (slots are single-assignment), so after a `match` whose continuing arms leave a record in different states — a field written on one arm, moved whole on one, a creation that moved it succeeding on one — the lowering has no join of the two slot maps and marks the record unsettled: every later use refuses (`Q600`). Arms that return, and arms that agree, are unaffected. Size S. DISCHARGE: a join of leaf slot maps at a continuation (a fresh slot per disagreeing scalar leaf, bound on each arm before its `Goto`), with the owned leaves still decided per path by the checker.

named_followups.title: A record type in a composed epoch module is refused
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: `source.epoch.tasks.v1` runs the whole scoped-task route on its task half and then derives the epoch's capture and retained-result shape per argument and per owned Buffer result; no card has measured what a record's leaves and a record result mean against the epoch's allocation axis, so a record declaration in such a module refuses by name (`Q500`) before the task half is compiled. Record-returning programs sit outside F02 relational comparison; their native evidence is the byte comparison of the maintained trace. Size S/M. DISCHARGE: an `ObservedOutcome::Record` over the leaf outcomes, parsed from the header and its leaves, with CT03's conservativity method and no pinned digest moved.

named_followups.title: Byte access and error payloads through a record field on the task route
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: the scoped-task route reads and writes an owned record field whole (`qcore_buffer_read(r.buf)`, `qcore_buffer_write(r.buf, v)`), leases and lends it by a field capture, and drops or refills it, but the owner's byte read `qcore_buffer_read(r.buf, i)` and an error payload raised from a field `raise E::V(r.buf);` still take a plain name only, so each refuses at the route's shape `Q500`. named_followups.title: Read shares of two record fields, and a share beside a lease of another field, stay refused
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-TASK-RECORD-CAPTURES: the card lifted the one-write-leased-resource-at-a-time bound to a per-resource rule, so two fields may be leased to two workers at once, but two bounds it did not need stay global: at most one outstanding read loan at a time (so `read r.a share N` and `read r.b share N` to two workers refuse), and no outstanding read loan beside a write lease even of another resource (so a read share of one field and a lease of another refuse). Both are sound to lift per resource by the same argument — the ledger decides every share and lease per resource — but each is pinned by earlier tests (`crates/qcore-frontend/tests/read_loans.rs`, `read_shares.rs`). Size S. DISCHARGE: the two bounds per resource, those pins moved by name, and the per-leaf Lean statement extended to read shares.

named_followups.why: Found by CG04-LOOP-SITE-GENERATIONS (gateway rule 11a). The flow does not relate a guard on a loop counter to the iteration, so an acquisition only the first pass runs (`for (pass = 1; pass <= 2; pass++) { ... if (pass == 1) outbuf = rd_malloc(uof); }`, snappy.c:1705) is re-acquired on the abstract second pass and its earlier generation is reported leaking at four exits (snappy.c:1680, 1694, 1712, 1721) where the source frees or returns the one buffer. DISCHARGE: a counted-loop fact that decides a `pass == k` guard per iteration (or a recorded decision to keep the reading), re-measured. AMENDED (LOOP-REACQUISITION-LEAK-ACCUSATION, gateway rule 42): at base 82ec0e80b the four earlier-generation leaves of rd_kafka_snappy_java_uncompress (:1680, :1694, :1712, :1721) are withdrawn under the function's rule-11a refusal at :1705 (the re-acquisition is now refused); the pass guard still keeps the current generation live at :1648, :1660 and :1701, which stay provisional Unsafe. DISCHARGE unchanged.

named_followups.title: A closure is a spawn target only: no closure stored, passed or called as a value
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-CLOSURES (user decision of 2026-09-29: closures with an explicit capture list, lifted into a hidden named worker). The lift makes a closure a named worker at its one spawn site, so a capture list anywhere else — `let c = |copy x| -> T { … };`, a closure passed to a worker, a closure called — is refused (`Q038` for a capture-list shape outside `spawn SCOPE`, `Q000` for one in a named worker's argument list). A closure value needs a type for it (its captures' custody travels with the value: a closure that moved an owned Buffer is itself affine), a spawn of a closure-typed binding, and a rule for when its captures are taken (at the value's creation or at its spawn). Size L. DISCHARGE: a closure type in the task route's value vocabulary whose custody is its captures', with the transferability judgment deciding each capture at the value's creation, a spawn of such a binding lowering to the same hidden worker, and Lean parity with `QCore.Closures`.

named_followups.title: Closures are not lowered on the epoch routes
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-CLOSURES (the brief's stretch item 4). A closure on `source.epoch.tasks.v1` or the pure epoch route is refused at `Q600` by name at the driver. The composed epoch route's plan names each worker it accounts for (`thread scope NAME { copy; peak …; effort …; }` inside the `epoch` scope), and a closure's hidden worker is named `ENCLOSING#closureN`, which no source can spell: lifting it needs a spelling for a plan entry that accounts for a closure (for example keyed by the closure's position, or a plan clause written beside the closure), which is a language decision, and the route's source split (`split.task_source`) must keep the closure whole. Size M. DISCHARGE: a decided plan spelling for a closure, the composed route lowering the hidden worker with the plan entry bound to it, and an epoch example twin-identical to its hand-written form.

named_followups.title: Closures are not lowered on the mutex route, and `share … under M` is no capture
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-CLOSURES (the brief's stretch item 4). A closure in a module declaring a mutex generation is refused at `Q600` by name at the driver. On `source.mutex.guard.v1` a child is a lexical `thread scope NAME [share PLACE under MUTEX] { … }` block, not a spawned worker, and `share PLACE under MUTEX` is a clause of that scope (card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS), not a capture a named worker's list admits — so the brief's `share NAME under M` capture spelling has no named-worker twin to lift to. Size M. DISCHARGE: a decision whether a closure on this route is the lexical child scope with a capture list (the clause moving into it) or a spawned worker the route learns to lower, then the lift with the mutex crossing's three-half decision (constraint 15o) unchanged.

named_followups.title: Closures are not lowered on the field-footprint route
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-CLOSURES. `source.bitfield-concurrency.v1` is selected before the task route and reads named workers' `write OBJECT.FIELD` captures against an explicit layout; a closure there is refused at `Q600` by name at the driver rather than handed to a route that reads no hidden worker. Size S. DISCHARGE: the route reading a closure's capture list as its spawn's (the lift already gives the capture list and the hidden worker), with its `DisjointFootprintsV1` certificate unchanged and a twin-identity row.

named_followups.title: A module refused in both a closure's body and its enclosing function may report the other refusal first
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-CLOSURES. A closure's parameter types are decided by lowering its enclosing function to the spawn site first; when that function refuses before the spawn site is reached, its refusal is the module's, while the hand-written twin — whose worker is declared, and lowered, first — would report the worker's own refusal when the body also refuses. The refused set is the same (each program is refused either way) and every admitted program is twin-identical; only which of two refusals a doubly-refused module shows first can differ. Size S. DISCHARGE: decide a closure's parameter types by a pass that reads the environment at the spawn site without stopping at an earlier refusal, so the worker can be lowered first as the twin's is; or record the order as the rule (a closure's types come from its spawn site).

named_followups.title: The float emission is built natively with Clang on Linux only
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-FLOATING-POINT. The emitted float C — the `_Static_assert`s on `<float.h>` and `FLT_EVAL_METHOD`, the `#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF` guarded to Clang, the compound-literal renderer buffers `(char[48]){0}`, the union compound literal spelling a NaN or an infinity, the hexadecimal float constants — is built and run here with Clang 21 on x86-64 Linux only. MSVC (`/fp:strict`, its C11 mode's compound literals) and Apple Clang on arm64 (where contraction is FMA by default and the build premise `-ffp-contract=off` matters most) are unmeasured. Size S. DISCHARGE: the card's native boundary table, renderer sample and extern/FFI/task rows built and run on Windows/MSVC and macOS/arm64, each platform against its own reference. named_followups.title: A byte view of a NaN payload is not determined
named_followups.why: Found by W48-QR-FLOAT-BUFFER-PAYLOADS, measured: the same task-route `0.0 / 0.0` stored into a `Buffer<f32>`/`Buffer<f64>` is x86-64's sign-set default NaN when divided at run time (the Rust reference, a `-O0` build) and the sign-clear quiet NaN when Clang folds it (`-O2`), so the owner's byte read of the payload's top byte differs between the reference and a native run in the sign bit (4 of 126 native payload runs). The card states it as specification §L14.7 limitation 16 (a NaN's sign and payload bits in a byte view are not specified, per the brief) and its native rows admit exactly that one-bit difference at that one line. Size S. DISCHARGE: typed float payload writes and allocations canonicalise NaN in the reference and the emitted C, the native rows compared byte for byte with no tolerance, and the limitation narrowed to NaNs built by byte writes.

named_followups.why: Registered by CALLEE-RETENTION-CLASS1 (sizes: functions decided alone on corpus a43d02cb). add_item_to_object 3: its constant_key arm stores the caller's `string` in the item (a retention beside a disposition, which C04.14 rejects) and its callers pass `false`/`true`, casts no literal premise reads (C04.5.1). cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts 2: `value` is retained by the file-scope global_error and an interior pointer of it is delivered through `return_parse_end`, which no out-slot mode states. rd_kafka_confval_set_type 5 and rd_kafka_interceptor_method_add 4: an enum typedef parameter or result (W43-LIBC-ABI-READER-SHAPES); the first retains `valuep` in its PTR arm only (an argument-conditioned retention). AMENDED (W43-ABI-ENUM-AND-CONST-PP, corpus 66910c10 a43d02cb 812/9/4,013 -> 686fca16 846/9/3,979, base 4f55fa4c4; system 87/4/357 and slice 45/1/354/4 Pending, no row moves): USER DECISION 2026-10-05. 1. **Integer projection for enum typedefs.** A parameter or result whose C type is an enum (tagged or untagged, through any typedef chain) is spelled in the contract as its **underlying integer type**, e.g. `i32` or `u32`. The reader takes that type from Clang's AST for the target (`fixedUnderlyingType` or the computed enum integer type), never assumes `int`, and requires an exact width and signedness match. If Clang does not state the type, refuse. No new type grammar; the contract does not record the enum's name. 2. **Shapes covered: enum typedefs and pointer-to-pointer-to-const** (`const char **`, `const void **`; today `pointer_projection` admits only `T **`). State the const-qualification rule precisely: which level is const, and what a `ptr<…>` spelling must say. Transparent unions (`__CONST_SOCKADDR_ARG`) and `va_list` stay registered, out of scope. 3. **Conditional clauses on an enum argument's value, in this card.** Some callees behave differently by an enum argument's value. `rd_kafka_confval_set_type` retains `valuep` only when `valuetype` is the PTR constant (5 functions alone). Add a guard, e.g. `when PARAM == CONST` (design the exact spelling; reuse the QUANT-INDEX-CHECKS comparison operators `==`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` and their evaluation model). A clause then applies only when the caller's actual is decided to satisfy the guard. An undecided actual gets the **cautious reading**: the union or join of every guarded clause, never the favourable one. Guards are over integer-typed (including enum-projected) parameters only, and constants are integer literals. Do not name enum constants: the integer projection carries no names, so state the value with its source citation in a comment. Requirements: total-or-reject grammar; guards must partition or cover: an uncovered value gets the cautious reading; Lean: the guard semantics, the cautious join, and the theorem that an undecided guard never yields Safe where the cautious reading would not; body check: where the body is available (W4 validation), each guarded clause is validated under its guard. named_followups.title: Decision 1's custody reading frees 4 of the 7 CG10-INTERIOR-ALIAS-NULLABILITY functions; the other 3 are blocked by something else, and custody's older reading of unbound names lists no premise
named_followups.why: USER DECISION 2026-10-10 (verbatim): 1. Move the NULL question (resolves CG10-INTERIOR-ALIAS-NULLABILITY). &B->F, or any use of B as non-NULL, is read as non-NULL only when every path to it already went through a real read or write via B, with B not reassigned in between. Forming &B->G and sizeof/unevaluated operands do not count as dereferences. The NULL question then moves to that dominating dereference, and that dereference becomes a published check in a new null-safety property. Proved: from a NULL test, a non-NULL contract result or parameter, a checked allocation, or a further dominating dereference up the chain. Otherwise: a NULL-dereference candidate, validated for reachability before any Unsafe and never presented as an upstream defect. A custody verdict relying on the non-NULL reading lists a named assumption tied to the dereference site until the null-safety check proves it. It appears in the per-verdict dependency set and roll-up. User motivation: NULL dereference is one of the most common bug sources, so the value is in surfacing candidates, not only in freeing functions. 2. Contract syntax (the user called it "quite ideal"): quant null-deref #B; Collocated check form, like quant checks. It means "this function dereferences B; B must be non-NULL." Caller side: the actual for B must be proved non-NULL, otherwise it is a candidate at the call site. Callee side: the body check validates that the body dereferences B without a prior NULL test. Inside the body, after the first dereference, B and &B->F are non-NULL (decision 1). A body that tests B first does not need the clause. Report it as stronger than necessary, never as wrong. Implemented by NULL-SAFETY-PROPERTY (gateway rule 14n; corpus 66910c10 903/9/3,922 24b59d52 -> 915 / 9 / 3,910, resource-diagnostics.json ded14632; system 91 / 4 / 353 (f4f19c2d); slice 50 / 1 / 349 / 4 Pending (249aa27a)): a scalar read or write through a target-free, unknown, possibly-null borrowed alias of the identity derivation is read non-null under the named premise null-deref:FUNCTION:LINE:VARIABLE, listed on the summary, the row, the row's contract_dependencies (transitively) and the Safe roll-up. Freed with premises: peek, sink_peek, rd_kafka_share_ack_type_from_msg_op, rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_regex_cnt (and 8 more corpus, 2 system and 5 slice rows). Left, each measured: append (after iov++ the binding is a stepped derivation; decision 1 ends the moved question at a reassignment, so custody reads nothing); mk_vhost_fdt_chain_lookup (its remaining leaf is the return of the unknown alias hc, an identity question apply_resource_action refuses for any unknown binding, not a nullness one); rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_has_duplicates (on the base it also carries an uncontracted rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort_by_topic and indirect accesses: a correction to the follow-up's population). Custody's pre-existing reading of a dereference through an unbound name (a formal, W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL: nullness outside the property) lists no premise: 37 custody Safe rows have a formal-sourced null candidate. DISCHARGE: a decision whether those readings list a premise too (they would join every custody Safe row that dereferences a formal), and, for append, whether an offset of a moved alias keeps the premise in custody as it keeps the moved question in the null property (C11 6.5.6p8). Re-measured by NULL-CANDIDATE-TRIAGE (corpus a4): the custody report is byte-identical; the null property proves 782 premise checks (676 before; candidates 1,000 -> 892, 2 now findings); custody Safe rows with an own premise 12, every premise proved 1 (unchanged): none of the 31 premise-carrying rows is discharged by the new member declarations (their premises read s->iov, i->storage and list elements). Re-measured by NULL-MEMBER-INVARIANT-SCOPE (corpus a2): custody byte-identical; premise checks the null property proves 782 -> 786 (candidates 892 -> 888); custody Safe rows with an own premise 12, every premise proved 1 (unchanged); system 2 / 0 and slice 5 / 1 unchanged.

named_followups.title: The off-Linux consumption probe (a read end kept from the spawn) has never been executed
named_followups.why: Recorded by HOST-UNREAD-REQUEST-ACCEPTANCE-BY-SCHEDULING (base e0b92ece6); amended by HOST-REQUEST-READ-BY-DETACHED-DESCENDANT (base b565f79ab). Off Linux the host cannot reopen the request pipe through /proc (/dev/fd is a dup there), so it keeps a duplicate of the read end from the spawn as its probe. That probe makes a broken request pipe impossible, so a live provider that closed its input is a Timeout at its deadline there, where Linux reports RequestUnconsumed; standalone_host and cycle20_verifier_plugins assert the two per platform. HOST-REQUEST-READ-BY-DETACHED-DESCENDANT keeps that arm unchanged (the host decides there on the probe's count, as before), and its probe cases in tests/request_consumption.rs assert per platform what the off-Linux host decides (RequestUnconsumed, or either outcome for a descendant that reads on its own schedule; the setsid case is Linux-only). Every measurement of both cards is Linux; the macOS CI job compiles the crate but runs none of its process rows, and no macOS host was available. Size: the non-Linux arms of request_pipe and request_consumption::holders, two standalone_host assertions and the probe binary's off-Linux expectations. DISCHARGE: the verifier-host process rows and the probe binary run on a macOS host, with their results recorded.

named_followups.title: Off Linux a descendant that keeps the request pipe with both outputs closed still gets an outcome that depends on timing
named_followups.why: Recorded by HOST-REQUEST-READ-BY-DETACHED-DESCENDANT (base b565f79ab). On Linux the host decides a successful exit only as the request pipe's last holder: it observes the other holders through a write end opened via /proc/self/fd/<probe> and POLLERR, waits for them up to the deadline, and refuses a pipe still held then (RequestHeldByDescendant). Off Linux /dev/fd is a dup, the probe is the read end itself, and no mechanism was found that tells the host's read end from another process's. By the user's decision ("keep previous macOS") the host decides there exactly as before the card, on the bytes left unread at the direct child's exit (Holders::CountOnly; Lean off_linux_decides_on_the_count_at_the_decision). So for the one shape, a descendant that inherited the request pipe, put both outputs elsewhere and reads on its own schedule, the outcome (accepted or RequestUnconsumed) still depends on whether its reads land before that moment (off_linux_a_late_reader_still_depends_on_the_schedule). Neither branch is a wrong Safe: the response is still checked. Never executed (no macOS host). Size: that shape off Linux; the card's census found no provider or fixture with it. DISCHARGE: an off-Linux holder check (for example a socket-pair request transport, whose peer close the host can observe), measured on a macOS host.

named_followups.title: providers/package.py build copies each provider executable with shutil.copyfile in the packaging process and then executes it
named_followups.why: Recorded by PLUGIN-PACKAGE-BUILD-WRITES-EXECUTABLE-IN-PROCESS (base b565f79ab, rebased onto 5ee141946), found by its census, not observed failing. providers/package.py build (lines 412-413 at the base) writes each package's provider with shutil.copyfile, sets 0o755, and verify() executes it (--verify-package, --contract-manifest) right after. If any other thread of the packaging process forked while that write descriptor was open, the forked child would hold a duplicate until its exec and the execve would fail with ETXTBSY (the mechanism EXECUTION-QUOTA-LOAD-INDEPENDENCE measured; the Rust SDK's counterpart was repaired by PLUGIN-PACKAGE-BUILD-WRITES-EXECUTABLE-IN-PROCESS). It cannot meet the race today: the script imports no threading module and every subprocess.run is sequential on its one thread, and nothing imports build() into a threaded program. Size: one function, five packages. DISCHARGE: build installs the executable without the packaging process holding a write descriptor on it (an out-of-process writer, as package::build does), or a documented single-threaded contract on build that its callers are checked against, or a recorded argument that no multi-threaded caller can exist.

named_followups.title: quirin-audit prepare's copy_with_times copies Monkey's executable files with fs::copy in the preparing process
named_followups.why: Recorded by PLUGIN-PACKAGE-BUILD-WRITES-EXECUTABLE-IN-PROCESS (base b565f79ab, rebased onto 5ee141946), found by its census, not observed failing. crates/qcore-audit/src/prepare.rs copy_with_times (fs::copy, which keeps the mode) copies the tracked Monkey tree into the persistent source copy, executable files included (configure, debian.sh, qa/run_tests.sh, libevent's autogen.sh and configure, build-aux scripts). A copied executable that some process ran while a fork of another quirin-audit thread still held the copy's write descriptor would fail with ETXTBSY. Neither half holds today: prepare copies sequentially on its only thread before its first cmake spawn, and nothing in the preparing flow executes a copied file (CMake's configure runs perl and the compilers). Size: one function. DISCHARGE: the copy holds no write descriptor in the preparing process on a file that keeps an executable mode (an out-of-process writer, or copying without the execute bits where no copy is ever executed), or a recorded, checked single-threaded contract on prepare's copy step.

named_followups.title: One pre-pass summary key changes with the clock, so route sidecars are not reproducible
named_followups.why: Found by AUDIT-CANONICAL-PATHS. The Fluent Bit compile database compiles lib/monkey/mk_bin/monkey.c, whose MONKEY_BUILT is `__DATE__ " " __TIME__`. DISCHARGE: preprocess under a fixed, recorded SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (Clang honours it for __DATE__ and __TIME__), or refuse or normalise the time macros in the identity. CFG-RELEASE observation: with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1761004800 set in the caller's environment, corpus, slice and system route outputs of two independently built sides are raw byte-identical and share every pre-pass summary key (1,058 / 1,039 / 1,037). AMENDED by MEASURE-TOOL: every route of every side quirin-audit measure runs gets one fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (default 1767225600, --source-date-epoch, recorded in run.json and in a baseline's inputs), which CFG-RELEASE measured removes the key difference and the tool's live-4 run confirms (system and slice contracts sidecars byte-identical between two sides); for sides measured without it the tool accepts a differing contracts sidecar only by the checked one-key substitution of AUDIT-COMPOSITION's compare_identity.py (compare::time_key: exactly one lifetime-source summary key differs, no collision, equal as JSON and as a line multiset after the swap) and names it in the record. The analyzer itself still hashes the clock-dependent text outside the tool; the DISCHARGE (fixed or normalised time macros in loop_lifetime_source::read_unit, with its test) stays open. Card CONTRACT-SUPERSESSION's identity run set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1790357241 on both sides and the key did not vary on any of the three routes, so an identity run can neutralise it by the environment; the published digest still carries the wall clock when the variable is unset.

named_followups.title: A component's analyzer revision is package@version plus an optional build commit, not the binary digest
named_followups.why: report_components::analyzer_revision (card AUDIT-COMPOSITION) spells qcore-audit@<version>:<QCORE_AUDIT_BUILD_COMMIT or unrecorded-build>. Two different builds without a recorded commit share a provenance key, so joining their contributions surfaces as composition-conflict (fail-closed) rather than as two producers. DISCHARGE: put the analyzer binary's SHA-256 (as checkpoint_run::run_identity takes it) or a mandatory build commit into Provenance, with a test that two differing binaries never share a provenance key.

named_followups.title: Matrix corpus rows are bound to profiles but not derived from them
named_followups.why: Found by EVALUATION-PROFILES. contract/evaluations/bindings.json classifies every key of the acceptance matrix corpus section, and a test refuses an unbound key, but the rows themselves stay hand-maintained: conditional_eight_home_cycle3, bound route by route to the three live profiles, still shows the W48 batch-5 figures (corpus 975 Safe) while the live baselines record BASE 710021bd7. DISCHARGE: build_matrix.py emits each bound row's profile name and policy and, for a live profile, the figures of its current baseline.json, so the row cannot drift from the profile.

named_followups.title: Re-base the live evaluation profiles onto a newer Fluent Bit revision every one to two months
named_followups.why: User decision 2 of 2026-10-24 (docs/plans/pluggable-cards/README.md section 3 A, corpus cadence): the live profiles eight-home, fluent-bit-system and fluent-bit-tail-pause follow the Fluent Bit repository, best effort every one to two months. EVALUATION-PROFILES recorded their first baselines on BASE 710021bd7 over Fluent Bit 66910c10a (corpus), 046accf6a (system) and 34155955e (tail-pause slice). The policy check treats a change of a live profile's tracked inputs as a re-base that must record the newly measured baseline, with its reason, in the same commit; the previous baseline stays in baseline_history. Frozen cycle profiles are never moved. DISCHARGE: recurring; each firing is a card that prepares the newer revision's inputs, re-reviews the pins whose sites changed (pin --check, C06.2), records the new baselines through evaluation_profiles.py record and names the date of the next firing.

named_followups.title: Wire baseline publication into the integrator's landing gate
named_followups.why: Card MEASURE-TOOL implemented `quirin-audit measure publish --from <out>/sides/<name>` (output private/baselines/<sha>, one immutable <profile>/ per route with baseline.json digests) and identity-verified reuse by --side NAME=baseline:<sha>; the exact landing commands are in docs/reports/measure-tool/README.md. No landing has published a baseline yet. DISCHARGE: the integrator's per-landing full gate measures the landed revision with a rev:<sha> side on the live routes and publishes it, and the next card reuses it as BASE after verification instead of rebuilding BASE. Card MEASURE-TOOL-LANDING-PUBLISH connected the publisher to scripts/land.py's post-gate sequence with clean-tree, first-parent baseline selection and explicit first-run bootstrap. The command-level test exercises bootstrap and later baseline selection. The named follow-up remains Open until the integrator publishes the landed SHA and a subsequent card reuses it with real plugin identity verification. Card LANDING-PUBLISH-COMPLETION made `land.py publish` apply the evaluation-profile policy before publishing: it refuses, and keeps the measurement, when a live profile's landed figures differ from the baseline committed in the landing, so a move lands only with its new baseline and an appended baseline_history reason. The first landed publication (`--previous b0b63da7`) is the integrator's step after the landing push.

named_followups.title: Bind contribution ledgers to the gateway rule registry once it lands
named_followups.why: scripts/contribution_ledgers.py (card CONTRIBUTION-LEDGERS) refuses a ledger for a rule absent from crates/gateway-rules/registry.toml once that file exists, reading any TOML table with a string `id` in file order for existence and for the order of contributions; until then it checks docs/agents/rules/<id>.md. GATEWAY-RULE-API had not landed, so the reader is generic and untested against a real registry. DISCHARGE: when the registry lands, its rows carry `id` equal to the rule-document id in consultation order (or registry_ids reads the API's actual field), a test reads the real registry, and each registry row may reference its contract/contributions/<id>/ directory.

named_followups.title: Measure rules 32/32a's contribution ledgers by switch
named_followups.why: Rule 32's report (docs/reports/w48-rk-log-caller-frame/README.md) records 7 eight-home rows Unknown to Safe under three named premises, separated from rules 34 and 35 by compile-time builds, not by a run-time switch; CONTRIBUTION-LEDGERS did not transcribe it (source report-transcribed is not accepted). DISCHARGE: after rule 32a's migration card, quirin-audit measure --profile eight-home (and the other live profiles) --rules-off 32a (with --per-rule beside any rule it interacts with) writes the ledgers with contribution_ledgers.py write, consistency passes, and the report compares the measured rows and premises with the recorded 7. RULE32A-PILOT (2026-10-31): rule 32a is a fixed hold (plan section 6 item 10, GATEWAY-RULE-API-HOLD-OFF retired), so --rules-off 32a is refused by design and 32a has no switch-measured ledger; the 7 recorded rows are callers outside the frame reading the caller-frame declarations, i.e. rule 32's contribution (Lean QCore.CallerFrameHoldSwitch.holding_more_moves_an_outside_row). Amended DISCHARGE: a card registers rule 32 with a refusing switch over the outside callers' reading of the caller-frame declarations (off: the declaration is not read, which never widens), then quirin-audit measure on the live profiles --rules-off 32 writes rule 32's ledgers with contribution_ledgers.py write, consistency passes, and the report compares the measured rows and premises with the recorded 7.

named_followups.title: Measure rule 36's contribution ledgers by switch
named_followups.why: Rule 36's rows (W48-BU-CMT-MAP-METRIC-GET) were measured by that card across revisions; CONTRIBUTION-LEDGERS did not transcribe them. DISCHARGE: after rule 36's migration card, a --rules-off 36 measurement on the live profiles writes its ledgers, consistency passes, and the report compares them with docs/reports/w48-bu-cmt-map-metric-get/README.md's recorded rows.

named_followups.title: Interrupting a measure host can leave the plugin and slot jobs alive
named_followups.why: Observed during MEASURE-TOOL-LANDING-PUBLISH integration: the bootstrap host and scoped gate shell returned exit 130 after interruption, but the measure plugin PID 3083741, its audit slot descendants and the scoped gate PID 3088618 remained alive. The abandoned scoped-gate tree was explicitly terminated after process-table attribution; the immutable rev-side measurement was retained for separate collection. DISCHARGE: cancellation of the audit host and landing wrapper terminates and reaps every spawned plugin/route process and releases its slot locks, exercised with a running or queued measure plugin; no other worktree process is signalled.

named_followups.title: Compile-time arm constants remain
named_followups.why: The 10n and ENUM_ARM compile-time constants were not trivially equivalent to a run-time switch and remain. DISCHARGE: each replaced by its registry row's switch with an identity run, in the migration card for its rule.

named_followups.title: Corpus build identity digests the side's working directory
named_followups.why: Under `quirin-audit measure` each side's pinned corpus route runs in sides/<name>/work-corpus, and the unit build identity (projection.rs hypothesis_context) digests the working directory, so corpus artifacts are never byte-identical across sides and the tool reports composition-conflict for equal provenance. DISCHARGE: the tool runs every side's corpus at one fixed working directory, or the identity excludes it, with a byte-identity test. Observed again by LANDING-PUBLISH-COMPLETION: corpus sides differ only in environment digest fields; component union 370 against 185 rows; compared by rows (0 moved, figures equal) in the card's corpus-peak run and in the first landed publication at d4c43b5ac. Observed again by RULE35-PILOT (base rev:80c8aea98, tip rev:555bd17db): 365 components for 185 rows, 0 rows moved; besides 64-hex digests the moved build identity also moves 24-hex `resource_contracts:` ids and id-sorted evidence order, which GATEWAY-RULE-API's substitution.py cannot pair; docs/reports/rule35-pilot/scripts/substitution_ids.py checks a one-to-one substitution of both token kinds with lists as multisets (all five differing corpus artifacts pass). A fix in the tool would retire both checkers.

named_followups.title: Bounds and outer contract views keep their own duplicate refusals and never consult pin stamps
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-SUPERSESSION decides duplicate resource declarations by pin stamp (contract spec C06.6). The bounds view (bounds_selection) and the outer view (outer_selection) still refuse a function declared twice, and their locks' stamps are written and verified but read by no loader. DISCHARGE: both views decide duplicates through qcore_schemas::contract_supersession::decide over their own locks' stamps, retaining superseded declarations and withholding conflicts under contract-conflict, with tests and an identity run.

named_followups.title: Only the legacy-C gateway names a contract conflict; other environment consumers see an uncontracted callee
named_followups.why: ResourceContracts::contract_conflict withholds a function from every table, so every consumer refuses its calls, but only the legacy-C gateway rewrites them to the contract-conflict hold. The checked extern-call route (qcore_verification::driver) and other API callers report an uncontracted callee, Unknown under a different reason. DISCHARGE: those routes name contract-conflict for a withheld callee (as they do for a pending review), with a test per route.

named_followups.title: A supersession inside a module elaborated through inclusion refuses the whole selection
named_followups.why: load_resource_contract_selection_stamped refuses when a superseded or conflicted declaration lies in a module carrying inclusion evidence, because the evidence replays the elaborated text byte for byte and a cut text would not replay. Fail-closed, but the duplicate is not decided. DISCHARGE: the cut is replayed by the evidence check (or applied before elaboration at the declaration's source module), so such a duplicate is decided like any other, with a test over an #include/inherit fixture.

named_followups.title: Archived pin lock sets are records; no audit route can select one
named_followups.why: The lock-set window (providers/pin-lock-window.json, user decision 9a) archives up to two earlier lock sets byte for byte under providers/pin-lock-sets/<revision>/, but every audit reads the live locks in providers/<crate>/. Comparing a re-based profile row by row with the previous revision under that revision's own lock set therefore needs a route option. DISCHARGE: the audit routes (and quirin-audit measure) accept a retained lock set by revision, refuse a retired one, record the set's revision and digests in the contract_revision section, and a test audits a fixture under an archived set.

named_followups.title: pin --check does not verify that a re-pin's stamp is later than the committed entry it replaced
named_followups.why: quirin-audit pin enforces the later-stamp rule when it writes a lock (an explicit stamp not later than the replaced entry refuses), but pin --check and pin --verify-contracts read only the working tree, so a hand edit or a merge that lowers a stamp is not detected. DISCHARGE: pin --check (or providers/contracts.py check) compares each entry's stamp with the same entry at a named base revision and refuses a changed entry whose stamp is not later, with a test.

named_followups.title: Add pinned shorthand bundles for repeated provider contract requirements
named_followups.why: CMetrics and CFL contracts repeat long require lists. Add explicitly declared, provider-owned requirement bundles such as `contract_cmetrics_resource_v1` and `contract_cfl_resource_v1` whose expansion is pinned by exact clause identity, order and provenance. Missing, unknown, cyclic, duplicate or signature-mismatched bundles must refuse. A bundle is syntax-level requirement expansion only: it is not an alias for executable `resource_contract_v1`, supplies no call permission and cannot weaken Unknown. DISCHARGE: matching parser/formatter and Rust semantic support, placeholder-free Lean definitions/theorems, canonical `.qv` declarations, provider inventory/count/load-path pins, mutation controls for every refusal and fresh native attribution if any verdict-bearing semantics move.

named_followups.title: pin --track-tip writes each lock before the run can refuse
named_followups.why: `quirin-audit pin --track-tip` (contract_pin.rs run) writes each selected target's lock inside its loop, and refuses only afterwards when a named function is declared by no selected crate (or when `track` refuses a later target), so a refused run can leave earlier locks rewritten. Card PIN-REGENERATE-STAMP-MONOTONICITY made the update/regenerate loop compute every lock before writing any; --stamp-only and --drop-revision already did. Found by code reading; no run has shown it. DISCHARGE: the track-tip branch computes every lock and checks every named function before any write, with a test that a refused multi-target run leaves every lock byte-identical.

named_followups.title: Production-source scans skip rule packages
named_followups.why: Tests that enumerate production sources as `crates/*/src` (for example qcore-verification's composition_bounds.rs `production_sources`, the E03-B-O3 vacuity tripwire) do not see `crates/gateway-rules/<package>/src`, which RULE35-PILOT introduced. Rule 35's package states no such derivation, so nothing is missed today. DISCHARGE: every production-source scan includes rule packages, with a test naming rule 35's package.

named_followups.title: W4 summaries of asserting wrappers carry no named build premise
named_followups.why: With rule 37 off (QCORE_GATEWAY_RULES_OFF=37), the checked specifications of rd_calloc and rd_strdup are withdrawn, which is the existing W45 withdrawal. Their callers then see what W4 validates from the in-unit asserting body: a non-null result through the enabled assert's terminating call. A caller with no sizeof, such as rd_calloc(1, 16) in tests/rule37_switch.rs, therefore stays Safe on that summary, and its row names no asserted_allocation premise. This is no Unknown-to-Safe by the migration, since the row is Safe with 37 on too. It also predates rule 37 for any undeclared asserting wrapper. But it means the deployed-build fact rule 37 makes explicit for a declared specification is only implicit, as the analysed-build assumption, for a W4-inferred one. DISCHARGE: decide whether a W4 summary that rests on a terminating assertion must carry a named premise (and implement it with an identity or measured run), or record that it rests on the standing analysed-build assumption. ARM-OBLIGATIONS: rows resting on a standing asserted_allocation specification now carry the premise (rule_obligations, folded into the assumptions digest); a W4-inferred summary of an asserting body still carries none, so this residual is unchanged. ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN: this residual is why the row grain is attributed by consultation, not by a rerun with the admission refused: with the specification withdrawn, W4 validates the same non-null result from the asserting body, so a differential rerun would let callers shed asserted_allocation while their verdict still rests on the deployed-build fact.

named_followups.title: The Windows full-suite leg's batched runner has not run on Windows
named_followups.why: TEST-STORAGE-BUDGET moved CI's msvc-clang-analysis full suite from `cargo test --workspace` to `python scripts/run_test_binaries.py --jobs 1 --batch-size 32` (static linking, batches built, run and deleted). The batched mode ran green on Linux in static mode with --jobs 8 (8,927 / 0 / 15, test set equal to the base, 6.19 GB peak), but never on Windows or with --jobs 1; the first CI run is its first Windows execution. Check that run's totals against the Linux figure and its per-batch deleted_bytes in summary.json; a dynamic Windows build would first need the DLL export counts of the large crates measured against the 65,535 limit. CI-RUST-JOB-PEAK (2026-10-31) could not observe a Windows CI run: `git ls-remote origin` shows refs only, GitHub's public API answers 404 for the private repository's workflow runs, and the host has no gh CLI or token; still open.

named_followups.title: Rule 36's package-local SourceHost repeats the API's TypedHost
named_followups.why: crates/gateway-rules/rule-36-exact-formal-return/src/source.rs defines SourceHost (node kind, string attribute, object field, type, children, the host's pointer-type test) because RULE35-PILOT's TypedHost was not yet in the API at the card's base; TypedHost now is, with the same reads minus node_field, so the gateway implements two typed-node capabilities over serde_json::Value. DISCHARGE: SourceHost becomes TypedHost plus whatever it adds (node_field, pointer_type) as an API capability, rule 36's package bounds on it, and an identity run (or the package's and gateway's rule-36 tests, if the change is proved behaviour-neutral) shows no movement.

named_followups.title: ReturnQuery has no honest values for the first return route
named_followups.why: qcore-gateway-rule-api's ReturnQuery requires origin: usize and decided: &Statement. Rule 36's route is asked first in return_statement, which is also the lowering of operands the elaborators hand back without a stream place, so the gateway host passes origin usize::MAX and, as decided, its own refusal (not supported, no evaluation); rule 36 reads neither. DISCHARGE: the API gives the return route position an optional origin and no decided value before the first route (or a separate first-route query), and the rule-36 host drops the placeholders.

named_followups.title: A published baseline is refused by a --profile measurement
named_followups.why: quirin-audit measure verifies a baseline:<sha> side by each route's digest, the SHA-256 of the route definition. The landing publication measures from inputs/live.json, which spells the eight-home link map as docs/reports/w48-bu-single-leaf-bodies/link-map.corpus.json; --profile spells it contract/evaluations/eight-home/link-map.json (the same bytes). RULE36-PILOT's first identity run (--profile with --side base=baseline:80c8aea98) was refused on all three routes after its TIP sides had run (about 5 h), so the plan's section 4 step 3 command cannot reuse today's baselines. DISCHARGE: the route digest is computed over the inputs' content digests rather than their spellings, or publication and --profile share one spelling, with a test that a --profile measurement accepts a baseline published from inputs/live.json; the refusal should also come before any side runs. RULE32A-PILOT (2026-10-31) hit it again: --profile with --side base=baseline:db2795100 refused all three routes after TIP (rev:492f0418a) had run for about 8 h. Recovered without re-measuring: --side base=run:<landing measurement>/sides/tip (the land.py side the baseline was published from, every listed file checked against the baseline's SHA-256 by docs/reports/rule32a-pilot/scripts/landing_equals_baseline.py) and --side tip=run:<measure-1>/sides/tip, which completes; this works only while the landing side is still on disk.

named_followups.title: A record shared by several cards has one ledger writer
named_followups.why: scripts/contribution_ledgers.py write copies every ledger of a native-comparison record, and check_contribution requires the amendments field to list every ledger of the same measurement and profile. The round-2 shared measurement (rules 33, 34, 36, one record) therefore had its nine ledgers written and listed by RULE36-PILOT; RULE33-PILOT and RULE34-PILOT cannot list only their own. DISCHARGE: write accepts a rule filter and check_contribution accepts a card's subset of a group when the rest of the group is committed, or the shared-measurement procedure names one writer for the whole group, recorded in operations.md.

named_followups.title: No route-map position for CFG-build body rewrites or derivation row routes
named_followups.why: ROUTE-MAP section 1 lists the per-CFG-build body rewrites (_Generic resolution, literal premises, 11r, and since rule 33 the removed-selection expansion) beside the token holds, and the custody derivation's function-row routes (rule 33's frame install and row under its selection entry, rule 37's checked-specification settlement) are not mapped at all. The only position of section 1 is token-hold, a hold, which forces not-switchable; so RULE33-PILOT registered its expansion arm at statement-rewrite and its entry-row arm at classification, by effect, as RULE37-PILOT did for its settlement arm. Placement by effect is unchecked: the generator and the route-map test cannot tell whether an arm sits where its host consults it. DISCHARGE: add non-hold positions for body rewrites and derivation rows to qcore-gateway-rule-api's Position and the route map, move the arms placed by effect there (an identity run per move), or record that placement by effect is the registry's policy.

named_followups.title: Obligations do not cross a unit export or a spawned thread
named_followups.why: ARM-OBLIGATIONS refuses rather than carries in two places: a cross-unit home whose row carries a rule-package obligation is not exported (an imported contract has no premise slot), and an admission asked on a thread a unit analysis spawns (std::thread::scope in deep_unit_ast, null_deref, typed_dispatch_census, loop_owner_region_macros, c_numeric_obligations) sees no frame and is refused. Both are fail-closed; the identity run moved no live verdict. Open obligations publish as Unknown only; no route publishes Pending for a named human-resolvable open key. DISCHARGE: carry obligations through a cross-unit import (an obligation slot on the imported summary that the caller's rows carry) and into spawned workers (a frame handle passed to the worker), each with a test, or record the refusals as the intended boundary.

named_followups.title: A host's admission obligations are still carried at unit grain
named_followups.why: ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN attributes only admissions of a named declaration (rule 37's checked-specification settlement) to rows. An admission asked through arm_obligations::consult at a host position (rules 33 to 36's hosts, the route table's fallbacks, RULE32A-PILOT's caller-frame hold host) and a nested analysis's carriage handed to the enclosing frame are carried by every row of the unit, because which rows read that lowering is not attributed (a lowering computed inside one function's work may be reused by a whole-unit pass). No such host returns an obligation today, so no live row is affected. DISCHARGE: when a host package first returns an obligation, attribute it to the function scopes whose work asked (contract_dependencies' active stack) with a census showing the lowering is not reused outside that work, plus a test, or record unit grain as the intended precision for that host.

named_followups.title: The row-grain attribution's wall-time cost is unmeasured
named_followups.why: ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN notes every function's work and body in the unit frame's attribution in every run (contract_dependencies::within and body now open their scope whenever a frame is open, not only under the audit's recording) and computes a reach closure for units with an attributed admission. In its measurement the TIP corpus route (rev:051aef7f2) took 2 h 25 min and the BASE one (rev:3e53c34fe) 1 h 53 min, each measured once, in different measure runs, under different host load, so the difference is unattributed. Runs without a recording (unit tests, the certificate recheck) now open per-function consultation logs too. DISCHARGE: interleaved wall-time medians of BASE and TIP on the corpus route (or the analysis of the 54 carrying units alone), and an optimisation if the attribution costs measurably, or a record that it does not.

named_followups.title: W44 admissions at a call of an inferred lifetime summary leave only the outer classification's gate
named_followups.why: Registered by RETAINING-CALL-MINTED-NAME-ACTUALS. Rule 12t's route also classifies a call of an inferred lifetime summary (a same-unit helper or a replayed import, `ResourceContracts::lifetime_summary`) under its minted name (`retaining_environment`), and W44's probe reads that summary's contract for the call's positions, but the summary is not a retaining declaration, so rule 38b does not mint its entries: an actual the probe admitted leaves the gate in the outer classification and is refused again in the inner one unless an older route exempts it there. In MK-EVENT-CELL-CROSS-FUNCTION's area (the lifetime summaries). DISCHARGE: mint the entries of a lifetime-summary callee at its Borrowed positions under rule 38b's conditions, with fixtures and a declared measurement.

named_followups.title: A cell-bearing call over a protocol record's non-protocol member gives the record a fact
named_followups.why: Registered by CELL-PROTOCOL-FB-DECLARATIONS. Rule 38c's host (legacy_descriptor_cells.rs::apply, operand_protocols) gives a protocol record a reached fact (touched, guard unknown) at every cell-bearing call whose actual is rooted at it, including actuals that name no protocol member (`mk_event_timeout_destroy(sched->evl, &timer->event)` in flb_sched_destroy's timer loop; C2's `mk_event_channel_destroy(config->evl, config->ch_self_events...)` in flb_engine_shutdown). The later guard test is then not read, and a record that keeps its protocol is reported broken (`descriptor-cell-protocol-broken`, `-overwritten`, `-escapes`; tests/cell_protocol_fb_declarations.rs `withheld_protocols_reading`, ignored). That is why the census-kept protocols of flb_sched (`ch_events[0] != -1`, ch_events[0..1], event.fd #same) and flb_config (`notification_channels_initialized == 1`, notification_channels[0..1], notification_event.fd #same) are not declared; their text is in the report's section 3. DISCHARGE: a protocol record gains a fact at a cell-bearing call only through an actual naming one of its protocol members (with Lean parity), the two declarations, fixtures, and a declared measurement (expected: leaf trades at flb_sched_destroy :856 and flb_engine_shutdown :1718, no status move). AMENDED (CELL-PROTOCOL-PER-END-GUARDS, 2026-11-03, docs/reports/cell-protocol-per-end-guards/README.md): a per-end sentinel group (rule 38f) already gains a fact at a cell-bearing call only through a cell of its own the call spells; the record guard keeps the reading this entry describes. flb_config's per-end `> 0` text (ch_manager[0..1], ch_event.fd #same(ch_manager[0]), ch_notif[0..1]; the report's section 3) is withheld to be declared with its flag protocol under this entry's DISCHARGE (declared alone it would put the Safe row flb_engine_started on the declaration while reading nothing there). AMENDED (CELL-RESULT-SET-ALIGNMENT, 2026-11-04): the planned-fix declarations for the user's third patch (docs/reports/cell-result-set-alignment/planned-contracts/teardown_destroy_patch_v3.qv, held off every route) state flb_config's ends per end with `live_set([1, MAX]) absent_set(-1)` (ch_data, ch_manager, ch_event.fd #same, ch_notif); the production text stays withheld under this entry.

named_followups.title: Candidate defects: guards that read a Monkey creator's descriptor 0 as absent, and timer arms that ignore a failed registration
named_followups.why: Registered by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE (census part 4, docs/reports/cell-guard-result-range/census/census.json). Source readings only; nothing is filed upstream. A creator's descriptor result is >= 0 on success under the C library's result sets, so a later guard that reads descriptor 0 as absent misreads a success value; each is reachable only when descriptor 0 is free in the process (stdin closed at start; flb_utils_set_daemon closes only stdout and stderr). Not tracked elsewhere (046accf6 lines): flb_input_collector_destroy (flb_input.c:3145) `coll->fd_timer > 0`, the strongest, since the holder's own absent value is -1 (:2242, :3181): a COLLECT_TIME timer on descriptor 0 is never destroyed and the collector holding its registered event is freed while the loop still holds it; flb_engine_started and flb_engine_failed (flb_engine.c:1034, :1048) `config->ch_notif[1] <= 0` report a write end on 0 as no channel; flb_engine_start's shutdown timer (flb_engine.c:1497 `<= 0` creates it again, :1563 `> 0` never destroys it); flb_sp_window_destroy (flb_sp.c:670) `task->window.fd > 0`; Monkey (Fluent Bit's lib/monkey and the corpus's Monkey): mk_server_worker_loop never tests its timer at mk_server.c:502 and destroys it only under `timeout_fd > 0` (:585), mk_server_lib_notify_event_loop_break (:630) and mk_server_lib_notify_started (:648) read a write end on 0 as no channel, and the test program test/lib_server.c:160 overwrites `ret` (:167) before testing it. named_followups.title: cfl_sds_printf is declared as a slot move without its borrowed tail, and its result has no mode
named_followups.why: Registered by CFL-MPACK-EXTERNAL-DECLARATIONS. cfl_sds_printf(cfl_sds_t *sds, const char *fmt, ...) (lib/cfl/src/cfl_sds.c:391-452, identical at 66910c10, 046accf6 and 34155955) may move *sds through cfl_sds_increase. (1) The trailing arguments are read by vsnprintf only, which is resource_variadic_borrowed_tail(), but the loader refuses the tail beside a slot clause (a slot or retention clause stands only beside plain parameter and result predicates, C04.14/C04.15). (2) The result is *sds after the call, or NULL. No v1 result mode states the pointee of a slot (the derived modes need a depth-one base, C04.3.1), so the result is resource_return_none(). That is exact for the 10 covered calls, which discard it; the 16 calls that bind it all pass arguments. DISCHARGE: admit a variadic tail beside a slot move, and a result equal to the slot's pointee after the move (or NULL), in the loader, gateway rule 12x and QCore.SlotMove with Lean parity. Then re-declare and measure.

named_followups.title: cfl_variant_create_from_array/_kvlist hand the caller's container to the result exactly when it is non-NULL
named_followups.why: Registered by CFL-MPACK-EXTERNAL-DECLARATIONS. cfl_variant_create_from_array(value) and _kvlist(value) (lib/cfl/src/cfl_variant.c:354-390) claim value for a new variant: cfl_container_claim_* sets value->owner, and cfl_variant_destroy then destroys value. They return the variant, or NULL with value untouched when the allocation or claim fails. Custody of value therefore moves into the result exactly when the result is non-NULL. v1 has no disposition keyed on a pointer result's nullness (C04.13). resource_consumed would hide the failure arm's obligation, and resource_owned would deny the hand-off, so both stay undeclared. On the user's current run at 046accf6 they hold 1 pair each, in cmt_decode_opentelemetry.c. named_followups.title: mpack_writer_init_growable keeps the caller's char ** slot and delivers an owned buffer through it at mpack_writer_destroy, on success only
named_followups.why: Registered by CFL-MPACK-EXTERNAL-DECLARATIONS. mpack_writer_init_growable(writer, target_data, target_size) (mpack.c:1127-1151) sets *target_data = NULL, stores target_data and target_size in the writer's reserved space, and MPACK_MALLOCs the buffer. named_followups.title: realloc is undeclared: its size-0 arm frees on glibc while a NULL result reads as the old block kept

No admitted clause restricts a declaration to a nonzero argument (C04.5 is equality with one literal; C04.14.1 guards only a retention), so it is not declared (fail-closed). Options: (A, recommended) a nonzero-argument precondition such as `requires resource_argument(size, != 0);` read structurally at the call site, C23-aligned, with loader, gateway and Lean parity; (B) a declared policy placing size 0 outside it, attributed like the pipe [1, MAX] policy; (C) a cautious failure arm leaving the old block undecided on NULL; (D) keep undeclared. Every live profile's baseline records the same twelve contract bundles; a published row lists only declarations (declarations, held, withdrawn), not the missed lookups the gateway notes (qcore_schemas::contract_consultation::Consulted.missed), so an added declaration's reach is unrecorded, and the record is evidence-only with callback candidates (relied) that need not be spelled; the refutation table (phase two holds call sites in every unit), the cross-unit link homes (QCORE_CROSS_UNIT_LINK_MAP, set by every measure route) and the pin evaluation are run-wide; current-route .qo checkpoints refuse QCORE_NULL_PROPERTY and QCORE_OUTER_PROJECTION and name the analyzer build commit; the pinned corpus route (80-83 % of tip analysis time on LIBC-GAP and CFL-MPACK r2) has no unit seam (W45-CHECKPOINT-PINNED-REPLAY-ROUTE). Options: (A, recommended with D) the gateway publishes per unit every name looked up (found and missed), the relied candidates and a whole-map-read flag, a new baseline carries it, and the measure tool reuses a unit only when the revision diff is contract data alone, no changed declaration meets the unit's closure, the tip's refutation table, link-home evidence and pin template equal the baseline's (fixpoint over re-audited units, else full) and the unit fingerprint matches; needs the user's approval to use an evidence-only record as a reuse input, a Lean locality statement and a gateway card; saves about 30-35 of 150-165 analysis minutes (system and slice). (B) profile reuse when no analyzer path or bundle changed: sound, no saving for contract cards. (C) advisory reuse by spelled names, never for a landing: unsound as a claim. (D) pinned-route group checkpoints first, then A on the corpus: the large saving. DISCHARGE unchanged, after that decision. AMENDED (CORPUS-GROUP-CHECKPOINTS, docs/reports/corpus-group-checkpoints/README.md): option D is done (the user chose "D then A"): pinned-route group checkpoints reuse within one revision; across revisions the analyzer build and the stage's whole contract environment differ, so every group recomputes. named_followups.title: A variadic callee that invokes a callback cannot state its tail: the loader refuses a variadic tail beside a callback clause
named_followups.why: Registered by LOG-PRINT-BODY-CONTRACTS. The resource loader's retaining branch (contract_loader.rs) refuses `resource_variadic_borrowed_tail()` and `resource_variadic_data_tail()` beside any callback clause ("a retention clause stands only beside plain parameter and result predicates"). cmt_log_print and cio_log_print render their tail with vsnprintf into a local buffer and hand only that buffer to the context's log callback, so the truthful declaration has both clauses; the shipped ones state the five fixed parameters only, the refusing direction, and a call passing an actual after `fmt` keeps "arguments beyond the declared parameters of `cmt_log_print` are outside the resource projection". Size by source reading at 046accf6: 18 of 61 cmt_log_print sites and 38 chunkio log calls pass a tail actual. DISCHARGE: admit the tail clause beside member and synchronous invocations in the loader; apply rule 11w's per-site tail reading to such a declaration in route G (legacy_retained_by.rs), never dropping an excess actual; Lean parity (a borrowed tail composed with an identity callback invocation is the identity on the caller's state); controls and a measured re-pin of the two declarations.

named_followups.title: A callback member stored from a setter's void * formal stays open (chunkio's cio_set_log_callback), and its candidates have no contracts
named_followups.why: Registered by LOG-PRINT-BODY-CONTRACTS. Rule 12n opens a member stored from a formal that is not a function pointer. chunkio's `void cio_set_log_callback(struct cio_ctx *ctx, void (*log_cb))` (`lib/chunkio/src/chunkio.c:316-319`, identical at 046accf6, 66910c10 and 34155955) stores its `void *` formal into `cio_options.log_cb`, so the run's set is open and every call of cio_log_print under its declaration is refused (`callback-member-open`). (Before this card's repair the spelling `void (*)` was read as a function pointer and closed the member.) The setter's only call, cio_create's `cio_set_log_callback(ctx, options->log_cb)` (chunkio.c:148), passes the member itself; the other stores are `opts.log_cb = log_cb;` in src/flb_storage.c:709, src/flb_fstore.c:492 and lib/chunkio/tools/cio.c:598 (three static functions named `log_cb`) and a null. DISCHARGE: forward a non-function formal's values soundly (every actual at that position of every call, with the address-taken rule, never only function-pointer-typed ones), Lean parity, controls; resource-v1 contracts for the three static `log_cb` candidates read from their bodies (the two Fluent Bit ones only log `str` and return 0); measured after S3-PREPASS-UNREAD-GRAPH-ISOLATION closes the run's sets.

named_followups.title: 19 librdkafka header definitions stay undeclared behind a named vocabulary or body-check gap: 40 pairs on the current route
named_followups.why: Registered by LIBRDKAFKA-HEADER-INLINES (census of the user's `quirin-audit current` run at Fluent Bit 046accf6, docs/reports/librdkafka-header-inlines/census/). Each is a `static` header definition, identical at 046accf6, 66910c10 and 34155955, whose body the run publishes no summary for. Not declared on review: rd_file_mkstemp 2 (a stream result whose body leaks the mkstemp descriptor when fdopen fails), rd_kafka_q_io_event 1 (the queue event-callback invocation itself; its candidates need a C04.19 registry declaration), rd_tmpabuf_write0 1 and rd_tmpabuf_write_str0 2 (they forward rd_tmpabuf_alloc0's borrowed result, now declared, which W4 may infer under C04.3.4 rule 6; measure first).
