named_followups.title: A body that releases or stores into a member of a formal parent it keeps has no summary mode: a user choice
named_followups.why: Registered by MEMBER-ACCESS-PROJECTION (046accf6 current run, census in docs/reports/member-access-projection/census/). Of the 267 functions the indirect-access refusal alone blocks, 25 release a member or element of a formal parent and keep the parent (cmt_opts_exit, metric_release_storage, free_chunk_header, rd_kafka_metadata_partition_clear, the twelve *_destroy_array helpers), 50 store a pointer that may carry an identity into a member (map->unit = cfl_sds_create(unit), confval->name = name) and 5 hand an embedded list's address to a releasing helper (rd_list_destroy(&conf->...)); across the run 2,395 pointer-member-read and 1,814 pointer-store leaves. Rule 5k admits a member release only when the body also releases the parent (P4); otherwise the effect is on the caller's object and no summary mode states it. Options: (1, recommended) a member-effect summary: per formal, the members a body releases and the members it stores a custody-carrying value into, checked against the body like rule 5k's P1-P3 and rule 13a, applied at the call site to the caller's place map (a released member's later use refused or accused as 5k's caller guard does; a stored member a field link in CG11's owned-field model), with contract-spec grammar, loader, gateway and Lean parity; (2) class 8 read strictly: a borrowed parent's member is an interior borrow, its release and stores into it refused by name, no verdict moves; (3) keep rule 5k as it stands and re-attribute the rest to a named refusal like rule 12k, no verdict moves. Recommended: 1, with 3's re-attribution first. The card that takes it should first run docs/reports/member-access-projection/scripts/run_current_census.py (the indirect-census build's call-argument and parity streams), which names each refused actual's position and route answer; it should also size statements with two calls (strlen(a->p) + strlen(b->q) is refused while each call alone is admitted). DISCHARGE: a user decision and the card it names, measured. AMENDED (MEMBER-EFFECT-SUMMARY): the user chose option 1 on 2026-11-05 ("Option 1 (rec.)"). Option 3's re-attribution is gateway rule 38i; the member-release half of option 1 is gateway rule 38j (derived bodies only); the store half is MEMBER-EFFECT-STORES and the declared form MEMBER-EFFECT-DECLARED-FORM. Element releases (`A[i]` of a formal array) and the `run_current_census.py` census remain open here.

named_followups.title: The host excludes slot waits a subcommand plugin declares, bounded only by the slot-wait limit
named_followups.why: Registered by MEASURE-QUOTA-AND-INCREMENTAL. The subcommand host stops counting --timeout-ms while the plugin keeps quirin_audit_plugin::SLOT_WAIT_MARKER in its output; the host does not verify that the plugin's descendants wait for a gate slot. --slot-wait-limit-ms (default the quota) bounds it: a run never exceeds quota + limit. The quota is a resource bound and no verdict path reads the wait, but a plugin can spend the limit while working. gate_slot.py polls with non-blocking flock, so the kernel's waiter list does not show its waits. DISCHARGE: a wait the host verifies itself, or a recorded decision that the limit is the bound. AMENDED (GATE-SLOT-FIFO-ORDER): --slot-wait-limit-ms now defaults to the overall wall bound (--wall-limit-ms, seven days, never below the quota), not to the quota, so a run no longer 'never exceeds quota + limit': it never exceeds the overall wall bound, which stops it whatever it declares (plugin-wall-limit). The remaining gap is unchanged: a plugin can spend the excluded wait while working, up to the bound.

named_followups.title: The declared form of a member effect for bodiless callees: G05d member-path states or a new clause (a user choice)
named_followups.why: Registered by MEMBER-EFFECT-SUMMARY (report section 4). Rule 38j derives member-release effects from bodies only. Two vocabularies already state a callee's effect on a formal's members: grammar G05d `quant live #P: TAG.PATH |-> #released|#moved|#stale|#kept;` (contract spec C04.19.6, rule 30), whose direct call affects only an object the caller linked at the path (an untracked member stays, P-B08-SHALLOW) and which is in force today (teardown_destroy.qv, the librdkafka callback candidates, #stale included); and the descriptor-cell lower form `resource_member_released(P, T.F, stale)` (rule 38), which owns that clause name. Options: (1, recommended) G05d is the declared form: a member-path declaration with no hand-off whose states are #stale or #released also enters the member-effect table, and its direct call is read through rule 38j's caller check where the actual is a formal's object, after re-measuring existing declarations (a direct call rule 30 read as `stays` may refuse); (2) a new resource clause with a new grammar id loaded only into the member-effect table, rule 30 unchanged (two vocabularies, two readings); (3) no declared form. DISCHARGE: a user decision and the card it names, with spec, grammar, loader, gateway, Lean parity and a measured arbiter.

named_followups.title: The store half of the member-effect summary: a body that stores a custody-carrying value into a member of a formal it keeps
named_followups.why: Registered by MEMBER-EFFECT-SUMMARY (report section 3). Statements `P->F = V` with `V` a pointer name or a custody-returning call into a member of an unrebound formal are named `member-store-through-formal` by rule 38i (about 160 leaves, 119 functions, 11 whose every access leaf it names on the 046accf6 current run, census estimate) and stay refused. Design carried forward: the body check reads the store like rule 13a's slot move (the place used only at that position; a formal value never used after), the effect states that `P->F` takes the value (a formal's custody, Stored-like, or a fresh call result), the summary is withheld from the W4 table as rule 38j's is, and at the call site a tracked parent gains a field link in CG11's owned-field model while an untracked member's old value must be established custody-free (fail closed otherwise); a formal parent cascades. Overlaps W44-CALL-RESULT-INDIRECT-DESTINATION (formal-parent half), W45-SUB-OBJECT-STORE-OWNED-VALUE and W43-INDIRECT-POINTER-VALUE-STORE. DISCHARGE: that card, with Lean parity and a measured arbiter.

named_followups.title: A lookup tie that the path fixed non-null could prove the candidate infeasible: a decision held from rule 39
named_followups.why: Registered by NULL-WITNESS-GUARD-CORRELATION. Rule 39 reads a lookup's place-read body (`return TAILQ_FIRST(&q->rkmq_msgs);`) only to name or refuse its miss; where the path's own test fixed the tied place non-null (rd_kafka_msgq_allow_wakeup_at, rdkafka_msg.c:1819 -> :1826) the miss is excluded on that path, yet the path ends unresolved, so the candidate stays Unknown instead of being removed by rule 15t's infeasibility proof. named_followups.title: Lookup misses the bodies exclude through data-structure invariants the search does not read
named_followups.why: Registered by NULL-WITNESS-GUARD-CORRELATION. Rule 39 refuses, as correlated, five corpus witnesses whose NULL event the bodies exclude only through an invariant: (1) the rd_tmpabuf arena discipline (rd_kafka_metadata_cache_entry_new, rd_kafka_topic_info_new_with_rack, rd_kafka_handle_Produce_metadata_update): `rd_tmpabuf_alloc0` returns NULL only when `tab->failed` (no tmpabuf body sets it non-zero) or `of + size > size`, where `assert_on_fail` asserts first; the callers size the arena with rd_tmpabuf_add_alloc over string lengths and loops, and the exclusion holds only while `NDEBUG` is undefined (the corpus compile database does not define it); (2) the message queue's count/list invariant (`rkmq_msg_cnt > 0` iff `tqh_first != NULL`) that rd_kafka_ProduceRequest's length read (`rd_dassert(cnt > 0)`) and its callee rd_kafka_msgset_create_ProduceRequest rely on. Both stay Unknown (candidate). DISCHARGE: checked invariant contracts (or body-derived arithmetic) for each, with the build-configuration dependence stated, fixtures, Lean parity and a measurement; never a caller test as evidence.

named_followups.title: A null row resting on a declared allocation or lookup result does not list the declaration
named_followups.why: Registered by NULL-WITNESS-GUARD-CORRELATION. The null walk (`null_deref/walk.rs`) and the path search (`witness.rs`) read a callee's resource contract through `contract_dependencies::unrecorded` when they classify its result as an allocation or lookup source; so the six rows LIBRDKAFKA-HEADER-INLINES made provisional Unsafe listed the same contract dependencies at both sides, and no row's `contract_dependencies` names the declaration its strong source or finding rests on. named_followups.title: Review the slot deadline and drain defaults against the receipts
named_followups.why: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. The defaults (audit stall 2 h, rust-suite drain 2 h, back-off 5 min, stop grace 60 s) were chosen from one measured pinned-corpus route (1 h 56 min with steady I/O) and the 2026-11-06 incident (10 h 18 min with zero I/O), not from a census. Before the card a drain admitted nothing until it finished; now each back-off lets queued audits start, so behind back-to-back long audits a rust-suite job can wait longer than the longest single audit. The receipts now record `limits`, `monitor` (samples, last progress, peak tree RSS, breach) and `slot_record.drain.attempts`. DISCHARGE: a review of a period of receipts (stalls, drains given up, rust-suite waits) with the defaults kept or changed by a recorded decision.

named_followups.title: A declared measurement cannot override its routes' slot deadlines
named_followups.why: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. The measure plugin clears each route's environment and passes only QUIRIN_GATE_DIR, QUIRIN_GATE_LEGACY_LOCK and QUIRIN_GATE_MEMINFO (crates/quirin-audit-plugin-measure/src/sides.rs GATE_VARIABLES), and runs `gate_slot.py audit` with fixed flags, so every route runs under the audit defaults (2 h stall, no wall-clock deadline) and a measurement whose route legitimately goes quiet longer has no override. DISCHARGE: the plugin forwards QUIRIN_GATE_STALL_TIMEOUT and QUIRIN_GATE_DEADLINE (or takes a flag) to gate_slot.py, records them in the route's run record, with a test.

named_followups.title: gate_slot.py status does not list waiters that hold no gate lock
named_followups.why: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. `gate_slot.py status` lists processes with a /proc/locks entry on a gate file: audit waiters show because they hold the legacy lock shared while they poll, and untimed legacy waiters are queued in the kernel. A job in a timed wait for the legacy lock (--wait-timeout while a `flock` legacy job holds it exclusive) holds nothing, and a nested job runs inside its parent's slot without a lock, so neither is listed. DISCHARGE: each slot job holds a lock on a per-job file under the gate directory from its first wait to its exit (or an equivalent the status reads), listed by status, with a test. AMENDED (GATE-SLOT-FIFO-ORDER): a waiter now holds a locked ticket file (<gate dir>/<family>/queue/) from the moment it holds the legacy lock until it is admitted or gives up, and status lists it with its queue position, also while a rust-suite drain backs off and holds no gate lock. Still unlisted: a job in a timed wait for the legacy lock (it has no ticket yet) and a nested job, and the ticket is dropped at admission, not at exit.

named_followups.title: Slot stall, resident-set and status readings need /proc
named_followups.why: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. The stall timeout, the resident-set report, `gate_slot.py status` and the drain's blocker CPU/I/O read /proc (/proc/<pid>/stat, io, cmdline, /proc/locks). Without it (macOS) the script says so and only the wall-clock deadline applies; status exits 1. Separately, the receipt's existing `max_rss_kib` reads wait4's ru_maxrss as KiB, which macOS reports in bytes. DISCHARGE: macOS readings (process tree, I/O and resident set through the platform's APIs, ru_maxrss scaled) with tests on that platform, or a recorded decision that the gate slots are Linux-only.

named_followups.title: R8 option A: reuse units across revisions behind the published per-unit lookup record
named_followups.why: Registered by CORPUS-GROUP-CHECKPOINTS (docs/reports/corpus-group-checkpoints/README.md section 6; USER DECISION 2026-11-06, verbatim: "D then A (rec.)", the button being "R8: option D first (per-group checkpoints for the pinned corpus route), then option A (gateway publishes per-unit lookups including missed ones; reuse only for contract-only diffs with matching cross-unit facts). I approve using that lookup record as a reuse input once it is published and checked."). The gateway publishes per unit every name looked up (found and missed), the relied callback candidates and a whole-map-read flag; then the pinned group identity's stage.environment_sha256 (today the whole contract environment) becomes the digest of the environment restricted to the group's units' closures (with include/inherit resolution), plus the refutation entries and homes meeting it, and the analyzer build is accepted from the base side only for a diff confined to contract data (providers/*/contracts/**, their locks, contract/**), recorded in the reuse decision; everything else in the identity stays. DISCHARGE: a contract-only card's measurement reuses unaffected groups (and units on the configured routes), with the composed comparison shown equal to a full run on sampled landings, fail-closed on any unverifiable input.

named_followups.title: Rule 5h reads __builtin_expect(E, K) as E on a stated premise that E's truthiness survives its conversion to long
named_followups.why: Registered by BUILTIN-EXPECT-NULL-TEST. The builtin's parameters are `long`: its value is `(long)E`, which has E's truthiness when E is a null or comparison test (int 0/1), or an integer no wider than `long` (LP64, the runs' targets); Clang rejects a pointer operand, but accepts a floating or `__int128` operand silently, where `(long)0.5` is 0 while `if (0.5)` is true. The token-level reading does not check the operand's type, so the premise is stated in rule 5h, not checked. DISCHARGE: read the operand's implicit conversion from the Clang AST (an integral cast from a type no wider than `long`, or a Boolean-valued operand) and refuse any other, with a fixture for a floating and a wider operand, Lean parity and a measurement (expected: no move; the census found no such operand).

named_followups.title: Read `*(&X)` as the named object X in the typed reader
named_followups.why: SCALAR-STATEMENT-FORMS' census of the user's current run (fluent-bit 046accf6): 96 `unrecognized assignment destination` readings are `*(&TopicsCnt) = (int32_t)_uva - 1`, the store rd_kafka_buf_read_arraycnt's expansion makes through the address of a scalar local. C11 6.5.3.2p3: `*&E` is `E`. The typed reader's path walk refuses a `&` step, so rule 41 refuses the destination (unread-destination). DISCHARGE: the reader reads `*(&X)` (parentheses and qualifier conversions only) as the place X with X's own class, never as a dereference of a pointer value; Lean parity; a measured re-pin. The same expansions also declare `T *_vp = &X;` (899 readings, refused as a pointer destination), so a function moves only with SCALAR-FORMS-LOCAL-ADDRESS-POINTER.

named_followups.title: A pointer local initialised from the address of a scalar automatic local
named_followups.why: SCALAR-STATEMENT-FORMS' census: the largest residue of `unsupported assignment expression` is the pointer declaration `uint64_t *_vp = &_uva;` (899 readings in the rd_kafka_buf_read_* macro expansions of rdkafka_mock_handlers.c, rdkafka_admin.c, rdkafka_request.c, rdkafka_fetcher.c and others), whose pointer only ever designates an automatic scalar of the same frame and is read through once (`*_vp = _v`). Rule 41 refuses every pointer destination by design. DISCHARGE: a named rule that binds such a local to a frame-local scalar place (no identity, no custody, never escaping the frame: no store into memory, no call actual, no return), with the reads and stores through it lowered to the place's own; refusal of every other use; Lean parity; a measured re-pin with the per-function moves of the macro-expanding functions.

named_followups.title: A comma of scalar steps in a `for` clause
named_followups.why: SCALAR-STATEMENT-FORMS: `for (j = i - 1; j > 0; j--, c++)` (mk_lib.c chunk_header, a function blocked only by this leaf) is one clause with two scalar writes; a `for` clause lowers to one CFG node (`Statement::For`'s `increment` holds one instruction), so rule 41 answers only a one-instruction reading and refuses the comma (unread-destination). DISCHARGE: a clause lowered as a sequence of nodes (the W45 list step's second increment node is a precedent), each comma operand read by rule 41 in order (C11 6.5.17p2 sequences them), with a fixture and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: `a - -2000` is read as a decrement by the lexical gate
named_followups.why: SCALAR-STATEMENT-FORMS' census: rd_kafka_offset2str (blocked only by this leaf) refuses `snprintf(ret[i], sizeof(ret[i]), "TAIL(%lld)", llabs(offset - -2000))` with `unmodeled increment or decrement expression`: the tokenizer emits one-character punctuation, so `- -` (binary minus, unary minus) and `--` are the same token pair and classify_simple_base's `has_increment` window fires. The refusal is fail-closed (no admission), but it names the wrong cause and hides the statement from every route that reads increments. DISCHARGE: the tokenizer keeps the adjacency of `--`/`++` (or the gate reads Clang's node), with a fixture of `x - -1` and of `x--`, and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: A scalar step nested in a store or a call actual
named_followups.why: SCALAR-STATEMENT-FORMS' census: 63 `unmodeled increment or decrement expression` readings are a scalar index stepped inside another statement (`result[index++] = keyvalue`, `seen[seen_count++] = callback_entry`, `append_sample_to_metric(..., sample_index++)`); most store a pointer into an element, which is CG11's/the indexed collection's, and the call actuals are rule 10u's. Rule 41 reads only a statement whose top-level node is the step. DISCHARGE: the elaborator's piece lowering (rule 10s) reads the step as a sequenced piece where the enclosing store or call is admitted by its own rule, with fixtures and a measured re-pin; no new admission of the pointer store itself.

named_followups.title: A `volatile` automatic scalar written and read with no value fact
named_followups.why: SCALAR-STATEMENT-FORMS refuses `double volatile val = 1.0;` (cmt_metric_dec, blocked only by this leaf) by name: rule 11h keeps no value-derived fact about a volatile object and orders its accesses as trace events, and no route here lowers a volatile write. A `ForgetScalar` of an automatic volatile scalar with no address taken would keep no fact either, but whether a volatile access may be lowered as an ordinary scalar write at all is rule 11h's decision, not this card's. DISCHARGE: a decision under rule 11h (user or rule owner) and, if admitted, the lowering with a fixture that a branch on the volatile refines nothing, Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: The fluent-bit per-library provider table scopes only the standalone monkey-libevent configuration
named_followups.why: Found by CURRENT-MONKEY-LINKED-CONFIGURATION: contract/profiles/fluent-bit/library-providers.json maps `monkey-libevent` to quirin-provider-libc + qcore-provider-libevent and lists it as a dependent library of fluent_bit. DISCHARGE: a reviewed `monkey` scope (the linked configuration's providers: libc for epoll/timerfd/pipe, the Monkey contracts, and no OpenSSL contracts until an OpenSSL provider exists) and fluent_bit's dependent list updated, or a recorded decision that linked runs never use per-library scoping.

named_followups.title: Rule 40's call-type check compares records reached through a member pointer by tag only
named_followups.why: Rule 40 (LINK-STANDING) compares a cross-unit callee's canonical signature and, for each tagged record the signature names, Clang's canonical layout where both units complete it. A record reached only through a member pointer of such a record is compared by tag alone, and enumeration constants are not compared, so two units whose same-tag definitions differ one pointer level down would still agree (an incompatible-type call the C standard leaves undefined). DISCHARGE: a transitive layout comparison over every record reachable from the signature, or a DWARF cross-check of the home object's subprogram type against the caller's, with the measured refusals.

named_followups.why: Registered by GATE-SLOT-SHORT-JOB-LANE. The user's decision named queued audits and drains, not a running suite, so the fail-closed side was chosen. DISCHARGE: a recorded decision either to keep it or to let the lane run beside a suite (and to mark the load-sensitive rows' receipts when it overlapped).

named_followups.title: A lane job stopped at its wall bound can leave a half-written tree
named_followups.why: Registered by GATE-SLOT-SHORT-JOB-LANE. A stopped lane command exits 124 and the receipt says lane.complete false, but the gate cannot know what the command had written. The rule asks commands to write their completion record last; whether `prepare` (and each other lane command) does so was not audited by this card. DISCHARGE: an audit of the commands sent to the lane showing each leaves no tree that reads as complete after a SIGTERM/SIGKILL, or a fix.
